title: schema: render_error prints a D-Bus method name as a systemctl verb
description:
lib/schema/schema.ml:483:

    | Unit_op_failed { op; unit_; reply; error_name = _ } ->
        Printf.sprintf "systemctl %s %s failed: %s" op unit_ reply

The template says the user could have typed `systemctl <op> <unit>`. The op values the Dbus adapter actually raises are Manager method names and wire-decode step labels (lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:558-560, 583, 622, 659, 670-693, 752-766):

  StartUnit, StopUnit, RestartUnit, Reload, Subscribe, ResetFailedUnit,
  GetUnit, GetUnit/read, Properties.Get, Properties.Get(Job),
  ActiveState/enter_container, ActiveState/read, Job/enter_variant,
  Job/enter_struct, Job/read_u, Job/read_o, sd_bus_add_match

So a real failure renders as "systemctl Job/enter_struct pctl-x.service failed: …" or "systemctl sd_bus_add_match - failed: …". Probe adds its own non-bus op ("wait", lib/probe/probe.ml:148), which the same template turns into "systemctl wait".

Pre-existing — the Dbus adapter has always raised method names. It was masked because the fakes and the unit tests fabricated lowercase verbs ("stop"); pctl-fl6 removed that divergence from In_mem, so the real wording is now what a test would show.

Fix: either drop the `systemctl` prefix ("StopUnit on pctl-x.slice failed: …") or give Unit_op_failed a rendering that names the D-Bus call rather than a CLI that was never run.

Filed from the review of e778a30.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Two things this ticket does not currently name, found in round 2 of the 761669c/f7ff155 review.

1. Three ops pass a PLACEHOLDER unit, and those render worse than the StopUnit case this ticket is about:

    lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:576   bus_error     ~op:"Reload"           ~unit:"-"
    lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:615   check_rc      ~op:"Subscribe"        ~unit:"-"
    lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:868   fail_on_neg_rc ~op:"sd_bus_add_match" ~unit:"-"

render_error turns these into "systemctl Reload - failed: …", "systemctl Subscribe - failed: …", "systemctl sd_bus_add_match - failed: …". "StopUnit pctl-x.slice" is a wrong verb on a real unit; these read as systemctl having operated on a unit literally named `-`, which is a worse kind of wrong — it invites the reader to go looking for that unit.

Severity ordering for whatever fix lands: placeholder-unit ops > the PascalCase method names this ticket names (StartUnit/StopUnit/RestartUnit/ResetFailedUnit/GetUnit) > the decode-step labels (Job/enter_variant, Job/read_u, ActiveState/parse, Properties.Get(Job)), which contain / and () and so at least read as internal.

2. test/unit/test_gc.ml:313-316 now PINS the bad wording as correct:

    Alcotest.(check string)
      "renders the systemctl failure"
      ("systemctl StopUnit pctl-x.slice failed: " ^ stop_failure_reply)
      (Gc.describe_exn e);

761669c changed the expected string from "systemctl stop …" to "systemctl StopUnit …" to follow In_mem's corrected op label. The assertion exists to prove the payload survives describe_exn (the comment above it says so), but as written it also certifies the verb. Whoever fixes this ticket must update that string, and until then a green test asserts the defect is intended.

No exit-code coupling: Schema.error_exit_code dispatches on the constructor, not the op string, so every Unit_op_failed maps to 5 regardless. test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:120 collects render_error output into an Alcotest failure message only — no substring assertion, so test_gc.ml:315 is the single pin.

title: cli/pipeline: module comment lists apply_plan as a Make(P) helper; it lives in Lifecycle
description:
lib/cli/pipeline.ml:12 says:

    - Make(P): the port-dependent commands — up, reload, down,
      restart, results — plus internal helpers that hold a
      Systemctl.t (with_handle, apply_plan, opportunistic_sweep, purge).

There is no apply_plan in lib/cli/pipeline.ml. grep -rn 'apply_plan' lib/ returns only lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:127 (the definition) and its two call sites in the same file. Make(P) does hold with_handle, opportunistic_sweep and purge, so only the one name is wrong.

Pre-existing; surfaced by the pctl-e0d review because the reload-economy work reads this comment when tracing where reloads are issued from, and the wrong name sends the reader to the wrong module.

Fix: drop apply_plan from the list.

title: systemctl/dbus: three sites drop bus failures without narrowing, unlike the sibling sites the repo already narrowed
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing the pctl-jbd retry diff. Grouped because the fix and the precedent are the same for all three; split if they turn out to want different answers.

The precedent: pctl-8sd added Schema.is_no_such_unit and pctl-2m8 applied it in gc, on the principle that a best-effort site should name what it tolerates rather than catching everything. These three did not get that treatment.

1. lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:596-603 manager_unsubscribe_best_effort — binds `let _rc = ...` and returns unit. The header comment ('systemd may have dropped the connection during shutdown') justifies tolerating a disconnect; the code tolerates every rc including EINVAL and AccessDenied. Weakest of the three: it only runs from close (dbus.ml:426), where there is nothing left to do about a failure. Arguably fine as-is with a comment saying 'every rc, deliberately'.

2. lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:608-617 reset_failed_unit — same `let _rc = ...` shape. Its comment says 'Swallows not-loaded/not-failed errors: callers use this best-effort, same as systemctl --user reset-failed with a glob that matches nothing'. That is a claim about two specific replies, and the code makes no attempt to check which reply came back. A transport failure leaves the `failed` tombstone in place and the caller believes it was cleared. Fix: check rc, tolerate the not-loaded/not-failed names by equality, propagate the rest.

3. lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:802 — `try entry.cb s with _ -> ()` inside the sd_bus_add_match handler, with no comment at all. Silently drops any exception from a subscriber callback, so a bug in a probe callback disappears. There is a real constraint here — an exception must not escape into the C dispatch frame — but 'must not escape' is satisfied by catching and REPORTING, not by catching and discarding. Fix: keep the catch, eprintf the exception with the subscriber's unit name, and say in a comment why it cannot be re-raised.

Related but tracked separately: pctl-a7p (unit_state answering Inactive on any Pctl_error) is the same family but worse, because it substitutes a wrong value rather than dropping an error.
close_reason: reset_failed_unit now checks rc and tolerates only NoSuchUnit — verified on systemd 260.1 that an unloaded unit answers that name and a loaded-but-not-failed one succeeds, so the old comment's 'not-failed error' does not exist. manager_unsubscribe_best_effort keeps every rc with a comment saying so and why (close is unwinding). The add_match handler reports a raising subscriber to stderr instead of discarding it; In_mem's notify does the same so the fake does not diverge.

title: gc: empty boot_id classifies every project as Orphan, so 'pctl gc --yes' purges all of them
description:
Pre-existing (not introduced by the dead-code-cleanup diff, which only renamed the reader).

lib/gc/gc.ml:97,118,139 read the boot id via Clock.Real.read_boot_id, which degrades to "" on any read failure (lib/clock/clock.ml:44).

lib/gc/gc.ml:32-37:
    match row.session_id with
    | Some s when s = boot_id && s <> "" -> Schema.Live
    | _ -> Schema.Orphan

With boot_id = "" the guard can never hold: s = boot_id forces s = "", which the s <> "" clause then rejects. Every row with an existing path becomes Orphan. Gc.purge (gc.ml:117-133) removes every Orphan, so 'pctl gc --yes' deletes the whole registry — units stopped, unit files removed, rows dropped — whenever /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id is unreadable.

Before the diff this was Gc.current_boot_id = try State.Session.read_boot_id () with _ -> "" — same degrade, same hazard.

Fix: route all three gc sites through Clock.read_boot_id_exn, which propagates instead. Gc.opportunistic_sweep already wraps its body in a warn-and-proceed try, so a raise there degrades to a skipped sweep rather than an aborted command; purge and report should fail loudly.

Note the comment added at lib/clock/clock.ml:11-16 asserts the opposite — that State.Session.reset is the *single* caller that must not get "".
close_reason: Completed: commit:c7fb526033426ca04d980417e2d4b0d2419668d8

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Fixed in the working tree (uncommitted; awaiting commit sha to close).

lib/gc/gc.ml:97,118,139 now read via Clock.read_boot_id_exn instead of the degrading Clock.Real.read_boot_id, so an unreadable boot id refuses to classify rather than reclassifying every project as Orphan.

lib/clock/clock.ml: read_boot_id_exn additionally raises Sys_error (path ^ ": empty boot id") when the trimmed read is empty — the reviewer's second finding. A zero-byte or whitespace-only read previously returned the exact "" the function existed to prevent, so routing gc through it would not have sufficed alone.

The false 'single caller' comment is replaced by the real hazard list (Session.reset AND Gc.class_of_row).

Blast radius: opportunistic_sweep already wraps its body in warn-and-proceed, so it degrades to a skipped sweep; purge and report now fail loudly instead of deleting rows. Clock.Real.read_boot_id survives with exactly one caller — Pipeline.with_project's metadata stamp, where "" legitimately means NULL session_id.

Regression cover: test/unit/test_clock.ml (new) pins all four leak paths — trims a good read, raises on blank/zero-byte/missing.

Gates: dune test exit 0 (incl. 4 new cases); dune build @e2e --force exit 0, all 22 scenarios OK against a live user session; nix build .#pctl exit 0.

title: prose: the sd_bus_error_set_errno mechanism is stated in five places and asserted in one
description:
pctl-srj deleted the two surviving copies of the REFUTED claim ('transport failure leaves sd_bus_error empty'). The corrected claim then spread. One fact — every fail: path in sd_bus_call/sd_bus_call_methodv runs sd_bus_error_set_errno, so a transport failure arrives named, e.g. System.Error.ENOTCONN — now appears as prose at:

  lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:32
  lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml:56-58
  lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:109
  lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:343-344
  lib/schema/schema.ml:98

and is asserted at test/unit/test_bus_errors.ml:74-76 (`check false (Some "System.Error.ENOTCONN")`).

dbus.ml:343-344 even ends with '— see [Bus_errors]' and then restates the mechanism it is pointing at.

Per CLAUDE.md's Prose rules the why exists exactly once, and a fact a test can check belongs to the test. Fix: keep the full account in one place (Bus_errors, next to the names it justifies), point the other four at it in a clause, and let test_bus_errors.ml own the value.

Filed from the review of e778a30.
close_reason: One full account left, in Bus_errors next to the names it justifies. dbus.ml's Sd_bus_error.parts, format_bus_reply and schema.ml's field doc are now one-clause pointers at it; bus_retry keeps only its distinct claim (ETIMEDOUT arrives as DBus.Error.Timeout, which is why Timeout is not in the peer-gone list) and points at Bus_errors for the naming path. test_bus_errors still owns the asserted value.

title: gc: opportunistic_sweep's best-effort daemon_reload now inherits a 5s retry budget it then discards
description:
Raised in the review of pctl-jbd and deliberately left for a separate call.

lib/gc/gc.ml:117 and :128 both do:

    ignore_best_effort (fun () -> M.daemon_reload handle)

ignore_best_effort (gc.ml:71-73) catches Schema.Pctl_error and returns unit. Since pctl-jbd, Dbus.daemon_reload retries a peer-gone reply for up to Bus_retry.peer_gone_budget (5 s) before raising. So during a window where the user manager is off the bus, each of those two call sites can now block for 5 s and then throw the result away — per project, inside purge's per-row loop. opportunistic_sweep runs at the top of every mutating command (up/reload/down/restart), so a 'pctl up' issued while a nixos-rebuild is reexecing the manager can sit for 10 s in the sweep before it does any work.

Mitigated but not solved by the same change: the raised error now carries '(gave up after N attempts over X.Xs)', so the exhausted case is at least distinguishable — in a message gc discards. The user still sees nothing.

Worth noting the bound is only reached when the manager does NOT come back, in which case the command's real work fails immediately afterwards anyway. Measured recovery on this host was ~1 s, so the common case costs ~1 s and succeeds. That is the argument for leaving it.

Three options, none obviously right:
  1. Leave it. Sweep reloads are cheap when the manager is healthy and the 5 s worst case coincides with a session that is broken anyway.
  2. Give the best-effort call sites a zero budget, so gc keeps its old fail-fast behaviour and only the load-bearing reloads in Lifecycle retry. Needs a way to pass a budget through the Systemctl port, which today has 'daemon_reload : t -> unit' and no options.
  3. Have ignore_best_effort log what it swallowed instead of dropping it, so a 10 s stall is at least explained. Cheapest, and independently defensible.

Related: pctl-e0d (four reloads per command).

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Count correction after pctl-e0d: gc's remove_project now issues ONE best-effort daemon_reload (after the deletions), not two. This ticket's finding is unchanged in kind — that one reload still inherits Bus_retry.peer_gone_budget (5s) and still discards the outcome via ignore_best_effort — but the worst case it can stall is now 5s per swept row, not 10s.

title: test_bus_errors: no_such_unit's wire spelling is asserted nowhere — a typo in the constant fails no test
description:
Mutation-confirmed at f7ff155: changing

    lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml:33
      let no_such_unit = "org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit"

to "...NoSuchUnitTYPO" leaves `dune test --force` GREEN.

Cause: test/unit/test_bus_errors.ml:29,34 feed the constant into the predicate that compares against the same constant —

    check true (err ~error_name:Bus_errors.no_such_unit
                    ~reply:"org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit: Unit x.service not loaded." ());

so the assertion holds for any value. :37's negative case uses a literal ("...NoSuchUnitXxx") but only proves inequality, which a typo'd constant also satisfies. The reply strings beside them are literals but nothing classifies on reply — that is the entire point of pctl-nir.

is_peer_gone does not have this hole: its three names are pinned as literals, so a typo there IS caught.

This matters more than a normal fixture gap because the whole e778a30/761669c/f7ff155 arc rests on 'Bus_errors owns the vocabulary and matches by equality'. The owned value is the one thing not checked, and it is a wire constant — the class of value where a silent typo turns a tolerated reply into a propagated one, changing pctl down from exit 0 to exit 5 on a unit systemd already GCed.

Also: pctl-jbi's close reason says 'test_bus_errors keeps its literals deliberately — it is the recording of the vocabulary, so referencing the constants there would be tautological.' The file does not match that description — :29 and :34 reference Bus_errors.no_such_unit, which is exactly the tautology the reason says was avoided. So the policy lives only in beads and the file does the opposite.

Fix: one positive case per name against a hardcoded literal —
    check true (err ~error_name:"org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit" ())
and put the deliberate-literal rule in the file header, where the next reuse sweep will see it.

Filed from round 2 of the review of 761669c/f7ff155.
close_reason: The name is a literal in test_bus_errors.ml with an explicit check string against Bus_errors.no_such_unit, and the rule is stated in the file header: every wire name is written out here, never taken from Bus_errors, because this file is the recording. Typo the constant → RED, confirmed.

title: lifecycle: after a reboot, pctl up starts nothing — the durable manifest matches the re-rendered units, so every row is Unchanged
description:
Derived by reading code, not executed — no repro run. Every step below cites the line that settles it.

Scenario: `pctl up`, then reboot without `pctl down`.

1. The manifest survives the reboot. `Session.reset`'s `reset_query` (lib/state/session.ml:15-22) NULLs only `projects` columns (host, started_at, spec_file, session_id). The `manifest` table is untouched; its only other writers are `Gc.remove_project` and `Lifecycle.reload` itself.

2. The unit files do NOT survive. `Unit_store.Fs` roots at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/user.control` (lib/unit_store/fs.ml:30), which is tmpfs. After the reboot there are no unit files and no running services.

3. `up` is `reload ~spec:(Some spec)` (lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:181-182). It compares the persisted manifest against a freshly rendered one — `manifest_before = Projects.load_manifest`, `manifest_after = WA.run` (lifecycle.ml:129-136). `diff_manifest` (lib/state/projects.ml:177-199) compares stored hash to rendered hash and never consults the filesystem.

4. The rendered bytes are identical to last boot. Unit content is a pure function of (spec, project id, host, project path) — `Write_all.run` (lifecycle.ml:66-85), `service_dropin_body` (lifecycle.ml:55-59). No timestamp, no boot id. The host is re-allocated to the same value: `Host_alloc.allocate` is `(md5_first_byte id_s mod 253) + 2` (lib/identity/identity.ml:58) and `taken` is empty because session reset NULLed every host.

5. So every plan row is `Unchanged`, and `apply_row` (lifecycle.ml:111) matches `Unchanged -> ()`. `apply_plan` issues two `daemon_reload`s and starts nothing.

Result: `pctl up` writes the unit files, prints "project <id> up · N units · host=127.0.0.N", exits 0, and zero services are running. Recovery requires `pctl down` (which empties the manifest via `reload ~spec:None`) and then `up`.

Not covered by tests: test/e2e/harness.ml gives each test a fresh XDG_STATE_HOME, so no test ever sees a durable manifest with an empty user.control. test/integration/test_state.ml:137,158 exercise `reset_with_boot_id` at the state layer only.

Same failure without a reboot: delete a project's files from user.control by hand, then `pctl up`.

Candidate fixes (not decided): have the session reset delete the manifest rows of every project whose session it clears — the units it names provably no longer exist — or have `up`/`reload` treat a manifest entry with no file on disk as `Added`. The first keeps the filesystem out of the diff; the second makes the diff honest about disk state.

Found while reviewing pctl-oik (UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md rewrite). It also falsifies the glossary line "Session id … Equal to the current boot id ⇒ the project was started on this boot": the stamp happens in Pipeline.with_project (lib/cli/pipeline.ml:184-192) before Lifecycle runs, so this path marks the row Live while starting nothing.
design:
Decided by grill 2026-08-03. Fix = D1: the diff's left side comes from disk, not from SQLite.

## Reference check (read locally, not recalled)
home-manager a184bd2 (2026-03-30), sd-switch bc44b75, nixpkgs 6242698 (2026-06-12).

- Both take the "before" side from FILES, never a DB. sd-switch loads $oldGenPath/home-files/.config/systemd/user (systemd.nix:534) and byte-compares (lib.rs:128-137); switch-to-configuration parses old_unit_dir.join(unit) (main.rs:1170,1285).
- Both put cross-invocation bookkeeping on tmpfs. s-t-c's resume lists are /run/nixos/{start,restart,reload}-list (main.rs:68-70), and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nixos for user scope (main.rs:175-188).
- Neither owns the start decision. Both drive the plan loop from live systemd state (lib.rs:111-115; main.rs:1157,1229) and let WantedBy= plus active-target restarts start new units (lib.rs:133-136; main.rs:1239-1266).

pctl deliberately took the other side of that trade: fs.ml:5-7 picks user.control precisely because it disappears across reboots. So pctl owns the start decision, and must not keep the ledger in a longer-lived store than the thing it describes.

## Shape
- `manifest` keeps its name and its table; migration 004 rebuilds it without `sha256` (rebuild rather than ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN, so it does not depend on the linked SQLite version). It now records ONLY ownership: which unit filenames this project may delete. load_manifest/replace_manifest change to Unit_filename.t list, which is a compile error at each of the 34 call sites across 10 files — the intended loud break.
- The unit->hash map becomes its own type, and the pure diff moves out of state/projects.ml:171-202 into lib/plan/ as `Plan.diff ~installed ~rendered`. test/unit/test_manifest.ml follows it. "rendered", not "desired": pctl stays a differ, so the right side names its provenance (lib/render/) rather than asserting a claim about reality.
- `installed` = for each OWNED name, US.read the main + drop-in and hash via the existing hash_entry. Read owned names ONLY, never the union with rendered — otherwise a leaked unowned file on disk hashes as Unchanged and never starts, which is this bug re-entered from the other side.
- Write_all splits into a pure Render_all plus a write step.
- The file-removal set is `owned \ rendered_names`, NOT the diff's Removed rows: a unit whose main file vanished but whose drop-in dir survived produces no Removed row, and the drop-in would leak.
- Ownership persists two-phase: `owned U rendered_names` before the writes, `rendered_names` after the removals, both before apply_plan. Invariant: the manifest always names a superset of pctl's files on disk. This closes two leaks — US.write raising mid-loop (Install_failed: ENOSPC/EACCES), and start_unit propagating from apply_row (lifecycle.ml:112) before replace_manifest (:181) ever runs.
- Unit_store gains `read : t -> unit_:Unit_filename.t -> entry option`; In_mem.inspect is promoted to it. None means the main file is absent, and nothing else — any other errno raises Install_failed. A lenient `with _ -> None` would turn a permissions fault into "restart everything, every run".
- Fs.write with dropin=None must delete an existing drop-in dir. fs.ml:74-77 currently returns without touching it while In_mem.write replaces the whole entry, so the adapters already disagree; in_mem.ml's header claims it mirrors Fs's observable semantics. read . write = id becomes load-bearing here: without it a stale slice drop-in makes the slice permanently Changed on every reload.
- lifecycle.ml:40-49 gets deleted. It documents a one-time hash-formula churn against stored hashes that will no longer exist.

## Why not the alternatives
- Clearing manifest rows in Session.reset fixes only the reboot trigger and leaves the class open (hand-deleted files stay broken). It also keys the fix on boot id; D1 needs no boot id at all.
- Deleting the manifest table entirely (filesystem fully self-describing via PCTL_ID in the drop-in) needs two ownership rules, one of them a parse of a generated file, and makes gc's correctness depend on a drop-in that could have been half-written.
- Making `up` a reconciler (Unchanged requires unit_state = Active) was rejected: Schema.kind includes Oneshot and mkProject.nix:106 always forces Type=, so it would re-run every oneshot and every genuinely-failed service on each invocation. up and reload are the same function (lifecycle.ml:184-185), so they cannot be given different convergence semantics without breaking "reload is the only primitive".

## Behaviour changes to note
- A user editing a unit file inside user.control by hand now surfaces as Changed and self-heals, where today it was invisible.
- Post-reboot `pctl up` now prints `+N` rows where it printed `=N`.
acceptance_criteria:
## Tests

Integration (test_lifecycle.ml, whose header at :5-6 already earmarks exactly these):
- reboot: up -> Session.reset_with_boot_id ~boot_id:"boot-2" -> fresh empty In_mem store -> up -> every row Added, every unit started.
- hand-delete: up -> US.remove one service -> up -> that unit Added, the rest Unchanged.
- superset invariant: fail_next_write -> up raises -> the manifest already names the units written before the failure.
- persist ordering: fail_next_start -> up raises -> the manifest is persisted anyway.

Unit:
- Fs: write {dropin=Some _} -> write {dropin=None} -> read gives dropin=None. This is the ONLY place the Fs defect is catchable; In_mem never had it, so every fake-backed test is blind to it.
- Plan.diff relocated from test_manifest.ml, behaviour unchanged.

E2E (new test, template = test_down_missing_units.ml):
- up -> assert active -> `systemctl --user stop <slice>` -> rm the unit files and .d dirs from user.control -> daemon-reload -> pctl up -> is-active reports active.
- The stop is REQUIRED. Deleting a unit file kills nothing (measured in test_down_missing_units.ml's header), so without it the services stay active, `up` no-ops on an already-active unit, and the test passes without ever exercising a start — a test that cannot fail for the right reason.
- Test header records what a real reboot changes that this does not (boot id, host reallocation, systemd's loaded-unit set) and why none of it is load-bearing under D1.

Gate: dune test green; dune build @e2e --force green; scripts/e2e-repeat.sh green.

## Docs (same commit — these lines become false the moment the code lands; pctl-oik is closed, so they land here)

- UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:29 Manifest — no longer "{unit-filename: sha256} snapshot ... used as the left side of the next reload diff". It is the set of unit filenames a project owns, persisted in the registry, and it is the authority for what down and gc may delete. The left side of the diff is read from user.control per invocation.
- :41 Registry — amend "plus its manifest rows" to say what those rows now hold.
- :73-76 Reload diff — "present in new manifest, absent in old" becomes "present in rendered, absent in installed". The added(+) row's ACTION changes under pctl-added-restarts-g31, not here.
- :105 rule — "up writes one Registry row and one Manifest; reload reads the Manifest" no longer describes the flow.
- :121 dialogue — "The new spec file produces a new manifest. Diffing against the stored manifest ..." restates the removed design.

title: docs: the rewrite plan's error listing has a second drift, two lines above the paragraph added to disclose its drift
close_reason: exit → exit_code corrected, and the parenthetical inventory deleted — the paragraph now names Schema.error as the contract without claiming to enumerate the divergence.

title: e2e: the reexec-kicker machinery is now duplicated verbatim across two test files
description:
test/e2e/test_unit_state_survives_reexec.ml is the second test to drive a backgrounded daemon-reexec kicker, and it copies the whole apparatus from test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml rather than sharing it. Byte-identical or near-identical pairs:

  kicker_script          reload:56-64   unit_state:64-72   (identical)
  count_lines            reload:74-77   unit_state:82-85   (identical)
  scratch_path           reload:79-82   unit_state:87-90   (differs only in the filename prefix, which must differ)
  capped ()              reload:112-115 unit_state:144-147 (identical)
  marker/marker_tmp/tally/log + clear () + Fun.protect
                         reload:96-105  unit_state:124-133 (identical shape)
  'kicker did not complete' Alcotest.failf + log dump
                         reload:127-134 unit_state:167-173 (differs only by a line wrap)

None of these exist in test/e2e/harness.ml, which is the shared library every e2e test already links.

pctl-ra1 predicted the read_file half of this exactly — 'test/e2e links e2e_harness, not test_helpers or cli's internals, so the fifth caller will copy it again' — and the fifth caller duly did, verbatim, including the ''-on-missing behaviour that ticket flags as load-bearing. This ticket is the rest of it: read_file is one function out of six.

Not filed as a defect in the new test. Copying was the right call for landing pctl-g9l, and the second instance is what establishes the shape — one copy is not yet a pattern. But a third reexec test should not have to make the same decision.

Fix: lift the kicker apparatus into harness.ml as one unit — something like Harness.with_reexec_kicker ~count ~gap (fun ~confirmed -> ...) that owns the marker/tally/log paths, the set -e script, the completion assertion and the cleanup, and hands the body a confirmed-count. Take read_file with it and close pctl-ra1's e2e half at the same time. Both existing tests then call it.

Filed from round 3 of the review (the working tree implementing pctl-g9l/m6s/3mi/yt8/7kw).
close_reason: Extracted test/e2e/reexec.ml into the harness library: kicker script, marker protocol, tally, derived cap, poll_until_finished, request_stop, settle. Both reexec tests use it; the six verbatim copies (including pctl-ra1's predicted fifth read_file) are gone. Done now rather than deferred because the round-3 redesign would otherwise have forked a diverging second copy.

title: Session.reset bypasses the Clock port, so a frozen clock does not freeze the boot id that decides row deletion
description:
Introduced as a visible seam by the dead-code-cleanup diff (pctl-lrc), which made Clock the single boot-id source and added a 'clock' dependency to lib/state/dune.

lib/state/session.ml:55-57 calls the concrete reader directly:

  let reset (conn : Db.t) : unit =
    reset_with_boot_id conn ~boot_id:(Clock.read_boot_id_exn ())

while lib/cli/pipeline.ml:184 stamps the row through the port:

    let boot_id = P.Clock.read_boot_id () in
    ... session_id = (if boot_id = "" then None else Some boot_id);

Two consequences.

1. The Clock port is not honoured on the path that deletes rows. test/integration/test_pipeline_up.ml:25 uses 'Clock.frozen ~now:"2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00" ~boot:"test-boot"'. In that test with_connection (pipeline.ml:40-45) resets against the REAL /proc boot id while with_project stamps "test-boot", so reset_query's 'session_id != ?' predicate does not match what the test wrote. A second with_connection in the same test would NULL the row it just created. Today the tests do one pipeline call each, so it passes by luck.

2. The 'if boot_id = "" then None' branch at pipeline.ml:192 is dead in production and encodes a false invariant. Every path into with_project goes through with_connection first (pipeline.ml:169), where Session.reset already raised if the boot id was unreadable or blank. The site comment on Clock.Real.read_boot_id (clock.ml:53-56) presents "" as a legitimate NULL, but by the time it runs "" cannot occur. This is the same shape as the false 'single caller' comment the cleanup diff removed.

Fix (recommended): add read_boot_id_exn to Clock.S — Real forwards to the top-level function, frozen returns 'boot' and raises if it is empty. Have Pipeline.with_connection read it once through the port and pass it to State.Session.reset_with_boot_id, and reuse that same value for the with_project stamp. That honours the port on both paths, lets pipeline.ml:192's dead branch go, and drops the new 'clock' dependency from lib/state/dune since Session then only needs reset_with_boot_id.

Alternative, if the port should stay two-valued: leave Session.reset as-is and just delete the '= ""' branch with a comment naming with_connection as the guarantee. Cheaper, but leaves the frozen-clock inconsistency in (1).

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Seam is now committed as c7fb526033426ca04d980417e2d4b0d2419668d8. The comment on Clock.Real.read_boot_id was corrected in that commit to say "" is unreachable at Pipeline's stamp (with_connection runs Session.reset first) rather than presenting it as a legitimate NULL — point 2's false-invariant half. The port bypass itself is untouched and still owned here.

title: cli/pipeline: down ~quiet:true maps every failure to exit 0, so a propagated stop failure reports success
description:
Pre-existing, but pctl-8sd makes it consequential: Lifecycle.down now propagates a non-no-such-unit slice stop failure, and this site erases it.

lib/cli/pipeline.ml:292-295:
    if quiet then
      try
        work ();
        0
      with _ -> 0
    else run work

`with _ -> 0` is broader than Pctl_error — it swallows Failure, Sys_error, Not_found, everything — and returns the success exit code.

Sole caller is test/e2e/harness.ml:209 teardown, which additionally wraps it in `try ... with _ -> ()`. So the observable effect today is that e2e teardown cannot fail: a project whose slice would not stop leaves its units on disk and its processes running on the dev's session, and the test suite reports green. That is the 'Straggler' failure mode UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:91 already names, with the one signal that would have caught it discarded.

Fix: decide what quiet means. If it means "don't print", drop the catch entirely and let the exit code carry the failure. If teardown genuinely must not abort, catch in the harness (which already does) and have it print the rendered error rather than swallowing at the pipeline layer. Either way the double swallow should collapse to one deliberate site.

title: prose: the StopUnit-on-a-slice-succeeds claim is now in three places, one of which says it is not restating it
description:
761669c fixed pctl-2nc by collapsing the sd_bus_error_set_errno mechanism to one account, then wrote a new fact into three.

Owner (the recording against real systemd) -- test/e2e/test_down_missing_units.ml:14-22:
    - `dbus-send --session ... Manager.StopUnit` on an unloaded .service
      answers "org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit ..."; on an unloaded
      .slice it SUCCEEDS and returns a job path.
    systemd synthesises .slice units that have no fragment ...

Copy 1 -- lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml:24-25:
    an unloaded .service answers this name, an unloaded .slice succeeds
    and returns a job path.

Copy 2 -- test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml:191-193:
    For the .slice these tests arm, StopUnit on this systemd SUCCEEDS
    instead -- systemd synthesises fragment-less slices ...

bus_errors.ml:30-31 then says the e2e file 'exists for' the slice half and holds it 'instead of restating it' -- five lines after restating it.

Per CLAUDE.md: a fact belongs to whatever can be checked mechanically, and the why exists exactly once. The e2e file diffs against reality; the two comments diff against nothing.

Fix: bus_errors keeps the loads/does-not-load split (that is its own fact, it justifies the per-op difference) and the pointer, dropping the .service/.slice outcome sentence. test_lifecycle keeps its second paragraph's conclusion -- that these two cases assert the policy rather than record a slice reply -- and drops the restatement of why the slice succeeds, pointing instead.

Filed from the review of 761669c.
close_reason: bus_errors keeps only its own fact (loads vs does-not-load, so the two ops disagree per unit type) and names the e2e file as where the types are recorded. test_lifecycle's helper drops the mechanism and says what its cases assert instead. The outcome sentence now exists once, in the recording.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Correction, from round 2. This ticket's body attributed the phrase 'instead of restating it' to lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml:30-31. That is wrong — the phrase is from pctl-9rt's CLOSE REASON, not from the file. Checked:

    git show 761669c:lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml | grep restat  -> no match
    git show HEAD:lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml     | grep restat  -> no match

So the rhetorical point in the title ('one of which says it is not restating it') does not hold against the code; it held against the ticket that closed 9rt.

The substance was still partly real — the .service/.slice outcome sentence did appear in bus_errors.ml:24-25 and in test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml:191-193 alongside the e2e recording — and f7ff155 collapsed it correctly: bus_errors.ml:22-28 now states only the per-op rule and points at test_down_missing_units.ml for which unit types those are.

Weaker than filed, in other words: three passages that overlapped, not one passage contradicting itself.

title: in_mem: fail_next_read is one-shot per unit, so unit_job_pending's narrowing cannot be driven by any caller
description:
761669c added [fail_next_read] and closed pctl-7yg with 'arming both unit_state and unit_job_pending, since the Dbus adapter reaches both through one GetUnit'. The field comment says so too:

lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml:39-44:
    fail_next_read : (string, string option * string) Hashtbl.t;
        (* unit -> (error_name, reply) for the next [unit_state] or
           [unit_job_pending]. Same one-shot shape as [fail_next_stop].
           Both reads are one GetUnit in the Dbus adapter, which is where a
           peer-gone reply lands during a daemon-reexec, so the fake models
           them as failing together. *)

They cannot fail together. raise_if_read_armed (in_mem.ml:166-173) does Hashtbl.remove before it raises, so the arm is consumed by whichever read runs first.

In Probe.wait_unit_state (lib/probe/probe.ml:180-200) the order is fixed:

    M.subscribe_unit_changes handle ~unit:service_unit try_resolve;
    let initial = M.unit_state handle ~unit:service_unit in
    try_resolve initial;

unit_state always runs first and eats the arm. unit_job_pending is only reached afterwards, from try_resolve's `Maybe_terminal arm, by which point the table is empty. So dbus.ml:772-774's narrowing -- the one pctl-q2j argued matters most, because a swallowed bus fault there ends the wait early and reports a starting service as terminated -- still has no test, and no test can be written against the fake as it stands.

Fix: key the table by (unit, op), or add a separate fail_next_job_pending, or drop the one-shot removal in favour of an explicit clear. Then add the case: push Inactive, set the pending-job marker, arm the job-pending read, assert wait_service raises rather than returning a terminal Inactive row. Correct the field comment either way -- 'models them as failing together' is false today.

Filed from the review of 761669c.
close_reason: Split into fail_next_unit_state and fail_next_job_pending, one table per read — the Dbus adapter issues a separate GetUnit + Properties.Get pair for each, so 'failing together' was wrong about the adapter as well as unusable. Added the case the ticket specifies (Inactive + pending job + armed job read → wait_service raises, not a terminal row) and one pinning that reading state first does not consume the job arm. Mutation-checked: absorbing the job arm fails both.

title: gc: two catch-alls in opportunistic_sweep swallow Eio cancellation and Out_of_memory
description:
lib/gc/gc.ml:111-115 and 118-120. Pre-existing in shape; this diff moved the boot-id read inside the outer try and its new header comment now leans on the outer catch as a safety property ('opportunistic_sweep already wraps its body in warn-and-proceed, so there a raise degrades to a skipped sweep').

            | Schema.Unknown -> (
                try remove_project ~conn ~handle row
                with e ->
                  Printf.eprintf "pctl gc: warn — failed to sweep %s: %s\n" row.id (Printexc.to_string e))
      ...
      with e ->
        Printf.eprintf "pctl gc: warn — sweep aborted: %s\n" (Printexc.to_string e)

Warn-and-proceed is the documented policy for the sweep (gc.ml header: 'Failures warn to stderr and return unit; never abort the outer command'), and that policy is right for I/O failures. But 'with e' also catches Eio.Cancel.Cancelled, Out_of_memory and Stack_overflow. The cancellation case is user-visible: Ctrl-C during the sweep at the top of 'pctl up' prints 'pctl gc: warn — sweep aborted: Cancelled' and the command carries on into the rest of with_project instead of unwinding.

Fix: narrow both handlers to the failures the policy is about — Schema.Pctl_error, Sys_error, Unix.Unix_error — and let anything else propagate. Note the outer handler is also what the new header comment relies on to make a read_boot_id_exn raise degrade to a skipped sweep, so Sys_error must stay in the narrowed set.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Two more sites with the same shape, added by e778a30 (review of the pctl-nir/a7p/q2j batch):

  lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:861-866 — `try entry.cb s with e -> prerr_endline …` in the sd_bus_add_match handler
  lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml:74-78 — the same catch in the fake, added for adapter parity

Both are an improvement on what they replaced (`with _ -> ()`, pctl-26e item 3) and the Dbus one genuinely cannot let an exception into the C dispatch frame — but `with e` still covers Eio.Cancel.Cancelled, Out_of_memory and Stack_overflow, which is this ticket's complaint.

Reachability of Cancelled specifically I did not verify: Probe's callback (probe.ml:183-196) does a synchronous bus call plus Eio.Promise.resolve, neither of which is obviously a cancellation point. The In_mem copy has no C frame at all, so it does not need a catch-all for the stated reason. Whatever narrowed set this ticket lands on should cover all four sites.

title: clock: the empty/unreadable boot id raises Sys_error, which pctl reports as 'unexpected error' with exit 1
description:
lib/clock/clock.ml:39, introduced by the dead-code-cleanup diff (pctl-lrc) on the prior review's own prescription ('raise Sys_error (boot_id_path ^ ": empty boot id")').

  if raw = "" then raise (Sys_error (path ^ ": empty boot id")) else raw

Sys_error is not Schema.Pctl_error, so it falls through to the catch-all in Cli.Pipeline.run (lib/cli/pipeline.ml:55-57):

  | e ->
      Printf.eprintf "pctl: unexpected error: %s\n" (Printexc.to_string e);
      1

The user sees 'pctl: unexpected error: Sys_error("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id: empty boot id")' and exit 1. The condition is expected, named, and diagnosable — reporting it as 'unexpected' with the generic bucket contradicts the exit-code taxonomy documented at lib/schema/schema.ml:486-497, where every known failure gets its own code.

Not urgent: the message does name the path and the problem, so it is debuggable. What is wrong is the channel.

Fix: raise Schema.Pctl_error with an arm that names the file and what to check. Registry_io { id; reason } fits without widening the error type (bucket 4). A dedicated arm is cleaner but changes the public error type and the exit-code table, which is a domain-model call.

Note for whoever takes this: test/unit/test_clock.ml asserts 'with Sys_error _', so the tests move with the change.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Introduced by c7fb526033426ca04d980417e2d4b0d2419668d8 as described. test/unit/test_clock.ml asserts 'with Sys_error _', so those four cases move with the fix.

title: docs: the plan's test-only API listing names a module that does not exist and is two APIs stale
description:
docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md:460:

    - Test-only API: `Fake.fail_next_start`, `Fake.push_state`, `Fake.inspect`.

Two problems. The module is Systemctl.In_mem — there is no `Fake` module in the tree (CLAUDE.md calls it 'the in-memory fake', which is the concept, not the name). And the listing is stale by three entries: fail_next_stop (e778a30), then fail_next_read (761669c), then fail_next_unit_state + fail_next_job_pending (f7ff155).

This is the same file and the same failure mode as pctl-xgl and pctl-47k, ~180 lines from the hunk that added 'read it for shape and the code for truth' — a hand-maintained inventory in prose that no artifact checks. It is the third listing in this document to drift, which is the argument for not keeping listings rather than for correcting this one again.

lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml:11-19 already carries the same list and travels with the code.

Fix: replace the line with a pointer at In_mem's header. If the plan's narrative needs to mention the fake has test-only arming APIs, say that without enumerating them.

Filed from round 2 of the review of 761669c/f7ff155.
close_reason: The Fake.* listing is gone; the plan names Systemctl.In_mem and defers to that module's header for the fault-injection API, which is where it can be checked.

title: test_probe: the new case's comment names the wrong set of reads as the raising path
description:
test/unit/test_probe.ml:386-389 (new in 761669c):

    * The read that fails here is the initial one inside [wait_unit_state]
    * (probe.ml), which is the only one on the raising path: a failure inside
    * the subscription callback is reported and dropped by the Dbus handler
    * instead, which is tracked by pctl-vv4.

'the only one on the raising path' is false. lib/probe/probe.ml:197-199:

    M.subscribe_unit_changes handle ~unit:service_unit try_resolve;
    let initial = M.unit_state handle ~unit:service_unit in
    try_resolve initial;

try_resolve initial runs synchronously in the caller's fiber, and its `Maybe_terminal arm calls M.unit_job_pending (probe.ml:192). So an Inactive initial read puts a SECOND read on the raising path, in the same fiber, propagating to the same caller.

The contrast the comment is drawing -- synchronous initial path raises, subscription-callback path is caught and dropped by safe_unit_state_forward (dbus.ml:778-789, pctl-vv4) -- is correct. Only 'the only one' is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that hides the untested read: see pctl-6ph, where unit_job_pending's narrowing turns out to have no test at all.

Fix: 'the reads on the synchronous initial path' rather than 'the only one'.

Filed from the review of 761669c.
close_reason: Comment reworded to 'both reads on the synchronous initial path', and both are now actually covered — the second one is pctl-6ph's case. The contrast with the subscription-callback path (pctl-vv4) is kept.

title: systemctl fakes: In_mem cannot fail unit_state, so pctl-a7p's narrowing has no test
description:
pctl-a7p asked for: 'Add an integration case: arm the fake to fail get_unit_path with a non-NoSuchUnit reply and assert unit_state propagates rather than answering Inactive.' e778a30 shipped the narrowing without it.

lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml:153 is `let unit_state t ~unit:u = current_state t u` — total, never raises. The fake's only fault injection is fail_next_start (in_mem.ml:163) and fail_next_stop (:169), so no test in test/unit or test/integration can drive lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:725-727:

    let get_unit_path_opt t ~unit:u =
      try Some (get_unit_path t ~unit:u)
      with Schema.Pctl_error e when Bus_errors.is_no_such_unit e -> None

What IS covered: Bus_errors.is_no_such_unit itself (test/unit/test_bus_errors.ml) and the Removed-arm stop propagation (test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml). What is not: that a NoReply from GetUnit reaches the caller instead of becoming Schema.Inactive — the exact regression the ticket was filed for, and the one the pctl-xxf reexec window makes reachable.

Fix: add `fail_next_unit_state t ~unit ~error_name ~reply` to In_mem, same one-shot Hashtbl shape as fail_next_stop, and one integration case asserting unit_state raises Unit_op_failed rather than returning Inactive. unit_job_pending wants the same treatment — it shares get_unit_path_opt.

Filed from the review of e778a30.
close_reason: In_mem gained fail_next_read (~error_name ~reply, same one-shot shape as fail_next_stop) arming both unit_state and unit_job_pending, since the Dbus adapter reaches both through one GetUnit. New case in test_probe: wait_service propagates the Unit_op_failed with the peer-gone name instead of returning a terminal row. Mutation-checked — swallowing the raise in the fake makes it fail with 'got state active', which is the old behaviour. Note this pins the caller-side contract; Dbus.get_unit_path_opt itself still has no test, as the fake cannot drive the real adapter.

title: lifecycle: tear-down swallows the slice stop_unit failure, then deletes every unit file
close_reason: Completed: commit:62bb2582b831887ae9c5e78f4fd6e34c47109b2e

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
## Review — uncommitted working tree (pctl-8sd)

Gates run this session: `dune build` clean · `dune test` exit 0 · `dune build @e2e --force` exit 0 · `dune exec test/e2e/test_down_unloaded_slice.exe` → `test_down_unloaded_slice OK` (session `is-system-running` → degraded, live). No untracked files.

### Intent conformance
The ticket's core is implemented and correct: `lifecycle.ml:175` propagates every stop failure except no-such-unit, and it raises before the `daemon_reload` / `US.remove` / `replace_manifest` sequence, so nothing is half-torn-down. The header bullet the ticket called out is corrected. No missing or wrong requirements.

### Silent failures and implicit values
- `test/e2e/test_down_unloaded_slice.ml:45-53` — every precondition of the test can silently fail to hold, and the test still passes. `if Sys.file_exists p then Sys.remove p` no-ops on a wrong path; both `systemctl_user` calls discard their rc (`let _ = …`), so a failed out-of-band `stop` or `daemon-reload` leaves the units loaded. The name says *unloaded* slice, but nothing asserts the slice was unloaded — only that it is inactive. If any of that degrades, `down` runs against units that are still present and `assert_unit_gone` passes trivially, i.e. the test silently becomes a duplicate of `test_down.ml`. Fix: `Harness.check_rc_zero` on both `systemctl_user` calls; `Harness.assert_unit_exists` before each removal and `Harness.assert_unit_gone` after; assert the slice is *not loaded* (`systemctl --user show -p LoadState`) rather than merely inactive.
- `lib/schema/schema.ml:456-464` — the justification comment claims more than was verified: "Both Systemctl adapters format [reply] name-first … a transport failure leaves the sd_bus_error struct empty, so its reply is a decoded errno and fails the test". `Dbus.format_bus_reply` (`dbus.ml:339-344`) has four arms; `| None, Some message -> message` emits a bare message with no name, which is neither name-first nor a decoded errno. Behaviour is safe (it propagates), the comment is the defect. Fix: qualify to "name-first when the sd_bus_error struct carries a name; a name-less or errno-only reply fails the test, which is the safe direction".

### Standards and smells
- `lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:20` (new) and `test/e2e/test_down_unloaded_slice.ml:14,26` — "tear-down". UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:17 lists it as an alias to avoid: `| **Down** | Stopping the slice, removing installed units, dropping the registry entry | Stop, teardown |`, and the preamble says flagged synonyms "exist only to call out drift that should not appear in code or docs". Fix: "the down path". Pre-existing at `lifecycle.ml:156`, so one edit covers both.

### Reuse
- `test/e2e/test_down_unloaded_slice.ml:54-55` — `Harness.assert_false ~label:"slice not active before down" (Harness.is_active slice)` is verbatim `Harness.assert_unit_inactive` (`harness.ml:473-476`). Fix: call it. (Keep the stronger load-state assertion from the finding above instead, if taken.)
- `test/e2e/test_down_unloaded_slice.ml:46-52` — the hand-rolled unit-file + drop-in removal re-implements `Unit_store.Fs.remove` (`fs.ml:79-82`), which `rm_rf`s the drop-in dir and tolerates absence. `unit_store` is already in the e2e `libraries` and `Fs.create ()` reads the XDG env at construction, so this is a drop-in replacement — and `harness.ml:160-165` states path construction routes through `Unit_store.Fs` precisely "so this harness never duplicates the user.control layout". Fix: `let st = Unit_store.Fs.create () in List.iter (fun uf -> Unit_store.Fs.remove st ~unit_:uf) [ Schema.Unit_filename.slice ~id; Schema.Unit_filename.service ~id ~service:"web" ]`, dropping the separate drop-in line. Also drops the redundant `id_s`/`slice` locals (`Harness.slice_name id_s` and `slice_filename_for ~id` return the identical string).

### In-scope fixes before commit
All five above. Two are comment/wording (`schema.ml` justification, "tear-down"), three are the new e2e test (loud preconditions, `assert_unit_inactive`, `Fs.remove`). None touch the production fix, which stands as written.

### Beads hygiene
- `pctl-8sd` has no resolution comment yet (`br comments list pctl-8sd` → "No comments"); status is still `in_progress` and close reason unset — the user's call after this report.
- No parent map/epic exists for `pctl-8sd`, so there is no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` block to update.
- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is exported and in sync (`br sync --status` → Dirty issues: 0, Status: In sync) but currently `MM` — the Phase-5 filings below are unstaged. `git add .beads/` before committing.

### Filed
Filed pctl-2m8, pctl-8za, pctl-q2j, pctl-67s, pctl-fl6, pctl-nir, pctl-ufh.

### Verdict
Not ready for `/commit`: five in-scope fixes above (three in the new e2e test, two comment accuracy), plus `git add .beads/`. The production change itself is correct and gate-green.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Narrowed the down path's slice stop_unit catch to Schema.is_no_such_unit (a prefix test on Unit_op_failed's reply); every other stop failure now propagates before the units are deleted.

Measured on this host (systemd 257): dbus-send Manager.StopUnit on an unloaded .service answers "org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit: Unit x.service not loaded.", but on an unloaded .slice it SUCCEEDS and returns a job path - systemd synthesises fragment-less .slice units. `systemctl --user show -p LoadState` agrees: a never-existing .slice reports `loaded`, a .service `not-found`. So the tolerated branch is unreachable for a slice on this version; kept anyway as the documented intent, and exercised through the fake in the integration layer.

Also measured: `pctl down` on an unregistered path fails earlier with Registry_io (exit 4) and never enters Lifecycle, so reaching the tolerated case needs a registered project whose units were removed out of band. Production `pctl down` surfaces the propagated failure as exit 5 - `~quiet:true`, which erases it (pctl-67s), has exactly one caller: e2e teardown.

Tests: test_down_tolerates_stop_failure inverted to test_down_propagates_stop_failure (asserts the raise plus survival of the unit files, manifest rows and allocated host, so a retried down can still stop things); added test_down_tolerates_no_such_unit; a Schema.is_no_such_unit unit test including non-prefix rejection; new e2e test_down_missing_units.

Review fixes applied, with one deviation: the review asked to assert the slice is not-loaded via LoadState - impossible per the measurement above, so the test was renamed test_down_unloaded_slice -> test_down_missing_units and asserts what actually holds (fragments gone, drop-in gone, slice inactive, service LoadState=not-found).

Gates: dune test green, dune build @e2e --force exit 0, nix flake check all checks passed.

title: lifecycle: apply_row's [Removed] arm still swallows every Pctl_error, not just no-such-unit
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing pctl-8sd, which narrowed the sibling site.

lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:116-117:
    | Schema.Removed -> (
        try M.stop_unit handle ~unit:unit_s
        with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> ())

The module header (lifecycle.ml:15-17) justifies this as "systemd may have already GCed the unit after its file was deleted" — and the reload path does delete the file first (lifecycle.ml:149-152 removes Removed rows from the unit store before apply_plan, and apply_plan daemon_reloads before stopping). So a no-such-unit reply here is genuinely expected.

But the catch is not limited to that. A transport failure, a bus disconnect, or a stop that systemd refuses is swallowed identically — and by then the unit FILE IS ALREADY GONE, so the still-running process is orphaned with no unit left to manage it. The excuse covers "unit was GCed", not "the bus died".

Fix: narrow to `with Schema.Pctl_error e when Schema.is_no_such_unit e -> ()` (the predicate added by pctl-8sd) and update the header bullet to say no-such-unit only. Add an integration case arming fail_next_stop on a Removed service row with a non-NoSuchUnit reply and asserting it propagates.
close_reason: apply_row's Removed arm tolerates only no-such-unit; module header bullet corrected. Two integration cases added: a Removed row whose stop fails with NoReply propagates and leaves the manifest intact, and one whose stop answers NoSuchUnit completes.

title: gc: the new Reload retry turns a peer-gone window into a silent multi-second stall, because both gc reloads are swallowed
description:
Raised in the pctl-jbd review; the retry diff acknowledges it in a comment but does not fix it, so it needs to be tracked.

lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:570-573 (new):

    (* Say so when the budget was spent, so an immediate rejection and
     * a five-second exhausted retry are distinguishable. Callers that
     * discard the error still get the seconds in the message —
     * [Gc.opportunistic_sweep] swallows this one entirely. *)

That last clause is exactly the problem. lib/gc/gc.ml:117 and :128 both call M.daemon_reload inside ignore_best_effort (gc.ml:71-73), which catches Schema.Pctl_error, so the carefully constructed "(gave up after N attempts over 5.0s)" string is built and then dropped with nothing printed.

Cost, now that the retry exists:
  - remove_project issues two reloads, so each swept row can burn 2 x Bus_retry.peer_gone_budget = 10 s.
  - opportunistic_sweep (gc.ml:140) runs at the top of up/reload/down/restart (lib/cli/pipeline.ml:170, :204), once per Unknown row.
  - purge (gc.ml:163) runs it per non-Live row.

So with the user manager off the bus for a non-transient reason — ServiceUnknown / NameHasNoOwner are in peer_gone_error_names and are NOT necessarily a passing reexec — 'pctl up' gains up to 10 s of dead air per Unknown row and 'pctl gc --yes' up to 10 s per non-Live row, with no output at all. Before the retry these failed instantly (and just as silently).

Two things to decide, separably:
  1. Should gc's reloads opt out of the retry? A sweep is opportunistic; waiting 5 s for a manager that may not come back is a poor trade there, unlike on the lifecycle path where the reload is load-bearing. A ~budget parameter on daemon_reload, or a non-retrying variant, would express that.
  2. Regardless of (1), the swallow should not be total. Every other gc failure path prints 'pctl gc: warn — ...' with describe_exn (gc.ml:151-155, :175-178); ignore_best_effort is the one that prints nothing. Give it the same warn-and-proceed treatment so an exhausted retry is at least visible.

Note the interaction: fixing (2) alone still leaves the stall; fixing (1) alone still leaves it silent.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Count correction after pctl-e0d: 'both gc reloads' is now one. remove_project issues a single best-effort daemon_reload, after the file deletions. The silent stall is still there and still swallowed; the ceiling halves.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Location + arithmetic update after the pctl-e0d working tree (not yet committed). This ticket's body and its 2026-08-04 comment both point at code that has moved.

Was cited as: gc.ml:117 and :128, i.e. two reloads inside remove_project; the 2026-08-04 correction narrowed that to one, still inside remove_project.

Now: remove_project issues ZERO reloads (lib/gc/gc.ml:127-130 says so explicitly). The reload moved out to the two entry points, one per RUN, and only when something was removed:
  lib/gc/gc.ml:167   if !removed then ignore_best_effort (fun () -> M.daemon_reload handle)   (opportunistic_sweep)
  lib/gc/gc.ml:196   if removed > 0 then ignore_best_effort (fun () -> M.daemon_reload handle) (purge)

Both are still inside ignore_best_effort (gc.ml:71-73), so both findings stand unchanged in kind:
  (1) the retry stall is still there — but the ceiling is now 1 x peer_gone_budget per COMMAND (5s), not per Unknown row, and zero when the sweep removed nothing. 'pctl gc --yes' likewise: 5s for the run, not 5s per non-Live row.
  (2) the swallow is still total, and one case got WORSE in consequence rather than better. purge's trailing reload is now the only reload on that path — gc.ml:194-195 states it: 'No lifecycle work follows pctl gc --yes, so this is the only reload that will tell systemd the files are gone.' Nothing downstream flushes it. Meanwhile purge still prints 'removed <id>' per row (gc.ml:185) and returns the count, so a run whose only reload failed reports unqualified success while systemd keeps every deleted fragment loaded. opportunistic_sweep is the milder case: any later command's own reload flushes the stale view.

So point (2) of this ticket's 'two things to decide' now has a concrete worst case to name, and point (1)'s magnitude drops. The fix is unchanged: give ignore_best_effort's reload the same 'pctl gc: warn — ...' + describe_exn treatment every other gc failure path already gets.

title: bus_errors: the NoSuchUnit claim is broader than what was measured, and disagrees with the e2e file's version
description:
lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml:22-27 (new in e778a30):

    Verified on systemd 260.1: Manager.StopUnit and Manager.ResetFailedUnit
    on an unloaded unit both answer this name (dbus-send --session
    --print-reply).

test/e2e/test_down_missing_units.ml:15-27, measured on this repo's host at systemd 257, records the opposite for one kind of unit:

    - `dbus-send --session … Manager.StopUnit` on an unloaded .service
      answers "org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit: Unit x.service not
      loaded."; on an unloaded .slice it SUCCEEDS and returns a job path.
    systemd synthesises .slice units that have no fragment, so a slice can
    never be made not-loadable

So 'an unloaded unit' is false for slices, and the two blocks pin different systemd versions (260.1 vs 257) with nothing reconciling them. This is the case CLAUDE.md's 'verify the case, claim only the case' names: the measurement was on services, the sentence claims units.

It is not academic — Lifecycle's down path stops a SLICE and tolerates no-such-unit there (lifecycle.ml:19-25), and per the e2e file that tolerance is unreachable on the slice, which is why test_down_missing_units asserts the observable contract instead.

Fix: narrow bus_errors.ml's sentence to .service, and either re-measure the .slice case on 260.1 and record both, or point at test_down_missing_units.ml for the slice behaviour rather than restating it.

Filed from the review of e778a30.
close_reason: Re-measured on 260.1: StopUnit on a never-existing .slice SUCCEEDS and returns a job path, on an unloaded .service answers NoSuchUnit; ResetFailedUnit answers NoSuchUnit for a slice too, because it does not load the name (GENERIC_UNIT_LOAD, dbus-manager.c). Comment now states the per-op split and points at test_down_missing_units.ml for the slice contract instead of restating it. test_lifecycle.ml's helper corrected too — it arms a slice, so those two cases assert the policy, not an observed reply.

title: systemctl/dbus: unit_state reports Inactive for ANY Pctl_error from GetUnit, so a bus fault reads as a healthy stopped unit
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing the pctl-jbd retry diff.

lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:673-682:

    let unit_state t ~unit:u =
      (* GetUnit may fail with NoSuchUnit for a unit that has never been
       * loaded. systemd's own `systemctl is-active` reports "inactive" in
       * that case, so mirror that. We treat any exception on get_unit_path
       * as "inactive". *)
      match
        try Some (get_unit_path t ~unit:u) with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> None
      with
      | None -> Schema.Inactive
      | Some path -> ...

The comment's justification covers NoSuchUnit and says so; the catch covers every Pctl_error. Same shape as pctl-8za and pctl-2m8, both of which were narrowed to Schema.is_no_such_unit.

Why it matters more than the usual over-broad catch: the value is not discarded, it is REPLACED with a plausible wrong answer. A transport failure, a denied call, or a peer-gone reply all render as 'this unit is inactive' to whoever asked — probe (lib/probe/probe.ml) and 'pctl status' among them. A running service reports as stopped, and nothing anywhere says a bus call failed.

Newly reachable in practice: pctl-xxf establishes that GetUnit (dbus.ml:686) is one of the unretried calls during a daemon-reexec window, where it answers org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply. So during any NixOS / home-manager activation, unit_state can silently report every unit as Inactive.

Fix: narrow to `with Schema.Pctl_error e when Schema.is_no_such_unit e -> None` and let everything else propagate. Correct the comment to say no-such-unit only. Add an integration case: arm the fake to fail get_unit_path with a non-NoSuchUnit reply and assert unit_state propagates rather than answering Inactive.

Check unit_job_pending (dbus.ml, the Properties.Get(Job) path) for the same shape — a swallowed error there yields 'no job pending', which is the same class of plausible wrong answer.
close_reason: unit_state and unit_job_pending share get_unit_path_opt, which tolerates only Bus_errors.is_no_such_unit; everything else propagates. safe_unit_state_forward now returns a state option and reports the failure instead of answering Inactive.

title: lifecycle: Added must restart, not start, when the unit is still running
description:
Under pctl-468's D1 fix, `Added` stops meaning "this unit is new" and starts meaning "no file on disk". Those are not the same, because deleting a unit file kills nothing — measured and recorded in test/e2e/test_down_missing_units.ml's header (fragment gone, unit still loaded, processes still running).

Repro: hand-rm a service's unit file from user.control, edit the spec, `pctl up`.
- `installed` has no hash for it -> Added
- apply_row calls start_unit (lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:112)
- systemd no-ops because the unit is already active
- the process keeps running the OLD config; pctl prints `+` and exits 0

Today the same case yields Changed -> restart_unit and is handled correctly, so D1 regresses it. The information to distinguish "new" from "vanished but running" is not recoverable: the file was missing, so there is no installed hash, and no query to systemd reveals what the vanished file used to contain.

## Fix
services: `Added -> restart_unit`. slice: `Added -> start_unit` (unchanged).

RestartUnit on an inactive or unloaded unit simply starts it, so this is identical to today for genuinely-new units and for the whole post-reboot path (nothing is active there). Zero extra D-Bus calls. Querying unit_state on Added rows was considered and buys nothing, since restart-on-inactive already IS start.

Cost: a spurious bounce when a file vanished, the content would have matched, and the service was healthy. Accepted — a spurious restart is visible and self-correcting, a stale process is neither, and reaching it requires a manual rm against a running service.

## The slice carve-out is not symmetry
`restart` on an active slice cascade-kills every service in its cgroup. Delete only pctl-<id>.slice and leave the service files intact: the slice goes Added -> restart -> every service dies, while the services are Unchanged -> not restarted -> the project is entirely dead and `pctl up` reports success. Strictly worse than the bug D1 fixes. Same hazard lifecycle.ml:96-99 already documents for Changed on a slice, so is_slice_unit gains a second use rather than a new concept.

## Docs
UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:73 defines "Action: added (+)" as `start`. It becomes `start` for the slice, `restart` for services.

## Tests
- integration: unit already active + file absent + rendered bytes differ -> assert restart_unit was called, not start_unit.
- integration: slice active + slice file absent -> assert start_unit, never restart_unit, and that no service was stopped.
acceptance_criteria:
Tests:
- integration: unit already active + file absent + rendered bytes differ -> restart_unit called, not start_unit.
- integration: slice active + slice file absent -> start_unit called, never restart_unit, and no service stopped.

Docs (same commit):
- UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:73 "Action: added (+)" is `start` for the slice and `restart` for services.
close_reason: Added restarts services, plain-starts the slice; two integration tests plus the UL action table

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
# Review — working tree, pre-commit

Gates run this session, both green:
- `dune test --force` → 17 tests in `lifecycle`, including `Added service that is still running is restarted` and `Added slice is started, never restarted`. Exit 0.
- `dune build @e2e --force` → exit 0 on the live session (`systemctl --user is-system-running` = degraded, session live). `test_unit_state_survives_reexec` and `test_reload_survives_reexec` both OK.

No untracked files; all four modified files are staged, so the gate reads what I reviewed.

The change itself is right: `apply_row`'s `Added` arm restarts services and still plain-starts the slice, `is_slice_unit` gains its second use rather than a new concept, and `test_up_reloads_once_before_the_jobs` was updated rather than left to drift. `In_mem.restart_unit` (lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml:161-169) is stop-then-start recorded as one wire call, and `do_stop` no-ops on `Inactive`, so the fresh-up path really is one call per unit — the updated expectation proves it.

## Intent conformance

- `test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml:351-354` — the "web was still active going in" check runs AFTER the call under test, and `restart_unit` leaves the unit `Active` regardless, so the assertion cannot fail. AC asks for "unit already active + file absent + rendered bytes differ"; the *already active* half is currently unverified. Fix: bind `In_mem.unit_state handle ~unit:(service_s "web")` next to `let before = ...` and assert that binding before `L.up`.
- `test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml:365-371` — the slice test never asserts the slice was active going in at all, where AC says "slice active + slice file absent". Fix: same treatment, read and assert the slice's state before the second `up`.
- `lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:118-121` — the comment states as present fact that `[Added]` means "no installed hash", and that this is what a deleted-file-under-a-running-process looks like. Neither holds yet: pctl-468 is open and blocked by this ticket, so today the diff's left side is the persisted manifest, a hand-deleted file diffs `Unchanged`, and `Added`-over-a-live-unit is reachable only by forging the manifest the way the new test does. Fix: condition the sentence on D1 the way the test comment at :319-322 already does.
- `UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:74` — the `changed (~)` row was rewritten too, where the Docs AC scopes only line 73's `added (+)`. The new text is true and pre-existing behaviour, and the table would otherwise be half-corrected. Judgement call, no `## Out of scope` to breach; noted, not asked for.

## Prose claims

- `test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml:359-364` — restates the slice cascade-kill hazard that `lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:101-106` owns, then says "Same hazard [apply_row] already documents", which makes the pointer decorative. Fix: keep the pointer sentence alone.
- `test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml:443-446` — restates the RestartUnit-on-an-unloaded-unit mechanism owned by `lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:122-124`. Fix: cite the `Added` arm instead of re-deriving it. (The bead's copy is fine — the long argument lives here by design.)
- `test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml:315` — "Drop [unit_] from the persisted manifest, leaving every other row." restates the `List.filter (not (Unit_filename.equal ...))` three lines below. Fix: delete that sentence, keep the D1/pre-D1 *why*. While rewriting: :324-325 "which is what [Added] must not answer to with a start systemd no-ops" is missing a "that" and doesn't parse.

## Filed

pctl-kab — the premise "deleting a unit file kills nothing" is cited to test/e2e/test_down_missing_units.ml's header, which records LoadState and StopUnit replies only and stops the slice before deleting anything. Asserted, not measured; nowhere in the suite.
pctl-c5e — `Unit_filename` discards its constructor's slice/service knowledge, so `is_slice_unit` re-parses it; this change takes the branch count from one to three.

## Before /commit

Three test fixes and three comment trims above. Then beads hygiene, none of it done yet: this ticket has no resolution comment and no close reason, `.beads/issues.jsonl` currently carries only the status→in_progress flip plus this comment and the two filings, so it needs `br sync --flush-only` and a re-stage of `.beads/` in the same commit as the code.

Verdict: not ready for `/commit`. The behaviour change and both gates are good; blocking is that the two new tests do not yet establish the precondition their AC names, so neither can fail for the reason it exists.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Review follow-up — all six verified in the tree, git diff HEAD shows nothing else changed.

Preconditions: both tests now read state_before ahead of the L.up under test (test_lifecycle.ml:337-346, :370-374), each with the reason at the site. Reads don't record ops, so capturing `before` ahead of them is safe and the ops assertions still pin exactly [daemon-reload; restart|start].

Comments: lifecycle.ml:118-126 conditions the deleted-file claim on pctl-468's D1 rather than asserting it of today's code; the slice test keeps only the pointer to apply_row; the reload-economy comment cites the Added arm; forget_manifest_row keeps the D1/pre-D1 why and drops the List.filter restatement.
