comments.author: manveru
comments.text: Shipped: apply_row's Added arm restarts services and plain-starts the slice (lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml), is_slice_unit gaining a second use rather than a new concept. Two integration tests in test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml pin it — an Added service over a live unit takes 'restart', an Added slice takes 'start' with no stop — each asserting its active-going-in precondition ahead of the call, proved falsifiable by pushing the unit Inactive. test_up_reloads_once_before_the_jobs updated: fresh-up services are RestartUnit, one call as before. UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:73-74 records added(+) as start for the slice, restart for a service. Gates: dune test --force green; dune build @e2e --force exit 0; scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5/5.

title: schema: Unit_filename carries no slice/service kind, so callers re-derive it with a '.slice' suffix test
description:
lib/schema/schema.ml's Unit_filename (:309-343) is constructed by two distinct smart constructors — Unit_filename.slice ~id and Unit_filename.service ~id ~service — and then throws that knowledge away: the type is a string, and nothing on it says which constructor made it.

So a caller that must branch on it re-derives the answer from the filename shape. lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:108-111:

  let is_slice_unit (r : Schema.plan_row) : bool =
    let s = Schema.Unit_filename.to_string r.unit_ in
    let n = String.length s in
    n >= 6 && String.sub s (n - 6) 6 = ".slice"

pctl-added-restarts-g31 doubles the number of arms that consult it (apply_row's Added arm joins Changed, and apply_plan's partition is a third use), which is what makes it worth a ticket now rather than at the first use.

The knowledge exists at construction and is discarded; the suffix test reconstructs it by parsing a value pctl itself generated. Per CLAUDE.md 'make bad values unrepresentable', the honest shape is a kind on the type — Unit_filename.kind : t -> [ `Slice | `Service ] recorded at construction, or a variant carried on plan_row — after which apply_row matches on the kind and the string parsing goes away.

Cost is not nothing: Unit_filename is used across 10+ files and is serialised into the manifest table, so the kind has to be derivable on the way back out of SQLite (which it is — the same suffix test, but in ONE place, at the deserialisation boundary, where a parse belongs).

Adjacent but distinct: pctl-ufh (the e2e harness sprintf's the unit-name convention instead of delegating to Schema).

Found while reviewing the pctl-added-restarts-g31 working tree.

title: lifecycle: two concurrent pctl runs on one project race on user.control and the manifest, with no lock anywhere
description:
Nothing serialises two pctl invocations against the same project id. No advisory lock on the state db, no lock file in user.control.

Real today, not hypothetical:
  - `pctl up` racing `pctl down`. Lifecycle.reload's down arm removes every unit file it owns (lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:177-179) while the up arm is writing them (:137 via Write_all). Whichever calls State.Projects.replace_manifest last (:181) wins, and the surviving manifest can disagree with what is actually on disk in either direction: files present that the manifest does not name (never removed by a later down or gc) or names with no file.
  - two concurrent `up`s are mostly benign only because Render is deterministic, so both write identical bytes.

pctl-468's D1 design adds a read of user.control before the write, which is the first time a run's decisions depend on what a *concurrent* run has put on disk: an installed-hash can now be read from a half-written file. It does not create the race, and the two-phase ownership persist agreed there keeps the manifest a superset in both interleavings, so this stays P3 rather than blocking.

No repro run — derived from the absence of any locking call in lib/state/db.ml and lib/unit_store/fs.ml.

Options if it is ever worth fixing: a per-project advisory lock (flock on a file in user.control, or BEGIN IMMEDIATE held across the lifecycle body). The second is simplest but holds a write txn across systemd round trips, which pctl-e0d measures at ~540ms each.

title: lifecycle/gc: down and the gc sweep return before the cgroup cascade has finished stopping anything
description:
Measured 2026-08-04 on this host (systemd 260, 138 unit files) while doing pctl-e0d.

Manager.StopUnit(name, "replace") queues a job and returns the job path. Nothing in pctl waits for that job. lib/gc/gc.ml already documents this exactly ("a successful return means systemd ACCEPTED the stop job, not that the processes are gone") but the down path relies on the opposite in two places:

1. lifecycle.ml down path deletes every unit file immediately after the slice stop, while the cascade may still be killing the services. lifecycle.ml own comment calls that state the one that "must not pass silently" -- processes alive in a cgroup with no units left to manage them -- and reaches it by the accepted-vs-complete gap rather than by a failed stop.
2. `pctl down` exits while the slice is still active, so a caller cannot sequence anything after it.

How it was found: before pctl-e0d, down paid two 540ms Manager.Reloads after the stop, which hid the gap. With one reload the window is ~0-500ms and observable. Journal, slow interleaving:

  Stopping pctl-<id>-web.service...
  Reloading finished in 508 ms.
  Stopped pctl-<id>-web.service.
  Removed slice Slice /pctl/<id>.

`systemctl --user is-active <slice>` immediately after `pctl down` returned "active" in 3 of 8 runs of test/e2e/test_down.ml. It always reached inactive within 500ms, so the stop job is never lost -- this is latency, not a dropped job.

Not a regression from pctl-e0d: the gap predates it and does not depend on the reload count. What changed is that the timing no longer masks it.

Interim: Harness.assert_unit_inactive now polls (harness.ml wait_activeness), matching what assert_unit_active always did. That makes the tests honest about the asynchrony; it does not remove it.

Fix shape (not decided): subscribe to the slice job/state via the same Systemctl subscription Probe uses and wait for inactive before the file removals, bounded by a timeout. Interacts with pctl-67s (down ~quiet swallows failures) and pctl-concurrent-runs-race-xn5.

title: test support: contains_substring is byte-identical in test/unit/test_helpers.ml and test/e2e/harness.ml
description:
test/unit/test_helpers.ml:21-27 (contains_substring) and test/e2e/harness.ml:449-455 (contains) are the same function under two names:

  needle = ""
  || (try ignore (Str.search_forward (Str.regexp_string needle) haystack 0); true
      with Not_found -> false)

Character for character identical apart from the name.

The obstacle is real: test/unit/test_helpers is linked only into test/unit/dune, and there is no support library spanning test/unit, test/integration and test/e2e. So the fix is either a small shared test-support library in the dune tree, or accepting the copy and saying so at both sites.

Worth noting before inventing a library for it: OCaml has no Stdlib substring search, but the two callers may not need Str at all - both are asserting "output mentions X", which String.length + a hand-rolled scan or a dependency the repo already carries could serve.

Pre-existing; neither site was touched by the pctl-e0d diff. Surfaced by that review.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
The rm_rf family is now four copies, and .1's bug fix landed in exactly one of them.

Copies: test/e2e/harness.ml (rec rm_rf), lib/unit_store/fs.ml:61 (rec rm_rf), test/unit/test_helpers.ml (rm_rf), plus Unit_store.Fs's use of it. pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.1 added the chmod-before-walk fix to the harness copy only — a directory left at mode r-x (systemd's $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/inaccessible/) is still undeletable by the other three.

Two more overlaps found in the same sweep, same shape as contains_substring:
  - test/e2e/harness.ml read_file (added by .1) and test/e2e/reexec.ml:67 read_file are two readers in ONE library (e2e_harness, wrapped false); reexec's still uses in_channel_length, which is the bug .1's version exists to avoid.
  - lib/unit_store/fs.ml:88 has_suffix re-implements String.ends_with.

Suggests the fix for this ticket is a shared test-support module rather than pairwise dedup: test/unit/test_helpers.ml is already a dune library and already carries rm_rf, read_file, contains_substring AND a working unsetenv via ctypes-foreign, which e2e_harness does not depend on and therefore hand-rolls around.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
THE OBSTACLE THIS TICKET NAMES IS GONE, and one copy has diverged.

This ticket's premise was that 'test_helpers is linked only into test/unit, and there is no support library spanning both'. pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.1 changed that: test/e2e/dune now lists test_helpers in e2e_harness's libraries (for its libc unsetenv binding). So Harness.contains ≡ Test_helpers.contains_substring is now a one-line delete, not a library-building exercise.

Two things that changed the shape of the remaining work:

1. rm_rf is now three NON-equivalent copies. harness.ml's was rewritten to use Unix.lstat/Unix.unlink plus a chmod before each walk; lib/unit_store/fs.ml:61 and test/unit/test_helpers.ml still use Sys.file_exists/Sys.remove. Consolidating naively onto either of the older two would REGRESS the harness — it would reintroduce the dangling-symlink skip. The correctness half of that is filed separately as pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.11; do that first, then collapse onto the fixed version.

2. read_file is now two copies in ONE link unit. harness.ml's uses In_channel.input_all; test/unit/test_helpers.ml's still uses in_channel_length, which is wrong for procfs (see lib/clock/clock.ml for the recorded reason) and is now linked into every e2e executable even though nothing there calls it.

Whether e2e_harness should depend on a test/unit library at all is worth deciding as part of this ticket rather than inheriting it: a shared test/support/ directory is the alternative, and it is also where the four-way rm_rf consolidation would naturally land.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my 2026-08-05 comment: the obstacle is back.

I wrote 'THE OBSTACLE THIS TICKET NAMES IS GONE ... Harness.contains ≡ Test_helpers.contains_substring is now a one-line delete', because pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.1 had added test_helpers to e2e_harness's libraries. title: pctl issues two Manager.Reload calls per command (~540ms each), four per up+down round trip
description:
Observed while investigating pctl-jbd, from the user journal on this host (systemd 260):

  Jul 30 22:21:24 systemd[20455]: Reloading finished in 542 ms.
  Jul 30 22:21:24 systemd[20455]: Reload requested from client PID 276641 ('test_gc_explici')...
  Jul 30 22:21:24 systemd[20455]: Reloading finished in 551 ms.
  ... four in a row per test binary

Where they come from:
  - lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:122 and :126 — apply_plan frames start/stop with a daemon_reload on each side.
  - lifecycle.ml:176 and :180 — the down path does the same around the file removals.
  - lib/gc/gc.ml:117 and :128 — opportunistic_sweep and purge each add one.

So `pctl up` costs ~2.2s of pure Manager.Reload before any service work, and `pctl up` on a host with a stale registry row adds another. On this machine the user manager's reload is ~540ms because it re-runs systemd-xdg-autostart-generator over the whole autostart dir each time (visible in the same journal window).

The ordering comment at lifecycle.ml:90-102 explains why each reload is where it is, and the reasoning holds — this is not a correctness bug. But the trailing reload of apply_plan and the leading reload of the next command are back-to-back with nothing in between, and gc's sweep reload runs immediately before lifecycle's. Worth checking whether the pairs can collapse.

Note before optimising: measure. 540ms is this host's number, driven by its generator set, not a pctl constant.
close_reason: one Manager.Reload per mutating command instead of two; gc reloads once per sweep, not per removed row

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Correction to this ticket's own arithmetic, caught in review of pctl-jbd.

The body says 'four Manager.Reload calls per up/down' and cites four 'Reload requested' journal lines per test binary. Those four are one up PLUS one down — each e2e binary does both. Per command it is two:

  lifecycle.ml:120-126, apply_plan — one daemon_reload before the row application and one after. Exactly two.
  lifecycle.ml:154 — reload calls apply_plan once on the up path.
  lifecycle.ml:176,:180 — the down path has its own two.
  gc.ml:117,:128 — two more, but only for a project the sweep actually removes.

So: two per up, two per down, plus two per swept project. ~1.1s of reload per command on this host, not ~2.2s. The finding stands, the magnitude halves.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Measured on this host, 2026-08-04, against the ticket's own 'measure before optimising' note.

daemon-reload is 553-615ms flat (mean ~580ms): 6 samples back-to-back, 3 more with a 2s settle between - settling makes no difference. Clearing 39 leaked failed units (463 -> 424 loaded) also made no difference, so the cost is the unit count itself, not tombstones.

Confirms the arithmetic. A ~2.3s floor sits on every e2e test including ones that assert almost nothing (test_up_no_wait 2377ms, test_host 2329ms, test_wait_active 2353ms). 4 x 580ms = 2.32s. Across 24 tests that is ~55s of a 98s suite (three samples: 96.7/95.7/98.1s; dune adds nothing, WALL 96711ms == SUM 96698ms).

Reload scales with loaded units. Two more points:
  minimal NixOS VM, 87 units                        -> 142-156ms
  nested systemd --user, curated SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH  -> 126-141ms
Two-point fit against 424 units/580ms gives roughly 39ms fixed + 1.28ms/unit. Consistent with this ticket's note that systemd-xdg-autostart-generator re-runs over the whole autostart dir each reload.

RE-PRIORITISATION: I briefly promoted this to the top test lever on the strength of ~28s saved. That was against 580ms reloads. Under the nested-manager harness (pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak) reload drops to ~130ms, so halving the count saves ~6s of the suite, not ~28s. No longer the dominant test lever.

Independent value that has nothing to do with tests: the developer's real session carries 424 units, so every hand-run pctl up pays ~2.3s of pure Manager.Reload. That is the reason to do it.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
P1 accepted (manveru: quick fix, makes subsequent work faster). Recording one caveat against 'quick', because this ticket's own text disagrees with it.

The four reloads per up+down are 2 in 'up' and 2 in 'down' — separate processes, so there is no cross-command pair to collapse. The collapse has to happen WITHIN a command, and that is where lifecycle.ml:90-102's ordering comment explains why each reload is where it is: the leading one so systemd sees newly written unit files before start, the trailing one so it forgets removed ones. This ticket says 'worth checking whether the pairs can collapse' — checking, not established.

The one pair that is genuinely back-to-back inside a single process is gc's sweep reload immediately preceding lifecycle's leading reload, and that only occurs when the sweep actually removed something. So the free win may be 1 of 4 rather than 2 of 4, and the rest is correctness-sensitive.

Not an argument against P1 — the daily cost is real and measured. An argument against assuming it is a one-liner.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
MECHANISM CORRECTION to my earlier comment. The 'reload scales with loaded units' model and its 39ms + 1.28ms/unit fit are mis-attributed.

Measured on this host, same session:
  desktop session  214 unit FILES in the search path, 421 units loaded, reload ~580ms
  nested manager     9 unit FILES (curated SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH), 318 units loaded, reload ~130ms

Loaded units differ by 1.3x while reload differs by 4.5x, so loaded count is not the driver. Unit FILES differ by 24x. Re-fit on files: roughly 110ms fixed + 2.2ms/file.

Loaded units include everything systemd synthesises from the running system — .device, .mount, .slice, .scope — which a nested manager still sees because it shares /proc, /sys and the mount namespace. That is why its loaded count stays high while its parse cost collapses. The VM's low count (87) was fewer devices AND fewer files; the two happened to correlate there, which is what misled the original fit.

Consequence for this ticket: unchanged. The per-command reload count is still worth reducing and the daily cost on a 214-file session is still real.

Consequence elsewhere: 'the VM is faster because it is a minimal machine' is wrong. It is faster because it parses fewer unit files, and a curated search path buys the same thing on the host at 254ms of startup instead of a boot. Recorded so the VM is not justified on speed — see docs/adr/0002, which justifies it on hermeticity and on systemd being a locked flake input.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
DECISION on the remaining sweep+lifecycle pair, which the review required before close.

Done: remove_project no longer reloads. opportunistic_sweep and purge each fire one reload after the whole row loop, and none when nothing was removed. So the sweep went from one reload PER REMOVED ROW to one per sweep, and a sweep that removes nothing — the common case, since it only acts on a project whose path has vanished — now costs zero.

NOT done, deliberately: collapsing the sweep's remaining reload into Lifecycle.apply_plan's leading one. They are back-to-back on up/reload/down with only file writes between, so it is a genuine redundancy. Declined because the sweep would have to know which caller triggered it: pctl restart issues zero reloads of its own (measured, below), and pctl gc --yes has no lifecycle work after it at all, so a sweep that skipped its reload on the assumption the caller would pay it would leave systemd holding deleted fragments on exactly those two paths. Cost of leaving it: one extra reload, only when a sweep actually removed a project. Not worth the coupling.

Measured after the change, scripts/measure-reloads.sh, 131 unit files in the search path, bare daemon-reload 531-551ms:
  up (fresh)         594ms  reloads=1
  up (idempotent)    569ms  reloads=1
  reload             566ms  reloads=1
  restart              9ms  reloads=0
  down               597ms  reloads=1
Was 2 per command. The script now runs every mutating command, not just up/up/down.

Side note for pctl-93d, which says 'both gc reloads are swallowed': there is one gc reload now, not two, and it is skipped entirely when the sweep removed nothing. The finding stands; its magnitude halves and its trigger narrows.

Fix: 'the two statements below', or drop the count and say 'before the removals and the reload below'.

test/unit/test_gc.ml:361-364 and :393-395 - second copies of gc.ml. ':361-364 ('one per SWEEP ... since the deletions are the only thing gc changes on disk ... and not one per removed row') restates lib/gc/gc.ml:127-130 ('Nothing between the deletions above and the end of this function talks to systemd, so a per-row reload bought ordering nothing needed') plus gc.ml:162-163. :393-395's 'It runs at the top of every mutating command' restates gc.ml:139-140 ('called at the top of up/reload/down/restart'). gc.ml owns both. Fix: keep the pointer to [Gc.remove_project] / [opportunistic_sweep] and the one sentence these tests add — that the per-row reload must not be restored.

test/unit/test_systemctl_sig.ml:135-136 - '[ops] is the only window onto call ORDER' is a second copy of lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml:256-259 ('so a caller's *sequence* is assertable and not just its end state ... leaves no trace in [inspect]'), which owns it. Fix: keep only what this test contributes — a mutator can forget to record or record the pieces it is built from, and restart_unit is the sole composite.

== Judged and discarded ==

Not findings, recorded so they are not re-raised: test_lifecycle.ml:348's 'worth more than everything else those commands do put together' holds on #59's own table (531-551ms of a 594ms up); the journald-flush race at :83-84 is unverified speculation with no observed miss; $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unquoted-under-set-u at :38 needs it unset, which pctl itself cannot run without; harness.ml:287's LoadState sentence is qualified two lines later by its own 'it also lies about slices'; In_mem's ops staying `string list` was already decided in #60.

== Beads hygiene ==

.beads/issues.jsonl was staged when this review started, and is dirty again after the filings below — re-run `br sync --flush-only` and `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. All 12 code files staged, nothing untracked. pctl-e0d carries its resolution comment (#59) and stays in_progress with no close reason — the user's call after this report. No parent map, so no '## Decisions so far' line to add. Every path, symbol and beads id in the new prose resolves.

== Filed ==

Filed pctl-e2e-write-spec-helper-eaq, pctl-dup-contains-substring-tda; commented on pctl-93d (its cited locations and per-row arithmetic went stale with this diff, and purge's now-only reload is swallowed while purge prints success).

== Verdict ==

Not ready to commit. Blocking: measure-reloads.sh:62's silent zero count; the trap's false alarm before the first up; dbus.ml:558's reload arithmetic. The rest are one-line prose fixes on files already open.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
SHIPPED. Manager.Reload count reduced from 2 per mutating command to 1, and gc's from one per removed row to one per sweep/purge run (zero when nothing was removed).

Production:
- lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml — apply_plan drops its trailing reload, keeping the leading one before any start/stop. The down path drops its leading reload and reloads after the removals instead.
- lib/gc/gc.ml — remove_project no longer reloads; opportunistic_sweep and purge each fire one after their row loop, guarded on having removed something.

Test surface:
- lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml — new [ops] recorder (mutating calls in order, reads excluded, restart recorded as the one wire call it is) plus [reload_count]. Makes call SEQUENCE assertable, which [inspect] never could.
- 5 integration cases pin the count and ordering per lifecycle path (up, idempotent up, reload dropping a service, down, aborted down = zero); 4 gc cases pin per-sweep and per-purge, both directions.
- test/e2e/test_reload.ml gained a real-systemd Removed case: nothing else in the suite reloads a service away.
- Harness.assert_unit_inactive now polls. The old single is-active read only looked deterministic because down used to pay a second ~550ms reload after the stop, which outlasted the cgroup cascade. Root cause filed as pctl-down-returns-before-cascade-qi7.

scripts/measure-reloads.sh — new. Runs up/up/reload/restart/down against the live session and counts each command's OWN reloads by matching the manager's 'Reload requested from client PID <n>' line. This is the artifact that can contradict the ticket's arithmetic.

Measured on this host, 131-138 unit files in the search path, bare daemon-reload 531-615ms:
  up (fresh) 1 · up (idempotent) 1 · reload 1 · restart 0 · down 1
Was 2 per command, so ~550ms saved on every hand-run pctl command on a desktop-sized session.

Declined, with reasoning in comment #59: collapsing the sweep's remaining reload into apply_plan's leading one. It would require the sweep to know its caller, and restart issues no reload of its own while gc --yes has no lifecycle after it.

Three reviewer findings that were real and are fixed rather than argued: the e2e LoadState assertions I first wrote proved nothing (measured — a stopped unit whose file is deleted reads not-found with zero reloads); the reload arithmetic in dbus.ml was wrong twice, the second time because my own gc hoist invalidated the wording I had just restored; and the trap in measure-reloads.sh needed an exit-code gate, not the flag I reached for first.

Gates: dune test, dune build @e2e, e2e-repeat.sh 5 (5/5), nix flake check — all green.

title: e2e harness: teardown leaks one state dir per scratch project, ~8.4M per run
description:
Each reality test gets a unique tmpdir -> unique project id -> unique slice (CLAUDE.md Tests section). That same uniqueness applies to the state dir: a service declaring StateDirectory = "pg" renders to pctl-<project id>-pg, so every run of every such test creates a fresh directory under $XDG_STATE_HOME.

Harness.teardown (test/e2e/harness.ml, run via with_scratch) takes the project down and clears the failed tombstone on its slice. It does not remove the state dir, and `pctl down` cannot do it either (Lifecycle.down clears runtime columns only). The tmpdir goes away; the state dir named after the id derived from that tmpdir stays forever.

Measured on this host (2026-08-02): ten pctl-project_<hash>-pg dirs, ~8.4M each, plus pctl-scratch_tuor_a02abe4c-{pg,server}. So `scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5` costs roughly 42 MB of postgres data dirs that nothing will ever collect.

The harness owns these dirs — it knows the project id it derived — so teardown can remove them by name without waiting on the gc policy question in pctl-gc-state-dir-reclaim-bd1. Suggest teardown enumerate $XDG_STATE_HOME/pctl-<its own id>-* and remove those, and only those: the sandboxing rule is that a test touches nothing outside its own project id.

Note the ten leaked ids are all distinct, so there is no accumulation-in-place to reuse; the count grows linearly with runs.

Depends on nothing in pctl-gc-state-dir-reclaim-bd1 — that one is about user-facing reclaim policy, this one is test hygiene the harness can fix unilaterally. Surfaced while fixing pctl-oik.

title: e2e harness: scratch base can move off /run/user/<uid> now the manager is the test's child
description:
harness.ml's fresh_tmpdir bases scratch dirs at /run/user/<uid> because the session's manager runs outside a nix-shell build sandbox and cannot see its $TMPDIR, so workspace services with BindPaths=<tmpdir> failed 226/NAMESPACE.

That reason is gone: each scratch's manager is now the test's own child and sees exactly what the test sees. The base is free to move to Filename.get_temp_dir_name (), which stops the suite writing into the shared per-uid runtime tmpfs at all.

Left out of pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.1 to keep that diff to the manager itself; the dissolved constraint is recorded in fresh_tmpdir's comment.

Falsifier before claiming it works: test_workspace is the BindPaths test, and dune build @e2e --force must stay green with the base moved. Watch AF_UNIX's 108-byte limit on <base>/<scratch>/run/systemd/private.

title: test/e2e: the three-line 'rewrite spec.json' idiom is copy-pasted at five call sites
bus_errors points at an e2e measurement pinned to a systemd the host no longer runs
description:
pctl-9rt was filed because two blocks pinned different systemd versions 'with nothing reconciling them'. 761669c rewrote one side and made the other side load-bearing, so they still disagree.

lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml:22-33 (new):
    ... Both measured on systemd 260.1 with `dbus-send --session --print-reply`.
    The slice half of that is what test/e2e/test_down_missing_units.ml
    exists for: it holds the observable contract for the one caller that
    stops a SLICE under this tolerance ([Lifecycle]'s down path) ...

test/e2e/test_down_missing_units.ml:14, untouched by 761669c (last touched by 62bb258):
    Measured on this host (systemd 257) while writing this test:

Host today: `systemctl --version` -> `systemd 260 (260.1)`.

So bus_errors now delegates the slice contract to a file whose recorded measurement is three majors stale, and pctl-9rt's close reason ('points at test_down_missing_units.ml for the slice contract instead of restating it') reads as reconciled when only one pin moved.

Per CLAUDE.md 'Verify the case, claim only the case' -- record what was tested and on what version -- the pointed-at recording is the artifact that owns the fact, so it is the one that has to be current.

Fix: re-run the two dbus-send/systemctl probes in that header on 260.1 and re-record, or drop the version pin from the e2e header entirely. The file's own closing sentence already argues the assertions hold on any version ('the test holds either way and fails loudly if some systemd version does answer NoSuchUnit while the tolerance is absent'), so the pin may not be earning its keep at all -- but then bus_errors' pointer needs to say the slice behaviour is asserted there, not measured there.

Filed from the review of 761669c.
close_reason: Re-measured all four probes in that header on 260.1 (the host) and re-recorded: StopUnit on a never-existing .slice returns a job path, on an unloaded .service NoSuchUnit; LoadState loaded vs not-found. Both readings agree with the 257 originals, and the header now says so and says why it must stay current — Bus_errors points at it.

title: e2e harness leaks one -fail.service tombstone per suite run
description:
Measured: clean session -> one full suite run -> exactly 1 leaked tombstone. 39 had accumulated before I cleared them, which is what put systemctl --user is-system-running in 'degraded'.

All 39 were pctl-project_<hash>-fail.service in state not-found/failed - no unit file on disk, but systemd keeps a failed unit loaded until reset-failed.

Cause: Harness.teardown clears the failed tombstone on the SLICE only (it calls reset_failed_unit on pctl-<id>.slice), not on a deliberately-failed service. CLAUDE.md documents the slice behaviour accurately; the service case was never covered.

Not a performance problem - daemon-reload measured 553-615ms both before and after clearing all 39, so the tombstones cost nothing. It is a hygiene and signal problem: a degraded session is a false alarm the developer learns to ignore.

Obsoleted by the nested-manager harness (pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak): a per-test manager dies with the test, taking its tombstones with it. Fix directly only if that epic stalls.

title: state: manifest FK cascade is inert — no PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON
description:
migrations/001_init.sql declares

  project_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

on the `manifest` table, but SQLite enforces foreign keys only when `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is set per connection, and I see no such pragma in State.Db.connect. So the cascade never fires.

Nothing depends on it today: lib/gc/gc.ml:130-133 wipes the manifest manually with replace_manifest ~rows:[] immediately before delete_by_id, which is why the inert constraint has never been noticed.

Found while designing pctl-468. Not fixed there — that work rebuilds the manifest table (migration 004) and carries the same clause across unchanged, so the situation is neither improved nor worsened by it.

Decide: either set the pragma at connect and drop gc's manual wipe, or delete the REFERENCES clause so the schema stops claiming an integrity guarantee it does not provide. A declared-but-unenforced constraint is the worse of the three states.
close_reason: duplicate of pctl-fk-pragma-inert-kcl, which was filed first today with the same two-ways-out framing

title: state/db: the foreign_keys pragma is never enabled, so manifest's ON DELETE CASCADE is inert
description:
migrations/001_init.sql:12-17 declares `manifest.project_id ... REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`. SQLite enforces foreign keys only when `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is set per connection; State.Db.connect does not set it, and no migration does either.

Consequence today: benign. Gc.remove_project already wipes the manifest by hand (lib/gc/gc.ml:130-131) immediately before deleting the project row (:132-133), so nothing depends on the cascade firing. The declaration is decoration that reads as an enforced invariant.

Two ways out, not decided:
  - set the pragma on connect and delete the manual wipe, so the schema statement becomes the single source of truth;
  - drop the REFERENCES clause and keep the manual wipe, so the code is the only claim.

Either is fine; having both, with one of them false, is not.

Found while designing pctl-468 (manifest -> ownership-set). Not blocking it: that work rebuilds the manifest table in migration 004 and can carry whichever clause is chosen.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
FALSIFIED at f7ff155+. The premise is wrong: the pragma IS enabled on every connection.

lib/state/db.ml:64-79 — foreign_keys_on_req is 'PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON'; enable_foreign_keys is called from connect_uri, and connect routes through connect_uri. The module header (db.ml:4-7) states the invariant explicitly. git log -S 'foreign_keys = ON' puts it in 84900b2, the commit that introduced SQLite state — so it has been there the whole time, not added since this ticket was filed.

There is also a passing test that would fail if the claim held: test/integration/test_state.ml test_foreign_keys_cascade inserts two manifest rows, deletes the parent project, and asserts zero remain. With FK off those rows survive and the assertion fails 2 <> 0. It runs green in 'pctl state'.

What survives is smaller and is not a bug: Gc.remove_project's manual manifest wipe (gc.ml, replace_manifest ~rows:[] immediately before delete_by_id) is redundant now that the cascade genuinely fires. The ticket's second 'way out' (drop the REFERENCES clause) is off the table, since the clause is enforced.

Suggest rescoping to a chore: 'gc: remove_project wipes the manifest by hand although the FK cascade already does it'. Priority P3 is right for that.

title: systemctl fakes: In_mem raises op="stop" where Dbus raises op="StopUnit", so integration assertions match a label no real error carries
description:
Pre-existing; surfaced by pctl-8sd's new integration test.

lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml:116 raises Unit_op_failed { op = "stop"; ... }.
lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:529 is `let stop_unit t ~unit:u = call_unit_op t ~op:"StopUnit" ~unit:u`, so the real adapter raises op = "StopUnit".

test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml (test_down_propagates_stop_failure) asserts
`Schema.Pctl_error (Schema.Unit_op_failed { op = "stop"; _ })` — correct against the fake, but it pins a label that never appears in production, so the assertion cannot catch a change in what the real adapter reports, and any code that ever matches on `op` would be tested against the wrong string.

Per CLAUDE.md the fake is a port adapter standing in for the real one; a value it fabricates differently from the real adapter is a recorded-double drift.

Check the other In_mem ops for the same divergence (start/restart/daemon_reload) and align them on the Dbus method names (StartUnit, StopUnit, RestartUnit, Reload). Then update the integration assertion.
close_reason: In_mem.stop_unit raises op=StopUnit, matching Dbus. The other ops raise nothing at all (start_unit sets Failed, restart delegates, daemon_reload is a no-op), so there was no second label to align. fail_next_stop now takes ~error_name ~reply, the pair the real adapter produces, and the integration assertion pins StopUnit.

title: the narrowing this whole batch exists for is guarded by no test at any layer — mutation-confirmed
description:
Mutation test, run at f7ff155 in a throwaway worktree. Reverted lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:719-721 to the pre-pctl-a7p form:

    let get_unit_path_opt t ~unit:u =
      try Some (get_unit_path t ~unit:u) with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> None

That is precisely the bug pctl-a7p, pctl-q2j and pctl-8za were filed about: a bus fault becomes Inactive / 'no job pending', so a running service reports as stopped and a wait ends early.

Results:
  dune test --force        -> exit 0, GREEN. Mutation survives.
  dune build @e2e --force  -> exit 0, GREEN. Mutation survives. (all 7 e2e tests ran,
                              incl. test_reload_survives_reexec, 12 reloads / 2 reexecs)

So the central fix of a seven-ticket batch ships with no regression guard anywhere.

For contrast, mutations that ARE caught:
  is_no_such_unit always true                 -> RED (4 suites: classification, wait_service, purge, primitives)
  In_mem.unit_job_pending arm removed         -> RED (in_mem 11 'read arms are per-read and one-shot')
So the CLASSIFIER and the FAKE are well guarded. Only the adapter that actually talks to systemd is not.

pctl-7yg's close reason discloses the gap — 'Dbus.get_unit_path_opt itself still has no test, as the fake cannot drive the real adapter' — and then the ticket was closed. Disclosure is not a guard, and the fake was the wrong place to look: e2e CAN drive the real adapter and was never asked to.

A lever exists. pctl-jbd established that a daemon-reexec window produces a real peer-gone reply on this host (NoReply / 'Remote peer disconnected', dbus-broker driver_goodbye), and test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml already drives reexec deliberately. A probe or status read issued across that window is the natural place to assert that the failure reaches the caller rather than becoming Inactive.

Fix: an e2e case that reads unit state across a daemon-reexec and asserts the error propagates. If that proves too flaky to gate on, say so IN bus_errors.ml/dbus.ml at the narrowing, so the next reader knows the branch is unguarded by construction rather than by oversight.

P1 because the gap is not in the code under review but in what the batch is allowed to claim: 'green' currently means nothing about the property the batch was for.

Filed from round 2 of the review of 761669c/f7ff155.
close_reason: test/e2e/test_unit_state_survives_reexec.ml drives the real adapter through the daemon-reexec window and asserts two things: no read answers Inactive for a unit that is running, and at least one propagated failure came from GetUnit — the only call get_unit_path_opt classifies. Splitting propagations by op was essential: roughly half land on Properties.Get and prove nothing. The kicker stops on the first GetUnit fault and keeps hunting otherwise, so the median run costs 1-2 reexecs. Measured on 260.1: 20 runs green, all exercising GetUnit; 6/6 RED with the catch-all restored. Statistical per run by construction, so a run that misses prints UNEXERCISED and e2e-repeat.sh exits 3 if no run in a batch hit it.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Round 3 of the review — the uncommitted working tree implementing this ticket plus pctl-m6s/3mi/yt8/7kw. All seven paths staged, nothing untracked, so the flake gate reads what I read. dbus.ml carries no leftover mutation (git diff HEAD on it is empty).

## The guard works, and it can still pass without testing anything

Independently reproduced: with `with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> None` restored, the new test goes RED 2/2 ('observed 3 wrong state(s) … inactive', rc=2). Unmutated, 3/3 green. So the test does what this ticket asked for.

But `raised` is printed, never asserted, and this ticket's wording was 'asserts the error propagates'. A run that never enters the window is green and indistinguishable from one that did.

It is worse than a bare vacuity gap, and this is the finding I would not ship without. Three unmutated runs, first propagation printed each time:

  run 1  systemctl Properties.Get pctl-…-web.service failed: …NoReply
  run 2  systemctl Properties.Get pctl-…-web.service failed: …NoReply
  run 3  systemctl GetUnit        pctl-…-web.service failed: …NoReply

The header (:35-38) already says only the GetUnit read is classified and 'a fault landing on the second propagates either way'. So a Properties.Get propagation exercises nothing this ticket is about — and in 2 of my 3 runs that is what the first propagation was. '4 propagated' can therefore be four irrelevant faults. Fix: count propagations whose op = "GetUnit" separately and key the assertion on that, not on the total.

Coupled to it: :39-40 says 'scripts/e2e-repeat.sh is what turns it into a gate'. It does not. The script (scripts/e2e-repeat.sh:60-66) classifies a run by exit status and `grep -c '^SKIP: '`; a green-but-unexercised run counts as a pass. Either print a distinctively-prefixed line when the GetUnit count is 0 and grep for it there too, or drop the claim.

## In-scope fixes

- test/e2e/test_unit_state_survives_reexec.ml:158-191 — assert on GetUnit propagations, per above.
- :39-40 + scripts/e2e-repeat.sh — the script cannot see a vacuous run; make it, or stop claiming it.
- :49-50 says 'REEXECS THE DEVELOPER'S USER MANAGER, twice'; :55 is reexec_count = 4. Six per suite run, not four. Self-contradiction inside one file.
- The tight spin is load-bearing and nothing says so. Measured ~105,000 reads in ~12s yielding 2–4 faults; the window is that narrow. A reader adding a polite sleep would silently destroy detection while leaving the test green. Say so at the loop.
- lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml:31 — 'the JOB_STOP-specific guard in bus_unit_queue_job_one'. Same misattribution class this batch's pctl-m6s was filed for: the guard is in unit_queue_job_check_and_mangle_type (unit.c:7057, guard at 7077-7079); bus_unit_queue_job_one (dbus-unit.c:1955) only calls it, at :1971. Everything else in the rewritten block is correct — I re-verified manager_load_unit succeeding with load_state=not-found, and ResetFailedUnit's flags=0 → bus_get_unit_by_name.
- lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:719-721 untouched. This ticket's fallback clause fired — 'if that proves too flaky to gate on, say so IN bus_errors.ml/dbus.ml at the narrowing' — and by the author's own header the guard is statistical. One line at the narrowing naming the e2e file and its statistical nature.
- test/unit/test_bus_errors.ml:28-33 — pctl-3mi asked for the deliberate-literal rule 'in the file header, where the next reuse sweep will see it'. It landed inside test_is_no_such_unit. Header is unchanged.
- test/e2e/harness.ml:206-219 — teardown runs the instant the 4th reexec completes, i.e. inside the settling window, and all three of its calls are `try … with _ -> ()`; only daemon_reload retries peer-gone, stop_unit does not. A NoReply there leaves this test's units and slice running on the session with nothing printed. First test to combine a manager reexec with with_scratch. Poll Harness.is_active until the manager answers before returning. (Same window: on a failure path the backgrounded kicker outlives the process and can reexec after exit.)

## Not blocking

:152 admits Schema.Reloading alongside Active with no justification at the site, while the comment below explains only why the other states are wrong.

## Gates run this session

dune test --force → 0 failures. test_unit_state_survives_reexec.exe → 3/3 green unmutated (105705 / 105290 / 102317 reads, 4 confirmed reexecs, 4 propagated each), 2/2 RED with the narrowing reverted. Mutation ran only in a throwaway worktree, since removed. I did not run the full `dune build @e2e` this round; the author reports e2e-repeat.sh 3 → 3/3 and nix flake check green, and I did not re-run those.

## Filed

pctl-4ih — six functions of reexec-kicker machinery now duplicated verbatim between the two e2e tests. Commented on pctl-ra1, whose predicted fifth read_file copy is one of them.

## Verdict

Not ready to commit. The GetUnit-vs-Properties.Get conflation means the headline artifact of this ticket can report success without having exercised the branch, which is the specific failure mode the ticket exists to end. Everything else on the list is small.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Round 4 — the uncommitted tree implementing this ticket plus pctl-m6s/3mi/yt8/7kw/4ih. Eleven paths staged, nothing untracked. dbus.ml carries only the note this ticket asked for; the narrowing is intact.

## The blocking finding is discharged

Propagations are now split by op and the assertion keys on GetUnit. Independently sampled 5 runs: all green, all exercised GetUnit, windows needed 1,2,1,1,1. With your 11 that is 16 runs, none unexercised. The early-stop redesign is also materially cheaper than what I reviewed — 1-2 reexecs typical against the flat 4.

e2e-repeat.sh's exit 3 is sound. I traced it against the skip and fail paths: `exercised` increments for any run without the line, including failed and skipped ones, but both of those exit earlier (1 and 2 respectively), so the counter only decides a batch in which everything passed and nothing skipped. Correct.

## pctl-m6s: the citation is right, and I verified the new historical claim

The comment now says the guard 'moved out of bus_unit_queue_job_one into unit.c between 257 and 260 without changing its test'. No 257 tree exists on this host, so I fetched v257 from upstream:

  v257  src/core/dbus-unit.c:1808  int bus_unit_queue_job_one(
  v257  src/core/dbus-unit.c:1829  if (type == JOB_STOP && UNIT_IS_LOAD_ERROR(u->load_state) && unit_active_state(u) == UNIT_INACTIVE)
  v257  src/core/dbus-unit.c:1830          return sd_bus_error_setf(error, BUS_ERROR_NO_SUCH_UNIT, "Unit %s not loaded.", u->id);
  v257  unit_queue_job_check_and_mangle_type — does not exist

  v260.1 src/core/unit.c:7079  if (t == JOB_STOP && UNIT_IS_LOAD_ERROR(u->load_state) && unit_active_state(u) == UNIT_INACTIVE)
  v260.1 src/core/unit.c:7080          return sd_bus_error_setf(reterr_error, BUS_ERROR_NO_SUCH_UNIT, "Unit %s not loaded.", u->id);

Identical test, moved function, only type→t and error→reterr_error renamed. The claim is exactly right, including 'without changing its test', and the argument for naming functions over line numbers is now itself evidenced. Third revision of this comment and the first one that holds.

## In-scope fixes

- CLAUDE.md:36 and :38 — this diff invalidated TWO claims in the standards file, not one. :36 is the exit-3 gap you named. :38 also says 'test_reload_survives_reexec is the exception to "tests only touch their own slice": it runs systemctl --user daemon-reexec twice against the live session' — there are now two such tests and the new one runs up to 8. Both lines are this diff's job: it is the change that made them false.
- test/e2e/test_unit_state_survives_reexec.ml:149 vs :154 — Reexec.check_completed runs before Reexec.settle, and check_completed raises when the kicker did not finish. That is the cap-fired path, i.e. the run where the manager is most likely still unsettled, so on exactly that path teardown lands inside the window. Swap them, or move settle into a Fun.protect finally.
- :69 max_reexecs = 8 sits exactly on the maximum of your own 11-run sample. Because request_stop ends the kicker on the first GetUnit fault, raising the cap costs nothing on a typical run — mine needed 1,2,1,1,1 — and only lengthens the rare tail run that would otherwise report UNEXERCISED. This is the one parameter here with no tradeoff; 16 is free.
- test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml — Reexec.settle's probe is S.Dbus.daemon_reload, the single call that carries a peer-gone retry budget, so it is the least sensitive probe for 'has the manager come back'. Its own comment calls it 'a bare handle read'; it is neither bare nor a read. A unit_state read on any unit would settle more honestly and costs the session less than an extra Manager.Reload.

## Beads hygiene

The six tickets are OPEN with no assignee, and `br list --status in_progress` returns nothing — the claim step in CLAUDE.md's contract (`br update <id> --claim --actor <name>`) never landed, so 'claimed' is not what the database says. Also .beads/issues.jsonl is currently MM: this round's filing is unstaged on top of your staged copy, so re-stage .beads/ in the same commit as the work.

## Filed

pctl-w53 — harness teardown swallows every failure, so a future reexec test that forgets to settle leaks units silently. Agreed it belongs in the harness rather than in convention; the check_completed/settle ordering above is the live instance and stays in-scope here.

## Gates run this session

dune test --force → 0 failures. test_unit_state_survives_reexec.exe → 5/5 green, all exercising GetUnit. I did not re-run the full e2e suite, e2e-repeat.sh or nix flake check this round; those remain your measurements.

## Verdict

Ready to commit once CLAUDE.md:36 and :38 are updated and the check_completed/settle ordering is swapped. Nothing else on the list blocks.

title: gc: remove_project issues StopUnit on the slice twice, once by name and once as a manifest row
description:
lib/gc/gc.ml remove_project calls stop_or_propagate on the slice by name, then iterates the stored manifest -- which contains the slice, because Lifecycle.Write_all persists it (lifecycle.ml). So the slice gets two Manager.StopUnit calls.

Observed as the op sequence in test/unit/test_gc.ml (the reload-economy test asserts it verbatim, so it is recorded rather than described):

  stop pctl-gone.slice
  stop pctl-gone-web.service
  stop pctl-gone.slice
  daemon-reload

Harmless -- StopUnit on an already-stopping unit is a no-op -- and cheap next to the reload, which is why it was not fixed under pctl-e0d. The by-name stop is the one that cannot be dropped: it is what fires the cgroup cascade when the manifest is empty or stale.

Fix: skip the manifest row whose filename equals the slice, or take the by-name stop out and make the manifest authoritative (which pctl-468 D1 already reshapes the manifest for).

title: gc: nothing ever reclaims a state dir, so StateDirectory data accumulates permanently
description:
Gc.remove_project (lib/gc/gc.ml:93-133) stops the slice + every manifest unit, deletes those unit files from user.control, wipes the manifest and the projects row. It never touches the state dir systemd created from a service's StateDirectory= logical suffix. Neither does `pctl down` (Lifecycle.down, lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:187-191, clears runtime columns only). So `pctl-<project id>-<suffix>` under $XDG_STATE_HOME is write-only: pctl creates the conditions for it and has no path that removes it.

Measured on this host (2026-08-02): 14 such dirs, ~111 MB, against 0 registry rows (`pctl gc --json` -> `[]`, live=0 orphan=0 unknown=0). Ten are ~8.4M postgres data dirs from e2e scratch projects; the largest are pctl-tuor_e96edffc-pg (16M) and pctl-scratch_tuor_a02abe4c-pg (11M).

Design constraint the empty registry exposes: a reclaim that hangs off row removal cannot help here. With no rows, nothing maps any of the 14 dirs back to a project, so all of them are already past rescue. A working sweep has to enumerate $XDG_STATE_HOME/pctl-* by NAME and cross-reference the project id embedded in it against the registry — which is close to the pre-SQLite gc design UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md used to describe (state dirs classified by cross-reference), except the cross-reference target is a registry row rather than a known marker.

Open questions for whoever takes this:
- Is deleting a state dir ever in scope for gc, or is durable service data something pctl should refuse to delete and only report? A postgres data dir is not obviously garbage just because the project row is gone.
- If reclaim is opt-in, what is the surface — `pctl gc --state-dirs`, a separate confirmation, or report-only always?
- Unparseable/foreign `pctl-*` dirs under $XDG_STATE_HOME need a class of their own; the current Unknown means "project path is gone", not "no owner found".

Surfaced while fixing pctl-oik (the UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE gc rewrite). Not fixed there: that ticket was docs-only, and this is a product gap with an undecided policy.

title: lifecycle: an all-Unchanged up still pays a 540ms Manager.Reload it has no work for
description:
Measured 2026-08-04, scripts/measure-reloads.sh on this host (138 unit files):

  up (fresh)         563ms  reloads=1
  up (idempotent)    575ms  reloads=1
  bare daemon-reload ~550ms

So an idempotent `pctl up` -- the most common invocation there is -- is ~550ms of Manager.Reload and ~25ms of everything else, for a diff on which apply_row does nothing at all. Guarding the reload on "some row is actionable" was implemented under pctl-e0d and BACKED OUT before handoff, because it needs an invariant that is currently false.

The invariant it needs: Unchanged implies systemd has already read these bytes. Nothing in the repo records that. pctl-468 is the open bug where it is provably false -- the manifest lives in SQLite under XDG_STATE_HOME and the unit files live on tmpfs under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, so after a reboot every row is Unchanged while user.control is empty. Skipping the reload there would take the post-reboot `pctl up` from "writes the files, starts nothing" to "writes the files, systemd never learns they exist" -- deeper, on a path that is already broken.

Under pctl-468 D1 the diff left side comes from disk, so Unchanged would then mean the bytes on disk match rendered. One gap survives even then: a process that wrote the files and died before its reload leaves disk == rendered with systemd unaware. Whether that window is worth caring about is the decision this ticket carries.

Guard: test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml "idempotent up: one reload, no job" pins the count at 1 and names this ticket, so the pair cannot come back by accident and the zero case is not reached by accident either.

title: probe: a missing probe executable aborts the wait instead of being retried as a failed probe
description:
Pre-existing. Adjacent to this diff because the diff deletes Schema.Probe_exec_failed as dead code — the constructor that named exactly this case.

lib/probe/probe.ml:112-115 states:

  (* Run the probe command ONCE; return true iff exit-0. Any spawn error
   * (executable not found, ...) is treated as false — matches the
   * Nushell 'probe-once' behaviour, which keeps the wait alive long
   * enough for a slow-to-appear readiness flag file to materialise. *)

run_probe_once (lib/probe/probe.ml:120-136) has no try/with. Eio 1.3 declares

  type error = Executable_not_found of string | Child_error of exit_status

in eio/process.mli, and Eio.Process.await returns only exit_status ('Exited | 'Signaled), so Executable_not_found can only reach the caller as a raised Eio.Exn.Io. It therefore escapes run_probe_once and tears down the wait instead of yielding false and retrying.

Fix: wrap the spawn/await in

  try ... with Eio.Exn.Io _ -> false

and decide deliberately whether a permanently-missing executable should still burn the full probe timeout, or fail fast with a distinct error. If the latter, Probe_exec_failed (deleted in the cleanup diff) is the shape to restore.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Review of the pctl-lrc working tree: the code comment that documents the non-existent swallow is still in the tree, and the same diff now adds a plan-doc note asserting the opposite, so the two contradict each other.

lib/probe/probe.ml:112-115:

  (* Run the probe command ONCE; return true iff exit-0. Any spawn error
   * (executable not found, ...) is treated as false — matches the
   * Nushell `probe-once` behaviour, which keeps the wait alive long
   * enough for a slow-to-appear readiness flag file to materialise. *)

run_probe_once (probe.ml:120-136) has no try/with — re-confirmed by reading it. Meanwhile docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md:49-54, added by that diff, states plainly that 'Probe.run_probe_once does not catch the Eio.Exn.Io that a missing probe executable raises'.

Correcting the comment is a one-liner and does not need this ticket's behavioural decision: say that the spawn error currently escapes and that pctl-j9k owns whether it should be retried as false or fail fast. Flagged in the review as an optional in-scope fix.

Separately, probe.ml:123-126 returns false for an empty exec list with the justification 'the Spec loader should have caught this. Defensive'. Whoever restores the error path should confirm the Spec loader actually rejects an empty probe exec; if it does not, that is a second unconstructed error path in the same function.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Comment at lib/probe/probe.ml:112-121 corrected to state the actual behaviour and point here — it previously claimed 'Any spawn error (executable not found, ...) is treated as false', which contradicted both the code and the note added at docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md. Behaviour deliberately unchanged; this issue still owns the fix and the timeout-vs-fail-fast decision.

title: e2e: daemon_reload intermittently fails with 'NoReply: Remote peer disconnected', failing the suite ~1 run in 3
description:
Observed during the review of the pctl-lrc working tree, on the host with a live user session ('systemctl --user is-system-running' -> degraded).

Measured this session:
  - dune build @e2e --force, run 1: exit 1
  - dune build @e2e --force, run 2: exit 0
  - dune build @e2e --force, run 3: exit 0
  - dune exec test/e2e/test_pctl_no_gc.exe, 6 solo runs: 6/6 exit 0

Run 1's failure, in test_pctl_no_gc at its first 'pctl up' (test/e2e/test_pctl_no_gc.ml:15, label up(a)):

  ASSERT up(a) exit=5
  ---- pctl stderr ----
  systemctl Reload - failed: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply: Remote peer disconnected

  Fatal error: exception Alcotest assertion failure

Exit 5 is the Bus_connect_failed / Unit_op_failed bucket (lib/schema/schema.ml:497). It came from Dbus.daemon_reload (lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:543-550) via check_rc.

Sequence-dependent, not test-local: the test passes 6/6 in isolation and failed only in the full suite, immediately after test_gc_explicit's 'pctl gc --yes' ('pctl gc: removed 1' / 'no projects registered' are the last lines before the failure). The suite runs the exes sequentially from one progn in test/e2e/dune:47-81, so this is a back-to-back Manager.Reload from a fresh connection right after the previous process's bus teardown.

'Remote peer disconnected' on a Reload call is the systemd user manager closing the connection while the call is in flight — a transient condition, not a pctl bug in the sense that the reload did not happen. pctl treats it as fatal.

Two things to decide, and they are separable:
  1. Should Dbus.daemon_reload retry a call that fails with NoReply / Remote peer disconnected (reconnecting the bus if needed) rather than surfacing exit 5? That is a product decision about pctl's robustness against a reloading user manager, not just a test fix.
  2. Regardless of (1), the e2e gate is currently ~2/3 reliable, so 'e2e green' is not a meaningful claim from a single run. Worth pinning down before anyone leans on it.

Not attributed to the cleanup diff: nothing in that diff changed the Reload call's semantics (call_method_no_args has the same ctypes signature as the deleted top-level sd_bus_call_method_no_args), and I did not run the suite on 0508423 to compare. Attribution is open.
close_reason: Bus_retry retries peer-gone bus calls across a daemon-reexec; e2e reproducer + e2e-repeat.sh added. Five review rounds, gates green.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted working tree implementing this ticket (bus_retry.ml + dbus.ml daemon_reload retry + test_bus_retry.ml). Report only; nothing edited or staged.

## Correctness

**lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:38 — `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Disconnected` does not belong in the retry list.** The module header at :16-18 justifies the whole list with "Nothing is wrong with pctl's own connection in any of these cases, so the same handle can just ask again." That is exactly false for `Disconnected`, which means the local connection is dead.

Traced in systemd source (local checkout, matching this host's systemd 260):
  - `sd_bus_call` (src/libsystemd/sd-bus/sd-bus.c): `if (!BUS_IS_OPEN(bus->state)) { r = -ENOTCONN; goto fail; }` and `fail: return sd_bus_error_set_errno(error, r);`
  - `errno_to_bus_error` (src/libsystemd/sd-bus/bus-error.c:120-166) has no ENOTCONN arm, so it falls through to `errno_to_bus_error_name_new` -> `System.Error.ENOTCONN`.

So retrying a `Disconnected` burns one pointless 0.25 s sleep, attempt 2 returns `System.Error.ENOTCONN` (not in the list, so the loop correctly stops), and the error the user finally sees degrades from `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Disconnected: Disconnected` to `System.Error.ENOTCONN: ...`. Strictly worse diagnostics in the one case the module says it does not want to retry.

Fix: drop `Disconnected` from `peer_gone_error_names`, and add a line to the header saying it is deliberately excluded because it names our own connection. The other three stay.

**lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:41-45 and test/unit/test_bus_retry.ml:143-145 — the `None` justification is factually wrong.** The comment says "[None] is a transport-level failure: sd-bus left the error struct empty because the message never reached a peer", and the test repeats it. Per the `fail:` path above, sd-bus *always* calls `sd_bus_error_set_errno` there, so a transport failure arrives with `name = Some "System.Error.<ERRNO>"`, not `None`. The branch's answer (do not retry) is right; its stated reason is not, and `System.Error.*` — the actual shape of a transport failure — is named nowhere in the module or its tests.

Fix: correct the comment to say transport failures arrive as `System.Error.*` and are rejected by the exact-match list; describe `None` as the residue (the `assert_return` paths that return an errno without populating the struct). Add `check false (Some "System.Error.ENOTCONN")` to the classification test.

## Standards

**lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:555 and lib/systemctl/dune:14 — the deadline is on a steppable clock, and it is what forced a new library dependency.** `~now:Unix.gettimeofday` is CLOCK_REALTIME. The repo's existing deadline code is monotonic throughout: `lib/probe/probe.ml:75-81` is `let mono_now env = Eio.Time.Mono.now (env#mono_clock :> Eio.Time.Mono.ty Eio.Std.r)`, and probe names every deadline variable `_mono`. This matters more here than usual because the module's entire discriminator is elapsed time (bus_retry.ml:20-28: an instant disconnect vs a 25 s call timeout under the same NoReply name) — an NTP step inside the window silently reclassifies one as the other.

It is also avoidable at zero cost: `Unix.gettimeofday` is the only `Unix` use in all of lib/systemctl, so it alone added `unix` to lib/systemctl/dune. `Eio_unix.sleep` needs nothing new — `eio.unix` was already there. And `Dbus.connect ~sw _env` (dbus.ml:472) already receives the env carrying `mono_clock` and discards it.

Fix: store `env#mono_clock` on `Dbus.t` at `connect`, pass `~now:(fun () -> Eio.Time.Mono.now clock)` / `~sleep:(Eio.Time.Mono.sleep clock)` (or keep `Bus_retry` on `Mtime.t` outright), and revert lib/systemctl/dune to `(libraries schema eio eio.unix ctypes ctypes-foreign)`.

## Silent failure

**lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:559-564 — nothing reports that a retry happened or that the budget was exhausted, and gc turns that into a multi-second silent stall.** A Reload that failed once and a Reload that burned 5 s over 21 attempts raise byte-identical `Unit_op_failed`. On its own that is a diagnostics nit. It stops being one at lib/gc/gc.ml:117 and :128, where both `M.daemon_reload` calls sit inside `ignore_best_effort` (gc.ml:71-73, which catches `Pctl_error`), inside `remove_project`, inside `purge`'s per-row loop. During a peer-gone window `pctl gc --yes` therefore stalls up to 2 x 5 s *per project* and prints nothing at all — previously it failed instantly and silently.

Fix: have `attempt` count itself and append the attempt count and elapsed seconds to `reply` before raising, so the exhausted case is distinguishable in the message gc discards and in the one the user sees. Whether gc's opportunistic reloads should opt out of the retry entirely is a separate call worth making explicitly.

## Ticket completeness

**Decision (2) of this ticket is not addressed by the diff, and the evidence for decision (1) is not in the repo.** This ticket names two separable things and says (2) holds "regardless of (1)": "the e2e gate is currently ~2/3 reliable, so 'e2e green' is not a meaningful claim from a single run. Worth pinning down before anyone leans on it." Nothing under test/e2e/ changed, and there is no repeat-runner.

I measured it this session on this host (`systemctl --user is-system-running` -> degraded, live session):
  - `dune build @all` -> exit 0
  - `dune test` -> exit 0, all suites pass
  - `dune build @e2e --force`, 5 consecutive runs -> exit 0, 0, 0, 0, 0

5/5 against the previously observed ~1-in-3 failure rate is decent evidence but not conclusive on its own (p ~ 0.13 if the old rate still held). The stronger evidence — "4/4 reexecs produced the failure with the retry disabled, 0/4 with it enabled" — exists only as prose in pctl-xxf's body; the scratch harness that produced it is not committed, so nobody can re-run it, and this ticket has no comment recording it. Per CLAUDE.md the reality layer is where real-systemd behaviour gets verified, and no e2e test reproduces the race.

Fix, before closing: record the measurement as a comment here, and either land a committed reproducer (an e2e or scratch test that reexecs the user manager under a concurrent reload) plus a repeat-run target, or split decision (2) into its own ticket so it is not closed by implication.

## Beads hygiene

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is modified but **unstaged** while every code file is staged. `git add .beads/` before committing.
- `br sync --status` -> "In sync", dirty issues 0. Verified after the filings below.
- This ticket has no comments; the resolution comment and the close reason are still owed.

## Filed

Filed pctl-wag; commented on pctl-nir, pctl-xxf.

## Verdict

Not ready to commit. Blocking: drop `Disconnected` from the retry list, fix the two wrong `None`/transport-failure comments, move the deadline to the monotonic clock and drop the `unix` dep, and either record/commit the reproducer or split decision (2). The retry itself is well-shaped and the gates are green.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Root cause, and the measurements behind the fix. Recorded here because the review noted the A/B evidence existed only as prose in another ticket's body.

## Attribution — it was not sequence-dependent on gc

The ticket read the failure as 'a back-to-back Manager.Reload from a fresh connection right after the previous process's bus teardown'. That is not what happened. User journal for the failing run (manager PID 20455, systemd 260, dbus-broker 37):

  Jul 30 22:21:26 Removed slice Slice /pctl/project_c3a2bc21        <- test_gc_explicit ends
  Jul 30 22:21:26 Reexecution requested from client PID 276470 ('switch-to-confi')...
  Jul 30 22:21:26 Reexecuting.
  Jul 30 22:21:27 Reload requested from client PID 276470 ('switch-to-confi')...

A NixOS / home-manager activation ran 'systemctl --user daemon-reexec' at the exact second the suite reached test_pctl_no_gc. The manager drops its bus connection across a reexec; dbus-broker then answers every call in flight to a departing peer with org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply 'Remote peer disconnected' (driver_goodbye, src/bus/driver.c:2579). The manager was answering again ~1 s later.

Falsifying the gc hypothesis directly: test_gc_explicit -> test_pctl_no_gc back to back, 0/20 failed.

So the ~1-in-3 rate was the rebuild cadence, not pctl and not the test order.

## Decision (1): retry — yes, for Reload only

Manager.Reload is idempotent and the peer is back within ~1 s, so re-issuing is the right answer. Landed as lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml + Dbus.daemon_reload.

Two things that took source reading rather than guessing:
  - sd-bus reports a genuine 25 s call timeout under the SAME NoReply name ('Method call timed out', sd-bus.c) and maps both to -ETIMEDOUT (SD_BUS_ERROR_MAP, bus-error.c). Neither name nor errno separates them; only timing does. Hence an elapsed-time budget on a monotonic clock, not an attempt count — a disconnect answers instantly and is retried, a timeout blows the budget on its first failure and propagates.
  - org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Disconnected is excluded: errno_to_bus_error_const produces it only for ECONNRESET/ECONNABORTED/ENETRESET, i.e. OUR socket, not the peer's. Transport failures also arrive named ('System.Error.ENOTCONN' via sd_bus_call's fail: -> sd_bus_error_set_errno), so exact matching rejects them.

A/B on this host, 40 reloads while reexec'ing 4x:
  - retry budget 0.0 (pre-fix behaviour): ok=36 failed=4 — one failure per reexec, verbatim the error in this ticket
  - retry budget 5.0: ok=40 failed=0

## Decision (2): the gate

Committed reproducer: test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml. Kicker runs out of process on purpose — daemon_reload is a synchronous FFI call that holds the Eio domain for its whole ~540 ms, so a sibling fiber could only ever fire between reloads, never inside one. Reloads are issued with no gap so the reexec has nowhere else to land, and the test fails if the kicker did not complete rather than passing vacuously.

Verified red/green as a reproducer, not just as a passing test:
  - budget 0.0: FAIL, '2 of 15 reloads failed across 2 reexecs'
  - budget 5.0: OK, 15 reloads, 2 reexecs, 0 failures

Repeat-run target: scripts/e2e-repeat.sh [runs]. Rationale documented in CLAUDE.md — the suite drives one shared session, so a flake surfaces as an occasional run, not an occasional test, and one green run proves nothing.

Gates this session: dune test green (15 suites); scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 3 -> 3/3; plus 4 earlier single @e2e runs, so 7/7 today. nix flake check -> all checks passed.

## Review findings, all applied

Dropped Disconnected from the retry list; corrected the two comments that described transport failures as arriving unnamed and added System.Error.ENOTCONN / DBus.Error.Failed to the classification test; moved the deadline onto env#mono_clock (matching lib/probe/probe.ml) and reverted the 'unix' dep on lib/systemctl, which existed only for gettimeofday, to 'mtime'; the exhausted case now appends '(gave up after N attempts over X.Xs)' so it is distinguishable from an immediate rejection.

Not folded in, filed instead: pctl-3bt (whether gc's best-effort reloads should opt out of the retry budget), pctl-xxf (every other bus call is still unprotected in the same window), pctl-e0d (four reloads per command at ~540 ms each).

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Second review round, on the working tree that answers the first one. Report only; nothing edited or staged.

Round 1's four blocking items are resolved. `Disconnected` is out of `peer_gone_error_names` with the exclusion explained (bus_retry.ml:53-63); the clock is `Eio.Time.Mono` off `t.mono` and `unix` is gone from lib/systemctl/dune; the exhausted case now carries "gave up after N attempts over Xs"; and decision (2) has a committed reproducer plus `scripts/e2e-repeat.sh`. What follows is new.

## Vacuity

**test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:38-41 — the kicker's `;`-chaining defeats the test's own vacuity guard.**

    Printf.sprintf "( %s; touch %s ) >/dev/null 2>&1 &"

The steps are `;`-separated, so a `systemctl --user daemon-reexec` that fails — no manager, denied, exit 127 — still falls through to `touch marker`, and `>/dev/null 2>&1` throws away why. All three assertions (marker exists, `reloads >= reexec_count`, `failures = []`) are then satisfiable with zero reexecs ever performed, and the test prints "0 failures". This is the reproducer for the bug; a silently-vacuous green is the one outcome it must not have, and it is the outcome the guard was written to prevent.

It does fire correctly on this host — `journalctl --user -b` shows 10 "Reexecuting" entries across the 5 runs I did, exactly 2 per run — so the defect is in the guard, not in the behaviour.

Fix: `set -e` inside the subshell, redirect to a log file rather than /dev/null and quote it in the failure message, or assert the manager actually restarted (compare `systemctl --user show -p InvocationID` before and after).

**scripts/e2e-repeat.sh:16 — a bad run count reports success.** Measured just now:

    $ ./scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 0
    e2e: 0/0 runs passed          # exit 0
    $ ./scripts/e2e-repeat.sh abc
    ./scripts/e2e-repeat.sh: line 28: printf: abc: invalid number
    e2e: 0/0 runs passed          # exit 0

`runs=${1:-5}` is never validated, `seq 1 0` yields nothing, the loop body never runs, `failed_runs` stays empty, and there is no `set -e`. A script whose stated purpose is "Use this before claiming the gate is green" reports green having run nothing. Fix: `[[ $runs =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo "runs must be a positive integer" >&2; exit 2; }`.

## Claims the code does not support

**lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:548 — "pctl reloads four times per [up]" is wrong; it is two.** `apply_plan` (lifecycle.ml:120-126) brackets the row application with exactly two `M.daemon_reload` calls, and `reload` calls `apply_plan` once (lifecycle.ml:154). The other two exist only when `opportunistic_sweep` actually removes a row. Fix: "twice per up, plus two more per project the sweep removes".

**lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:76-78 — the replacement `None` justification is wrong too.** It now reads "[None] is the residue — an rc raised before sd_bus_call was reached, e.g. message construction". Checked against the local systemd checkout: `sd_bus_call_methodv` (src/libsystemd/sd-bus/bus-convenience.c) routes both `sd_bus_message_new_method_call` and `sd_bus_message_appendv` failures to `fail: return sd_bus_error_set_errno(error, r)`, and its argument checks use `bus_assert_return(..., error)`, which populates as well. Message construction is therefore named like everything else.

Fix: say that `None` is effectively unreachable through `sd_bus_call_method` — every `fail:` path names the error — and is kept only so the match is total. That is a stronger statement than the one being replaced, and it is the one the source supports.

**lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:337-338 — the twin of the comment this diff just corrected is still standing, in the function the new code calls.** `format_bus_reply`'s header says "Transport-level failures often leave the struct empty — in that case we fall back to decoding the raw errno". That is the same claim bus_retry.ml:71-78 now correctly refutes, three lines from `attempt`'s call to it. Two comments in one file asserting opposite things about the same struct. Fix: correct it and note the `None, None` arm is near-unreachable. In scope because this diff is what establishes the correct fact.

**test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:14-16 — the header attributes another harness's measurements to this test.** "Measured here before the fix landed, with the retry budget set to 0: 4 reexecs produced 4 failures. With it at 5 s: 40 reloads, 0 failures." Those are the uncommitted scratch-harness numbers recorded in pctl-xxf's body; this test runs `reexec_count = 2`. "Measured here" is precisely the provenance claim CLAUDE.md's evidence rule exists to protect.

Compounding it: the numbers this test *does* produce never reach the terminal. `Printf.printf "test_reload_survives_reexec OK — %d reloads, %d reexecs, 0 failures"` is captured by alcotest into `_build/default/test/e2e/_build/_tests/`, so `dune build @e2e` shows only `[OK]`. Fix: quote this test's own red/green figures in the header, and either drop the printf or surface the counts through an alcotest check message.

## Documentation

**CLAUDE.md:11-17 — Layout does not list `scripts/`.** The diff adds a new top-level directory and documents it under Tests (:32), but Layout still enumerates only bin/, lib/, nix/lib/, migrations/, templates/init/, docs/. Layout is the map this file tells readers to consult. Fix: add a `scripts/` line.

## Gates run this session

    dune build @all            -> exit 0
    dune test                  -> exit 0
    ./scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5  -> e2e: 5/5 runs passed, exit 0
    journalctl --user -b       -> 10 "Reexecuting" across those 5 runs (2 per run)

The 10 reexecs confirm the new e2e test exercises the real race rather than passing by omission on this host, and 5/5 through the repeat script is the first evidence for this gate that a single run could not have given. Note what it does not cover: only Reload is retried, so the reexec at the tail of run N still lands on run N+1's unretried StartUnit / GetUnit (pctl-xxf). That did not bite in 5 runs.

## Beads hygiene

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is staged alongside the code this time. `br sync --status` -> "In sync", dirty issues 0, verified after the filings below.
- pctl-jbd carries the round-1 review and the reexec measurement as comments. Still owed before close: a resolution comment and a close reason of the form `Completed: commit:<sha>`.
- The measurement quoted in test_reload_survives_reexec.ml's header lives only in pctl-xxf's body — see the provenance finding above; a committed artifact would be better than an issue body either way.

## Filed

Filed pctl-93d, pctl-a7p, pctl-26e; commented on pctl-wag.

## Verdict

Not ready to commit. Blocking: the kicker's `;`-chaining and `e2e-repeat.sh`'s unvalidated run count, which between them let both new gate artifacts report green without doing anything; then the three wrong factual claims (four-reloads-per-up, the `None` residue, "measured here") and the two doc fixes. All are small and none touch the retry itself, which is now correct.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Third review round. Report only; nothing edited or staged.

Round 2's six in-scope items are resolved: the kicker runs under `set -e` with its output captured to a log that the failure message quotes, `e2e-repeat.sh` validates its run count, the reload-count claim now reads "twice per [up] … plus two more for each project the gc sweep removes" (matches lifecycle.ml:122,126), the `None` residue comment is corrected, `format_bus_reply`'s twin is corrected, and CLAUDE.md's Layout gained `scripts/`. Round 1's four are still in place.

I also checked the thing that would have been worst: `Alcotest.run ~and_exit:false` does raise on failure. alcotest 1.9.1 `engine/core.ml:431-435`:

    match (test_failures, t.config#and_exit) with
    | 0, true -> exit 0
    | 0, false -> ()
    | _, true -> exit 1
    | _, false -> raise Test_error

and `engine/cli.ml` passes `~catch:and_exit` to `Cmd.eval_value`, so with `and_exit=false` cmdliner does not swallow it. Uncaught → exit 2. The in-file comment at :119-121 is accurate and a failing case still fails the progn. No false green there.

## False green

**scripts/e2e-repeat.sh — reports "N/N runs passed" when every test skipped.** Measured just now:

    $ env -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS ./scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 2
    SKIP: dbus smoke — DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS unset
    SKIP: test_up — DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS unset
    ... (every binary)
    e2e: 2/2 runs passed          # exit 0

`Harness.skip_or_run` (test/e2e/harness.ml:422-427) prints `SKIP:` and `exit 0` whenever `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` is unset or `/run/user/<uid>` is missing, so the progn sees 24 successes and dune reports the alias green. The script's own header says "Use this before claiming the gate is green" — it is the one artifact in this diff whose entire job is to stop an unearned green, and it hands one out for a run that executed no tests.

The skip itself is pre-existing and correct (the Nix sandbox needs it). What is new is a wrapper that presents it as a pass rate.

Fix: gate before the loop — `systemctl --user is-system-running` (or `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` plus `/run/user/$UID`) and `exit 2` if absent; or capture each run's output and refuse to count a run containing `SKIP:`. The second is stricter and also catches a partial skip.

## Claims the code does not support
