title: bus_errors: the GENERIC_UNIT_LOAD citation is wrong — StopUnit never goes through that code path
description:
lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml:22-28 at f7ff155:

    Whether an op can answer it at all depends on whether that op LOADS the
    name first (GENERIC_UNIT_LOAD, src/core/dbus-manager.c): a loading op
    cannot reach the error for a name systemd is willing to synthesise.
    StopUnit loads, ResetFailedUnit does not

Checked against the systemd 260.1 source (nixpkgs#systemd.src, /nix/store/mpbgd46vg338bdmbcpijgflxsar5rlyy-source), which is the version this host runs:

GENERIC_UNIT_LOAD is declared at dbus-manager.c:795, inside the flags enum of method_generic_unit_operation, and is only ever read at dbus-manager.c:822. StopUnit does not call that function at all:

    dbus-manager.c:770  method_stop_unit -> method_start_unit_generic(message, userdata, JOB_STOP, false, reterr_error)

method_start_unit_generic (dbus-manager.c:747) calls manager_load_unit directly. So the sentence attributes StopUnit's behaviour to a flag StopUnit never reaches.

The half about ResetFailedUnit is right for the wrong stated reason — it DOES go through method_generic_unit_operation, but the point is it passes flags=0, and systemd says why in a comment right there:

    dbus-manager.c:897-900
      /* Don't load the unit (because unloaded units can't be in failed state) ... */
      return method_generic_unit_operation(message, userdata, reterr_error,
                                           _UNIT_TYPE_INVALID, bus_unit_method_reset_failed, /* flags= */ 0);

And 'a loading op cannot reach the error' is not the mechanism either: manager_load_unit SUCCEEDS for both a .service and a .slice. The .service gets load_state = UNIT_NOT_FOUND and the error comes later, from the JOB_STOP guard:

    unit.c:7077-7080
      /* Our transaction logic allows units not properly loaded to be stopped. But if already dead
       * let's return clear error to caller. */
      if (t == JOB_STOP && UNIT_IS_LOAD_ERROR(u->load_state) && unit_active_state(u) == UNIT_INACTIVE)
              return sd_bus_error_setf(reterr_error, BUS_ERROR_NO_SUCH_UNIT, "Unit %s not loaded.", u->id);

A synthesised .slice loads to UNIT_LOADED, fails that guard, and gets a job — which is exactly the observed outcome.

The observed OUTCOMES in the comment are all correct; re-measured on this host at 260.1:
  StopUnit  zzz-pctl-review-probe.service -> Error org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit: Unit ... not loaded.
  StopUnit  zzz-pctl-review-probe.slice   -> method return, object path "/org/freedesktop/systemd1/job/34118"
  ResetFailedUnit zzz-...service          -> Error org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit
  ResetFailedUnit zzz-...slice            -> Error org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit
Only the explanation is wrong.

This has now survived three passes over this comment (pctl-9rt filed it, 761669c rewrote it, f7ff155 rewrote it again) because every pass checked the measurements and none checked the citation. It is also in pctl-9rt's close reason ('because it does not load the name (GENERIC_UNIT_LOAD, dbus-manager.c)').

Fix: cite method_generic_unit_operation + flags=0 for ResetFailedUnit, and the unit.c:7079 JOB_STOP/load-error/inactive guard for StopUnit. Or drop the mechanism entirely and keep only the per-op outcome plus the pointer at test_down_missing_units.ml — the outcomes are what callers depend on and they are recorded.

Filed from round 2 of the review of 761669c/f7ff155.
close_reason: Wrong as filed, and my checkout was v257-3332 while the host runs 260.1 — read v260.1 for the fix. StopUnit reaches the reply through the JOB_STOP guard in unit_queue_job_check_and_mangle_type (load error AND inactive), not through GENERIC_UNIT_LOAD, which method_start_unit_generic never uses. ResetFailedUnit is the one that genuinely does not load. Comment names functions only, and records that the guard moved out of bus_unit_queue_job_one between 257 and 260 with its test unchanged — which is why line numbers do not belong there.

title: e2e runs against a nested systemd --user the test owns
description:
Reality tests run against the developer's live session. Measured: suite is 98s (three samples: 96.7/95.7/98.1), of which ~55s is Manager.Reload at 553-615ms x4 per test; dune adds nothing (WALL 96711ms == SUM 96698ms). Every run leaks one pctl-<id>-fail.service tombstone (39 had accumulated; session was 'degraded'). Two tests daemon-reexec the developer's desktop, one up to max_reexecs (observed 1,1,2,1,3,2,6,1 across 8 runs).

Fix: each test spawns its own systemd --user. Measured on this host: reachable in 254ms, reload ~130ms with a curated SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH, starts real services (cgroup delegation works, nests under the caller's scope).

See docs/adr/0001 and docs/adr/0002. Full spec was /tmp/pctl-nested-manager-harness-spec.md (ephemeral).

Seams: Harness (setup_with/teardown) is the single seam - no test file changes. Reexec is a second, smaller seam (2 tests). The e2e dune alias is the third touch point.

title: harness: spawn a private systemd --user per scratch
description:
Scratch gains a runtime/config/data/unit-path dir and a manager handle. setup_with populates them, spawns the manager, blocks until it answers a trivial D-Bus property read.

Unit_store.Fs already reads XDG_RUNTIME_DIR at handle creation, so redirecting that variable moves user.control into the scratch with no Unit_store change. The harness already putenv/restores XDG_STATE_HOME; the new vars follow the same discipline, which also means the systemctl subprocess helpers inherit them.

SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH = <scratch user.control>:<curated dir>, curated dir symlinking dbus.socket, dbus.service, basic.target, default.target, sockets.target, paths.target, timers.target, shutdown.target, exit.target from /etc/systemd/user.

MUST NOT use the trailing-colon form - it appends the default search path, restoring the 424-unit reload cost and re-coupling tests.
Omitting dbus.socket fails silently in a specific way: manager starts, no bus socket, every systemctl --user reports 'Connection refused'. Verified.

Measured target: 254ms startup, ~130ms reload.
close_reason: Each scratch spawns a private systemd --user on a curated unit path; teardown reaps it. dune test 0, e2e-repeat.sh 5/5.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Two measured facts for whoever implements this.

1. The curated search path is what buys the reload win, not machine minimality. Session: 214 unit files across its search path, reload ~580ms. Nested with 9 symlinked files: ~130ms. Loaded-unit count barely moves (421 -> 318) because a nested manager still synthesises .device/.mount/.slice/.scope from the host's /proc, /sys and mount namespace. Do not expect list-units to look small; expect the parse cost to be small.

2. SIGTERM does not reliably stop a nested manager. Two of my probe managers survived 'timeout --signal=TERM' and were still running with their scratch dirs already deleted and their buses unreachable. Teardown must not assume a polite signal works — reinforces the PR_SET_PDEATHSIG requirement in .2, and means teardown should verify the process is gone rather than fire-and-forget.

3. A constraint that DISSOLVES: harness.ml's fresh_tmpdir bases scratch dirs at /run/user/<uid> rather than $TMPDIR because the session's manager runs outside a nix-shell build sandbox and cannot see $TMPDIR, so workspace services with BindPaths=<tmpdir> failed 226/NAMESPACE. A nested manager is the test's own child and sees whatever the test sees, so the base is free to move. Worth doing — it is the reason tests currently write into the shared runtime dir at all.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my previous comment's point 2, with the mechanism.

I wrote 'SIGTERM does not reliably stop a nested manager'. Wrong diagnosis. systemd --user responds to SIGTERM by starting exit.target, and /etc/systemd/user/exit.target declares:

    Requires=systemd-exit.service
    After=systemd-exit.service

My curated set omitted systemd-exit.service, so SIGTERM started a target whose requirement did not exist, the job failed, and the manager stayed up. Four probe managers survived both 'timeout --signal=TERM' and a plain kill; they needed SIGKILL.

So the graceful shutdown path works — I disabled it by omission.

CURATED SET IS TEN UNITS, NOT NINE:
    dbus.socket dbus.service basic.target default.target sockets.target
    paths.target timers.target shutdown.target exit.target systemd-exit.service

Two consequences for the implementation:
  - Verify shutdown works as part of the harness, not just startup. A manager that starts but cannot be asked to stop passes every startup check.
  - PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (.2) is still required, as a backstop for the kill path rather than as the primary mechanism. Teardown should ask politely first, then confirm the process is gone.

General lesson worth carrying: curating the unit path removes capabilities as well as parse cost, and it does so silently. Anything the manager itself needs — shutdown being the obvious one — is a unit in that path.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
MEASUREMENT TRAP when verifying the curated search path.

'systemd-analyze --user unit-paths' does NOT ask the running manager. It recomputes the default search path in its own process from its own environment. Against a nested manager it silently reports the DEFAULT 46-entry path, not the two directories the manager was actually started with — I hit this and briefly concluded the curation had failed.

To see what a nested manager actually loaded, ask the manager over its bus:
    XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<scratch>/run systemctl --user show -p UnitPath
    XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<scratch>/run systemctl --user list-units --all

Related trap on the same measurement: list-units --all against a nested manager still reports a few hundred units even with ~10 unit files, because .device/.mount/.slice/.scope are synthesised from the host's /proc, /sys and mount namespace, which the manager shares. Session 421 loaded / 214 files; nested 318 loaded / 9 files. The count that predicts reload cost is FILES. An acceptance check written against list-units will look like the curation did nothing.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
## Review of the uncommitted working tree

Gates run this session: `dune test` → 0. `dune build @e2e --force` → 0, 39.5s wall (map records 98s). `scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5` → exit 0, 5/5 passed, no UNEXERCISED batch.

### Correctness / silent failures

- harness.ml sibling_scratch — `env_prev = []` plus a borrowed `manager` makes a scratch that destroys its owner: `teardown b` reaps A's manager and restores A's saved environment while A is live. Only the comment above prevents it. Fix: `manager : Owned of manager | Borrowed of manager`, `release` rejects Borrowed. (Three of five reviewers found this independently.)
- harness.ml await_manager — `| e -> Some (Printexc.to_string e)` retries every exception for 15s, and the loop never checks whether the manager already died. A bad sh_bin/systemd_bin, or a manager that exits at once, costs 15s per test and reads as 'slow', not 'never started'. Fix: `Unix.waitpid [WNOHANG]` in the loop, fail immediately with the exit status; narrow the catch to Unix_error/Pctl_error.
- harness.ml spawn_manager — the curated units are symlinked with `Unix.symlink` and no existence check, so a unit missing from /etc/systemd/user yields a dangling link and exactly the silent capability loss the comment above it documents. Fix: `Sys.file_exists` the target, `Alcotest.failf` naming the unit.
- harness.ml rm_cgroup — `try Unix.rmdir dir with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()` swallows EBUSY, the one errno that means processes are still in the cgroup, i.e. the leak reap_manager exists to detect. Fix: tolerate ENOENT, report anything else with the dir and cgroup.procs.
- harness.ml reap_manager — the SIGTERM `kill` swallows EPERM as well as ESRCH (recycled pid → waitpid ECHILD → teardown reports success while the manager runs on), and the cgroup.kill `openfile` swallows ENOENT/EACCES so the escalation can silently not happen.
- harness.ml reap_manager — 'HARNESS LEAK' is eprintf-only, so a manager surviving both SIGTERM and cgroup.kill leaves the suite green. The eprintf-not-raise choice is correctly justified for a Fun.protect finaliser; a module-level flag plus at_exit satisfies both.
- harness.ml spawn_manager — no cleanup on partial failure. setup_with's new comment covers everything PAST spawn_manager, but a raise between `Unix.mkdir cgroup` and the return leaks the cgroup and the tmpdir.
- harness.ml release — restores absent vars with `putenv k \"\"`. The comment says OCaml's Unix has no unsetenv; true of the stdlib, false of this repo — test/unit/test_helpers.ml:42-49 provides one via ctypes-foreign and documents that `putenv \"\"` is NOT equivalent for Sys.getenv_opt. (Unit_store.Fs does treat `Some \"\"` as unset, fs.ml:19, so that half of the comment holds.)

### Reuse

- harness.ml read_file — 16 lines of Buffer/input reimplement `In_channel.input_all`, and lib/clock/clock.ml:8-11 already does exactly this with the same procfs rationale, which means the comment is a second copy of a fact clock.ml owns. Fix: `In_channel.with_open_bin path In_channel.input_all`.
- test/e2e/reexec.ml:67 — a SECOND read_file in the same library (e2e_harness, wrapped false), still using in_channel_length, which is the bug the new one exists to avoid. Also unconverted: harness.ml's with_captured_fd reader and test/e2e/test_host.ml.
- harness.ml mkdir_p_exn duplicates Unit_store.Fs.mkdir_p (lib/unit_store/fs.ml:41, same 0o700, additionally EEXIST-tolerant); unit_store is already in e2e_harness's libraries.
- harness.ml poll_until duplicates wait_activeness's deadline loop line for line; inside it `ignore (Unix.select [] [] [] 0.01)` re-implements Unix.sleepf, already used in reexec.ml.
- harness.ml builds `<runtime>/systemd/user.control` inline twice — that layout is Unit_store.Fs.xdg_user_control's, and the harness's own comment elsewhere claims it never duplicates it.
- harness.ml user_manager_cgroup's `ends_at` hand-rolls a substring scan; `str` is linked and this same file's `contains` already uses Str.search_forward.

### Prose

- harness.ml curated_units — the hard numbers are unowned and already drifted. The comment says the session manager 'carries 99'; I counted 97 unique unit-file basenames on its UnitPath today, and comment 51 above recorded 214 for the same host and the same reload time. scripts/measure-reloads.sh is the artifact that should hold reload figures.
- harness.ml curated_wants — 'its WantedBy= lives in an [Install] section that only ever produced /etc/systemd/user/sockets.target.wants/' is false: /etc/systemd/user/dbus.socket has no [Install] section at all. The wants symlink is generated by the NixOS module. The conclusion (the path alone is insufficient) is right; the mechanism is wrong.
- harness.ml curated_units — 'the leak PR_SET_PDEATHSIG exists to backstop' is present tense for a mechanism that does not exist: grep finds PDEATHSIG only in that comment and docs/adr/0001:59. .2 is open.
- harness.ml teardown — 'keeps leftovers from bleeding into the next test on the same session' is now false; release reaps the manager, and its death is what removes its units. This is .3's rationale to delete.
- Diff-narrative tense will read as stale the moment it lands: test/e2e/dune 'Each test now owns', harness.ml 'It no longer has to be: the reason was', reexec.ml and test_worktree.ml likewise. State what is true, cite the bead for what is deferred.
- Opening sentences that restate the signature above them: rm_cgroup, await_manager, release, sibling_scratch. The sentences AFTER each one (journald attribution, 'too small to boot', the no-unsetenv note, never-teardown) are the parts that earn their place.

### Intent

Nothing missing from this ticket's own spec, and the two Verify-shutdown consequences from comment 52 both landed. Three boundary crossings are recorded on the tickets that own them: .3 (chmod shipped here, tombstone dance did not), .4 (four new preconditions), .5 (the retirement prose landed while both mechanisms stand), .6 (the kicker retarget shipped here — and its falsifier's NoReply half is now OBSERVED, see my comment there).

Filed: pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.10. Commented on .3, .4, .5, .6, pctl-w53, pctl-dup-contains-substring-tda.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
## Review round 2

Gates reproduced independently this session: `dune test` 0; `scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5` exit 0, 5/5; `nix flake check` all checks passed. All eight round-1 correctness fixes and all six reuse fixes verified present and calling what they claim. Two round-1 prose fixes did not fully land, and the new leak-reporting machinery has a defect that defeats its own purpose.

### Correctness

- harness.ml:67-77 — **the at_exit leak-failure destroys the failure it fires alongside.** `do_at_exit` runs BEFORE the runtime prints `Fatal error: exception`, and `Unix._exit 1` never returns, so the exception message, the backtrace, and every earlier-registered at_exit handler are skipped. 23 of the ~25 e2e tests report failures as uncaught exceptions (no `Alcotest.run`), and leaks are recorded in the same teardown that runs on failure — so a failing test that also leaks prints only 'HARNESS: failing the run on 1 leak(s) above' and exits 1 instead of 2. Probed on OCaml 5.4.1: a program registering an at_exit that calls `Unix._exit 1` and then raising `Failure` printed the handler's line, exit 1, and nothing else. This is the masking report_leak was built to avoid, reintroduced one level up. Fix: print and record at exit, but `exit 1` only when the body returned normally — e.g. have skip_or_run wrap the body, re-raise, and check `!leaks` after a normal return.
- harness.ml:769 — `Systemctl.Dbus.connect` is the ONE call in teardown not wrapped in a catch (it raises Bus_connect_failed, lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:504). A manager that died mid-test — the failure this harness exists to detect — makes teardown raise before `release s`, so the cgroup and tmpdir leak with no report_leak, and Fun.protect turns it into Finally_raised over the test's real failure. Fix: `Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> release s)` around the Eio_main.run.
- harness.ml:125-126 — rm_rf matches only ENOENT from `Unix.lstat`; any other Unix_error escapes release, out of teardown, from a finaliser. Same class as above. Fix: report_leak it.
- harness.ml:554 — the SIGTERM-ignored banner is Printf.eprintf, not report_leak, so a manager whose 'shutdown path is broken' leaves a green run whenever cgroup.kill then succeeds. That is exactly what comment 52 above asked the harness to catch ('A manager that starts but cannot be asked to stop passes every startup check').
- harness.ml:464-471 vs 538-552 — `manager_died` REAPS with waitpid WNOHANG. On await_manager's failure path (failf -> setup_with's handler -> release -> reap_manager) the SIGTERM therefore goes to a pid we no longer own: ESRCH is silently tolerated, but a recycled pid means either an EPERM reported as a leak or a signal to an unrelated process, and `is not our child (already reaped)` is the harness's own earlier waitpid presented as a diagnosis. Fix: cache the status on `manager` and skip signalling when it is already Some.
- harness.ml:626-631 — release's Borrowed refusal raises from what is normally a Fun.protect finaliser, masking the body's real failure for the same reason the file gives for report_leak not raising. It also relocates the runtime error rather than deleting it, against 'Strengthen a type only when it deletes a runtime error'. The shape that deletes it: leave `scratch` ownership-free and put env_prev in a separate `owned` wrapper that setup/teardown take, so `teardown sibling` fails to COMPILE.
- harness.ml:588, 616-622 + test/e2e/dune:21-24 — **env_prev/restore_env is inert**, and it is the sole reason test_helpers (from test/unit/) and ctypes-foreign are now in the e2e link. Nothing reads those variables after teardown; the process exits. Provable from the current tree: test_worktree releases FIFO, so `release b` restores a's values and leaves the env pointing at a's reaped manager and deleted tmpdir — with no consequence. My round-1 finding was correct that `putenv k \"\"` is not unset, and the fix does fix that; I should have asked whether the mechanism does anything first. Recommendation: delete the field, restore_env, and the dune dep. If it stays, the per-scratch snapshot is wrong under nesting — restore LIFO, or snapshot the session env once at module init.
- harness.ml:27 — **poll_until's extraction silently changed an interval.** `wait_activeness` slept 0.1s at HEAD; poll_until hardcodes 0.01s, and its main caller forks `sh -c systemctl --user is-active` per iteration, so every activeness wait in every test now does 10x the fork+exec. One constant cannot serve both a waitpid caller and a subprocess caller. Fix: `?(interval_s = 0.1)`, with gone_within passing 0.01.

### Prose

- harness.ml:252 — 'nothing in the units above references it' is false: /etc/systemd/user/dbus.service (which IS in curated_units) has `Requires=dbus.socket`, `After=dbus.socket` and `Sockets=dbus.socket`. The true claim is about the boot transaction, not references.
- harness.ml:114-117 — 'A manager killed rather than asked to stop leaves dangling invocation:<unit> links' has the cause wrong. Those links are ALWAYS dangling: systemd stores the invocation id AS the symlink target, not a path. Verified on the live session: `invocation:app-blueman@autostart.service -> 90f433db02ca491e856b35a22a942e43`. So Sys.file_exists is false for every one of them by construction; a kill only matters because a graceful exit removes the directory. The lstat fix is right, the recorded reason is not.
- harness.ml:19-20 — 'a CLOCK_REALTIME step only ever makes one give up early' is false for a backward step, which pushes the deadline out of reach and makes the wait exceed its bound — the direction that matters for gone_within, which is reporting a leak. mtime.clock.os is already in e2e_harness's libraries.
- harness.ml:112 — 'measured against systemd 260.1' is a version pin, which claims the behaviour churns; ADR 0002 already routes systemd-version drift to the VM's lockfile.
- Second copies: the systemd-analyze measurement trap (harness.ml:216-219) reproduces comment 53 above whole — the bead owns it; the trailing-colon SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH constraint sits in harness.ml:234, ADR 0001 and this ticket's description, and should live on the `"SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH=%s:%s"` line at harness.ml:376 that it constrains; the unsetenv rationale is in test_helpers.ml:39-44 (owner, at the binding), harness.ml:611-615 and dune:21-24.
- Diff narrative survives in three places: test_worktree.ml:11 'no longer proves what it was written to prove', reexec.ml:21 'now that', harness.ml:753 'redundant now that'.
- Signature restatements remain at await_manager:473 and reap_manager:535 ('Only ESRCH is tolerated on the signal itself').
- harness.ml:5 'each scratch owns a `systemd --user`' — a Borrowed scratch does not.
- Terminology, hard breach: UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:131 — '**Host** always means the allocated loopback address; for the machine, use "host system" or "dev host"'. harness.ml:213, 253 and 275 use 'the host's', 'on this host'. (Not the .8 glossary item.)

### Reuse

- test/e2e/test_host.ml:20-32 — the diff swapped read_file into a hand-rolled temp_file + dup/dup2 stderr capture that is `Harness.with_captured_stderr` (harness.ml:874) verbatim. Having touched those lines, use the helper.
- harness.ml:505-524 — await_manager hand-rolls the deadline loop poll_until now provides, and mixes a Unix.gettimeofday deadline with an Eio.Time.Mono sleep in one loop; reexec.ml in the same library already does this monotonically via Mtime_clock.

### Lower

- harness.ml:453-456 — the rm_cgroup unwind fires even when `Unix.mkdir cgroup` itself failed EEXIST, so a stale same-named cgroup's EBUSY would be reported as this run's leak. Enter the unwind scope only after mkdir succeeds.
- harness.ml:128 — rm_rf chmods every directory it walks though the lstat it just did carries st_perm; the comment justifies it for one directory.
- test_worktree.ml:29-30 — two independent managers boot strictly in series inside one executable, which .5 does not cover.
- harness.ml:487-524 — await_manager rebuilds a whole sd-bus connection every 10ms poll; once connect succeeds the handle stays valid. Structural; magnitude needs measurement.

Filed pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.11 (Fs.rm_rf has the same dangling-symlink bug in production). Commented on .3 and pctl-dup-contains-substring-tda.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
## Review round 3

Gates reproduced independently: `dune test` 0; `scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5` exit 0, 5/5; `nix flake check` all checks passed.

All eight round-2 correctness fixes verified present and correct, including the two I was most worried about: `exit_on_leaks` from skip_or_run (every e2e test does route through skip_or_run — checked all 25), and the `owned` wrapper (`teardown` on a sibling is a type error). `Dbus.close` is `closed`-guarded and `connect` installs no switch release hook, so await_manager's single reused handle cannot double-unref. `poll_until` cannot spin: `f` runs before the deadline test, so a zero or negative `remaining ()` yields one attempt then give_up. All round-2 prose findings verified fixed, not reworded.

### One thing the diff asserts that is not true

**test_reload_survives_reexec still daemon-reexecs the developer's session manager.** test/e2e/reexec.ml's header now says the kicker 'reexecs whichever manager the calling test has [Harness.activate]d — its own scratch's' and that 'an attempt disturbs nobody outside the scratch'; test/e2e/dune says 'these daemon-reexec their own scratch's manager. Nothing outside that scratch is disturbed, so the ordering protects nothing'. That holds for test_unit_state_survives_reexec (with_scratch at :99). It does not hold for test_reload_survives_reexec, which never calls setup or with_scratch: it goes from skip_or_run straight to Alcotest.run and `S.Dbus.connect ~sw env` on the ambient bus (:50, :82-86). Nothing activates a scratch, so the kicker inherits the session environment and reexecs the dev's session manager twice per run — ten times per e2e-repeat 5 batch.

Three consequences:
- CLAUDE.md:37 ('both run systemctl --user daemon-reexec against the live session ... must be last in the e2e alias') is still an ACCURATE description of the tree. It is the diff's two comments that are the false copy, not CLAUDE.md — do not 'fix' CLAUDE.md to match them.
- The dune ordering is still load-bearing, so .5 must not retire it on this premise. Recorded there.
- This epic's motivation 'Two tests daemon-reexec the developer's desktop' is half addressed. Giving that test a scratch is .6's work (its own notes already assume a nested manager); correcting the prose is this diff's. Recorded on .6, along with a correction to my earlier claim there that .1 had retargeted both.

### Correctness

- test/e2e/test_worktree.ml:29-30 — two `setup` calls before the Fun.protect arms, so if the SECOND raises, the first scratch's manager, its cgroup under user@<uid>.service and its tmpdir all leak, and since nothing calls report_leak for them exit_on_leaks cannot fail the run. Pre-diff this leaked only a tmpdir. Fix: nest the second setup inside the first's Fun.protect.
- harness.ml:648 — `ignore (Unix.write_substring fd \"1\" 0 1)` is unguarded. A Unix_error there escapes reap_manager, so `release` never reaches `rm_rf s.tmp` or its existence check (silent scratch leak), and because teardown calls release from a Fun.protect finaliser it becomes Finally_raised over the test's real failure — the masking class this round otherwise closed. Fix: catch it into report_leak, and structure release so rm_rf runs regardless.
- harness.ml:623 — the ESRCH swallow's justification is stale given the new guard at :630. Once `manager_died m = None` has confirmed an unreaped child, kill cannot legitimately return ESRCH (a zombie still accepts signals). Reaching it means the harness lost track of the pid, and it then exits silently: waitpid gives ECHILD, gone_within returns true, no leak recorded. Fix: report_leak on ESRCH too.
- test/e2e/test_dbus_smoke.ml:54 — `Alcotest.run` with the default `~and_exit:true` exits inside skip_or_run's body, so exit_on_leaks never runs. Harmless today (that test owns no scratch), but it means 'green must not be reachable with a leak outstanding' is not enforced for that shape. test_reload_survives_reexec already passes `~and_exit:false`; do the same here.
- harness.ml:147-149 vs :153-154 — 'Per-entry failures are not reported here' is contradicted six lines below, where a non-ENOENT lstat DOES report_leak and fail the run. Fix: state the split — stat failures fail the run, chmod/readdir/unlink/rmdir are left to release's aggregate check.
- harness.ml:150 + test_gc.ml:16,26 / test_list.ml:20 / test_pctl_no_gc.ml:18,28 — the aggregate check that justifies rm_rf's swallows lives in `release`, but these four call rm_rf directly and have no such check, so every per-entry failure there is unreported. Fix: move the post-check into rm_rf.
- harness.ml:33 — `?(interval_s = 0.1)` is a default that two of three call sites override. Global CLAUDE.md: 'Treat every value as required ... A fallback needs justification ... surfaced as a decision, not slipped in.' Fix: make it required and have wait_activeness pass 0.1 explicitly.

### Prose

- harness.ml:287-291 — the `status` comment's counterfactual is false. It says reading ECHILD 'would otherwise send [reap_manager]'s SIGTERM at a pid we no longer own', but :512-513 maps ECHILD to a Some and :630 signals only when manager_died returns None, so ECHILD cannot reach signal by either path. What the cache actually buys is a real exit status instead of the 'was reaped by someone other than the harness' fallback.
- harness.ml:25-27 — the monotonicity why is lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml's (cite it, don't restate the mechanism), and the second clause is wrong: 'the callers that time out are the ones reporting a leak' is false for the dominant callers wait_active/wait_inactive, which time out into assertions.
- test/e2e/reexec.ml:113-115 — request_stop still says 'so the developer's manager is not reexec'd more times than the evidence needs', which the header 20 lines above now contradicts. Ironically it is currently TRUE for test_reload_survives_reexec and false for the other caller; say which.
- test/e2e/dune:89-92 — 'Nothing outside that scratch is disturbed' repeats reexec.ml's header (owner) as well as being false. Reduce to a pointer.

### Reuse

- test/e2e/reexec.ml:196-213 — `settle` hand-rolls poll_until exactly (monotonic counter, predicate, fixed sleep, timeout) plus the `last`-error idiom await_manager just adopted, and Harness.poll_until is reachable from this module (it already calls Harness.read_file). Its bare 15.0 also duplicates manager_ready_timeout_s. `poll_until_finished` is correctly NOT a candidate — its header forbids a sleep in the loop.
- `Mtime.Span.to_float_ns (Mtime_clock.count c) /. 1e9` now appears four times: harness.ml:36, harness.ml:539, reexec.ml:159, reexec.ml:199. Fix: one `elapsed_s`.
- harness.ml:515 vs :618 — `manager_ready_poll_s = 0.01` is named, reap_manager passes a bare 0.01. One constant or neither.

### Lower

- harness.ml:672 — `owned` deletes the accidental error, which is what it was for, but with `(wrapped false)` and no .mli `Harness.{ owned_scratch = sibling }` still typechecks, so the comment's 'does not typecheck' is true of `teardown sibling` and not of a forged wrapper. A small `module Owned : sig type t val mint : scratch -> t val scratch : t -> scratch end` closes it without an .mli for the whole module.
- harness.ml:558-566 — `record` narrows to Pctl_error | Unix_error; any other exception from connect escapes with the handle unclosed, reclaimed only by Gc.finalise.
- harness.ml:94 — 'leak(s) above' is wrong under Alcotest.run, which captures a case's stderr into _build (as test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:38-41 documents). Re-print `!leaks` instead of pointing at them.
- harness.ml:574-600 — the poll-then-give_up shape appears twice verbatim with three closures existing only to be wrapped; one local `phase` helper called twice would drop two of them. Style, not a defect.

Filed pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.12 (setup couples spawn and await, so tests needing two managers boot in series — plus the test_worktree leak above). Commented on .5, .6, and corrected my earlier comment on pctl-dup-contains-substring-tda: round 3 deleted the test_helpers dep, so that ticket's original obstacle is back and my 'now a one-line delete' note there was wrong.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
## Review round 4

Gates reproduced independently: `dune test` 0; `scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5` exit 0, 5/5; `nix flake check` all checks passed.

All seven round-3 correctness fixes and all round-3 prose/reuse fixes verified present and correct. Spot-verified rather than taken on trust: `Option.get !handle` is genuinely unreachable (phase returns only after attempt returned true, which sets it); a negative `manager_ready_timeout_s -. elapsed_s elapsed` yields one attempt then fails loudly, never a negative sleep; `release`'s Fun.protect is safe because rm_rf swallows all four syscalls and report_leak cannot raise; `~and_exit:false` does raise Test_error and exit non-zero; test_worktree's nested protect covers A if B's setup raises, tearing down B then A each after its own activate; `Mtime.Span.to_float_ns` is down to one occurrence under test/e2e; `wait_activeness` is back at HEAD's 0.1s and no interval regressed.

### The prose is now false in the opposite direction, and I owe a correction

Round 3 I found reexec.ml and dune claiming both reexec tests hit their own scratch. Those three sites are now accurate. But the mirror-image claim was left standing in the test that DID get a nested manager:

- test/e2e/test_unit_state_survives_reexec.ml:60 — 'REEXECS THE DEVELOPER'S USER MANAGER, up to [max_reexecs] times.' False: that test calls Harness.with_scratch, so the kicker's inherited environment names its own nested manager. Same at :145-146 ('spend the developer's manager on reexecs that add nothing' — they are its own).
- CLAUDE.md:37 — 'both run systemctl --user daemon-reexec against the live session ... must be last in the e2e alias'. The 'both' is half false; only test_reload_survives_reexec does.

**Correcting myself:** in round 3 I wrote that CLAUDE.md:37 'is still an accurate description of the tree'. Too broad. What was true, and was the point, is that test_reload_survives_reexec still reexecs the session manager so the ordering is load-bearing. The 'both' claim went stale back in round 1, when test_unit_state_survives_reexec got a scratch — not in round 4. Leaving CLAUDE.md alone was right for the ordering sentence and wrong for the 'both'.

Neither file is in the diff, but the diff's own change is what falsified them, so they are in scope. Details and two further reexec-prose defects recorded on .6.

### Correctness

- harness.ml:570-572 — the `Unix.Unix_error` arm in `phase` is dead code, and the comment above it ('narrows nothing beyond the two exception types the bus path raises') is false: `grep -c 'Unix\.' lib/systemctl/dbus.ml` is 0, and connect/unit_state raise only Schema.Pctl_error. As written it is a broad catch that would demote a genuine harness syscall bug to a 15s retry and a `!last` string. Fix: delete the arm, correct the comment to one type.
- harness.ml:647-651 — the inner `Fun.protect ~finally:(Unix.close fd)` wraps a failing close as `Fun.Finally_raised`, which is not `Unix.Unix_error`, so `attempt` does not catch it: `rm_cgroup m.cgroup` at :658 never runs, the cgroup leak goes unreported, and since release runs from a finaliser the escape replaces the test's real failure. Unlikely (close(2) on a fresh cgroup fd) but it is the masking shape this round otherwise closed, and the fix is free: wrap reap_manager's body in `Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> rm_cgroup m.cgroup)`. The same shape sits at :589-590, where a failing `Dbus.close h` would replace phase 2's failf.
- harness.ml:813 — `teardown` never activates its own scratch, though it holds one. It drives `Cli.Pipeline.Prod.down` and `Systemctl.Dbus.connect`, both environment-selected, so `teardown o` on a scratch that is not the current one silently operates on the wrong manager. Today every caller either has one scratch or pays the precondition by hand (test_worktree.ml:36,43 `activate a; teardown owned_a`). Fix: `activate s` at the top of teardown, which also lets test_worktree collapse to two plain `with_scratch` calls.
- reexec.ml:219-222 — `settle`'s failure message prints the constant budget where HEAD printed the observed wait, and since poll_until probes before checking the budget a blocked probe can overrun it. A 40s settle would report 'within 15s'. Fix: keep a counter and print `Harness.elapsed_s`.
- harness.ml:160 — the chmod guard `st_perm land 0o300 <> 0o300` omits the read bit `readdir` needs, so a `-wx` directory passes the guard and then fails to enumerate. Not a shape systemd produces; comparing against 0o700 is the same line.
- harness.ml:168 — the survival check uses `Sys.file_exists`, which resolves symlinks, in the one function whose comment exists because Sys.file_exists lies about dangling links. It cannot fire today (p is always a `fresh_tmpdir` directory, and a surviving directory does answer true), so this is consistency with its own reasoning rather than a live defect — `Unix.lstat` for one line.

### Reuse

- test_reload.ml:6-10, test_gc_explicit.ml:5-9, test_gc.ml, test_list.ml — the `owned` migration hand-rolled `Harness.with_scratch` verbatim (`setup` + `scratch_of` + `Fun.protect ~finally:teardown`), in files the diff touched, while 15 other e2e files call the helper. Fix: `Harness.with_scratch ~services @@ fun s -> …`. test_pctl_no_gc.ml and test_worktree.ml legitimately keep their own — extra putenv/activate in the finaliser.
- test_gc.ml:23-26, test_list.ml:17-20, test_pctl_no_gc.ml:25-28 — this diff added `sibling_scratch` but left its teardown half copied three times byte-identically, with the sequence recorded in `sibling_scratch`'s doc comment instead of in code. Fix: `with_sibling ~of_ ~prefix ~services f` beside it, and delete the prose.

### Prose

- harness.ml:507-508 — the counterfactual round 3 killed at the `status` field has reappeared in `manager_died`'s doc comment: 'so a later caller reads that instead of ECHILD, and does not signal a pid the kernel may since have handed to somebody else'. ECHILD maps to a Some at :523 and :632 signals only on None, so it cannot reach kill by either path. It is also a second copy of :299-303, which is correct. Fix: cut the clause, keep the field comment.
- reexec.ml:202-204 — 'the interval is a fifth of a second because a reexec'd manager takes that order of time to come back' sits against lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:15, which owns that timing and records 'about a second later'; and 'the budget matches the one a fresh manager gets' restates `~timeout_s:Harness.manager_ready_timeout_s` on the line below. Borrowing the nested-boot constant for a session-manager settle is also a coincidence rather than a reason — a named `settle_timeout_s` would say so.
- test_dbus_smoke.ml:54-55 and test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:84-85 carry the same 'a failing case raises Test_error, exits non-zero just the same' why; `skip_or_run`'s own comment owns it. Keep only the site-specific half.
- harness.ml:674 — the Owned comment blames `(wrapped false)` for a record being forgeable; the absent .mli is what does that. `(wrapped false)` only affects module prefixing.
- harness.ml:860-861 — the second stacked comment on wait_activeness repeats poll_until's own is-active-fork reason (:28-30).
- Counts in prose away from their code: harness.ml:145 'five 000-mode nodes', reexec.ml:20 'twice per run' (the 2 lives in test_reload_survives_reexec.ml).

### On Owned

The trade is stated honestly and I am not re-flagging it. There is a cheaper shape than an .mli, though: move `setup_with`/`setup` inside the struct and export them from the signature. `t` then has no exported constructor at all, so `teardown (Owned.mint sibling)` is not expressible rather than merely deliberate.

Commented on .6 (the inverted reexec prose, the two further request_stop defects, and my round-3 overstatement). Nothing new filed — everything else this round is in-scope.

title: e2e harness: systemctl_is_active reports 'inactive' when the bus is unreachable
description:
test/e2e/harness.ml's systemctl_is_active runs `systemctl --user is-active <unit>` through run_capture and discards both stderr and the exit code, returning the trimmed stdout. Every activeness assertion and wait_activeness poll goes through it.

Pre-existing, but pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.1 turns it into a live failure mode: which manager the read reaches is now selected by XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, set by Harness.activate. A test that forgets to activate, or activates the wrong scratch, gets 'failed to connect' on stderr, a non-zero rc, and stdout that does not say 'active' — indistinguishable from a unit that is genuinely inactive. wait_inactive then succeeds for the wrong reason and the test passes.

The same shape is why the harness comment for the curated unit path notes that `systemctl --user` keeps working via $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/private even when the manager owns no message bus: the private socket masks the exact fault a bus read would surface.

Fix: have systemctl_is_active return the rc alongside stdout and fail loudly (Alcotest.failf naming the unit, rc and stderr) on anything that is not a recognised is-active word. Or replace it with a Systemctl.Dbus.unit_state read, which cannot answer at all when the bus is wrong.

Falsifier: point XDG_RUNTIME_DIR at an empty dir and call Harness.wait_inactive on any unit name — it should fail, not return true.
close_reason: is_active/load_state/active_enter_ts go through systemctl_read, which fails on a non-answer; test_harness_reads is the falsifier. e2e green.

title: unit_store: Fs.rm_rf skips dangling symlinks, then silently fails to rmdir the directory
close_reason: Fs.rm_rf walks with lstat/unlink; non-ENOENT failures raise the new Uninstall_failed (exit 4). Three unit tests, each failing against the old fs.ml.

title: e2e harness: setup couples spawn and await, so tests needing two managers boot them in series
description:
Harness.setup / setup_with spawn the nested manager and then block in await_manager until its basic.target is active. A test that needs two scratches therefore pays two full manager boots end to end, though nothing about the second depends on the first.

Sites: test/e2e/test_worktree.ml:29-30 (two setups back to back), test/e2e/test_host.ml and test/e2e/test_results.ml (same shape).

Not covered by pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.5, which is about parallelising the dune alias across executables. This is serial work inside ONE executable.

Fix: split the two phases at the harness seam — a spawn step that returns the owned scratch right after spawn_manager plus activate, and an await step taking that owned scratch — then spawn both and await both. Callers already re-point the environment per operation via activate, so nothing else changes. Magnitude is one manager boot per affected test; measure before and after with the existing suite timing rather than projecting.

Also fold in while touching this: manager_env rebuilds `overridden @ dropped` and reallocates `k ^ \"=\"` for every inherited variable inside the filter closure; hoist the excluded-prefix list above the filter.

Second finding at the same site, which is a correctness bug rather than a cost and should be fixed regardless of whether the split happens: test_worktree.ml arms its Fun.protect only AFTER both setups have returned, so if the second setup raises, the first scratch's manager, its cgroup under user@<uid>.service and its tmpdir all leak, and because nothing calls report_leak for them exit_on_leaks cannot fail the run. Nest the second setup inside the first's Fun.protect.

title: harness: manager must die with its parent (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG)
description:
Teardown does not run on SIGKILL. A killed test would leave its nested manager reparented to PID 1 with every unit still running - a worse leak than today's, in a shape no existing reaper recognises (the host's reap-pctl-orphans matches pctl-*.slice under user@5000, which a nested manager's units are not).

Set PR_SET_PDEATHSIG on the child, or spawn into its own process group teardown kills as a group. Correctness requirement, not polish.

title: harness: teardown reaps the manager; drop the tombstone dance
description:
The manager's death removes every unit it knew, so the pctl down + reset_failed_unit + stop_unit sequence in teardown becomes unnecessary.

Cleanup must chmod -R u+rwX before rm -rf: a user manager creates systemd/inaccessible/{chr,sock,fifo,dir,reg} at mode 000 and a plain recursive delete fails on them. Observed.

Acceptance: after a full suite run, zero pctl-* units in the developer's session, is-system-running unchanged, no scratch dirs left. Today's baseline is one leaked tombstone per run.
close_reason: teardown = release: the manager's death takes its units; no down/reset-failed/stop. After a full e2e run: 0 project_* units in the session, is-system-running unchanged, 0 scratch dirs, 0 pctl-e2e cgroups.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
SCOPE SPLIT by .1: the chmod landed, the tombstone dance did not.

.1 shipped this ticket's 'Cleanup must chmod -R u+rwX before rm -rf' line — harness.ml's rm_rf now chmods each directory 0o700 before walking it, because the nested manager plants $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/inaccessible/ inside the scratch and .1's own rm_rf would otherwise fail. It had to, so this is not scope creep, but this ticket now reads as undone work that is half done.

Still here for .3: teardown's Down.run + reset_failed_unit + stop_unit sequence, and its rationale comment ('keeps leftovers from bleeding into the next test on the same session'), which .1 left in place and which is now false — release reaps the manager, and the manager's death is what removes its units.

Remaining acceptance for .3 unchanged: zero pctl-* units in the developer's session, no scratch dirs left. Note .1 added a second leak surface for that check — reap_manager's rm_cgroup swallows rmdir EBUSY, so a cgroup the manager left busy is dropped silently rather than reported.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
The lstat half of cleanup landed in .1 too, and it is not recorded anywhere.

This ticket owns 'Cleanup must chmod -R u+rwX before rm -rf'. .1 shipped that, and also a second cleanup fix with no ticket behind it: harness.ml's rm_rf now uses Unix.lstat/Unix.unlink instead of Sys.file_exists/Sys.remove, because systemd stores invocation ids as symlinks whose target is the id rather than a path, so every /run/user/<uid>/systemd/units/invocation:<unit> entry is permanently dangling, Sys.file_exists answers false for all of them, they were skipped, and the containing directory then failed to rmdir silently. Verified on this session: invocation:app-blueman@autostart.service -> 90f433db02ca491e856b35a22a942e43.

Both halves were forced by .1 (the manager's runtime dir now lives inside the scratch, so .1's own cleanup cannot pass without them), so this is not scope creep — but this ticket's acceptance ('no scratch dirs left') is now partly met by code that shipped under .1, and the same bug in the production copy is filed as pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.11.

Also still open for .3, unchanged: the down + reset_failed_unit + stop_unit sequence in teardown, which harness.ml now explicitly cites this ticket for. Note that sequence has a second problem the retirement would also remove — its Systemctl.Dbus.connect is the one call in teardown not wrapped in a catch, so a manager that died mid-test makes teardown RAISE before reaching release, leaking the cgroup and tmpdir with no leak report and masking the test's real failure through Fun.protect.

title: harness: skip_reason gates on sd_booted, not an inherited session
description:
Today skip_reason checks DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS and /run/user/<uid> - both describe an inherited session. The nested harness brings its own bus and runtime dir, so the real precondition is that the machine booted with systemd (what sd_booted() tests).

Verified in the Nix sandbox: /proc/self/cgroup is 0::/, /sys/fs/cgroup absent, manager refuses with 'Trying to run as user instance, but the system has not been booted with systemd'.

The skip message must name that condition - it is the one thing no configuration works around.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
FOUR NEW PRECONDITIONS from .1 that skip_reason still does not check.

.1 hardcodes absolute paths and an environmental capability, none of them gated:

  systemd_bin = /run/current-system/systemd/lib/systemd/systemd
  sh_bin      = /run/current-system/sw/bin/sh
  session_unit_dir = /etc/systemd/user   (source of all ten curated symlinks)
  a writable delegated cgroup under user@<uid>.service

The first two are NixOS-only. If either is absent the failure surfaces as a 15s await_manager timeout whose message includes manager.log — recoverable, but 15s per test and it reads as 'manager slow', not 'no interpreter'. The curated symlinks are created with Unix.symlink without checking the target exists, so a missing unit in /etc/systemd/user yields a dangling link and the silent capability loss .1's own comment documents ('every entry is load-bearing and every omission is silent').

user_manager_cgroup does fail loudly (Alcotest.failf naming the marker and the cgroup) when the process is not under user@<uid>.service, but nothing checks that the cgroup is WRITABLE — docs/adr/0002 records runners that deny that.

So this ticket grows: sd_booted plus the three paths plus a write probe on the delegated cgroup. That also makes it the ticket that decides whether a non-NixOS host skips or fails.

title: e2e: drop the serialisation rule, run tests in parallel
description:
test/e2e/dune collapses all 24 tests into one sequential action because they share a session and would race on user.control and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. A manager per test removes that premise.

The two reexec tests also lose their 'must be last' constraint, since the manager they disturb is their own.

Replace the projected numbers with measured ones once this lands: ~42s serial and ~10s parallel are arithmetic from component measurements, not an observed run.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
How to measure on this host — three traps that cost me several attempts.

1. /usr/bin/time does not exist on NixOS. Use bash's 'time' builtin, or nix-shell in pkgs.time if a machine-readable format is needed.

2. EPOCHREALTIME honours LC_NUMERIC. On a comma-decimal locale it yields '1785799265,723471', so the usual ${EPOCHREALTIME/./} microsecond trick silently does not substitute, and '10#$e' then fails with 'value too great for base'. It failed on only SOME iterations, which produced plausible-looking but corrupt numbers before it errored — I published a wrong 6.7x figure from exactly that. Export LC_ALL=C before any timing loop.

3. bc is not installed. Use bash integer arithmetic on microseconds.

Baseline this ticket must beat, measured warm (build already done, so this is execution):
  dune test          0.285 s for 156 tests
  dune build @e2e    96.7 / 95.7 / 98.1 s across three runs
  dune adds nothing: WALL 96711 ms vs SUM of the 24 executables 96698 ms

The ~42 s serial and ~10 s parallel targets are arithmetic from component measurements, never observed. Replace them with a real run before anyone relies on the ordering in this epic.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
The prose is already here — .1 wrote the retirement argument into test/e2e/dune while both mechanisms stay in force.

The comment above the single-rule collapse now says 'the races this serialisation was built for ... are gone', and the comment above the two reexec tests says 'the ordering no longer protects anything'. Both are claims this ticket owns and has not yet measured; the file they sit in still serialises everything and still pins the reexec tests last. A reader of test/e2e/dune is told the constraint is dead by the file that enforces it.

Either this ticket lands soon or that prose should shrink to a pointer. Also note the numbers .1 put in harness.ml's curated_units comment (99 session unit files / 552-580ms, ten curated / 129-141ms / basic.target 160ms) are the 'projected numbers' this ticket promises to replace with measured ones — and the 99 already disagrees with this map's comment 51, which recorded 214 files for the same host and the same reload time. Whichever counting method is right, scripts/measure-reloads.sh is the artifact that should hold the figure.

One measured datum from the review session, for the baseline: with .1 applied and the serialisation still in place, dune build @e2e --force takes 39.5s wall against the 98s recorded in this map.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
DO NOT retire the reexec-test ordering on the premise test/e2e/dune now states — it is false for one of the two tests.

dune's comment says 'these daemon-reexec their own scratch's manager. Nothing outside that scratch is disturbed, so the ordering protects nothing'. test_unit_state_survives_reexec does have a scratch (with_scratch at :99). test_reload_survives_reexec does NOT — no setup, no with_scratch, no activate; it connects on the ambient bus (:50) and its kicker inherits the session environment, so it still daemon-reexecs the developer's session manager twice per run. Details on pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.6.

Consequence for this ticket: the ordering constraint is still real, and parallelising the alias while test_reload_survives_reexec reexecs the shared session is exactly the race the collapse was built to prevent — except now it would hit the developer's desktop mid-suite rather than one test's scratch. Sequence this ticket AFTER .6 gives that test its own manager, or keep the two pinned last while the rest parallelise.

Measurement note for the baseline, from this review session: with .1 applied and the serialisation still in place, scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5 runs at roughly 36s per run against the 96.7/95.7/98.1 recorded on the parent map.

title: reexec: retarget the kicker at the test's own manager
description:
Reexec keeps its out-of-process kicker - the documented reason holds: pctl's bus calls are synchronous FFI holding the Eio domain, so an in-process fiber could only fire BETWEEN calls, and the case that matters is a reexec landing INSIDE one. The kicker's systemctl --user invocations gain the scratch's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.

What improves is cost and blast radius, NOT determinism. Attempts become free, so max_reexecs can rise until observing the window is effectively certain, and a failure to observe stays a failure (e2e-repeat.sh exit 3 must keep working).

BLOCKED ON MEASUREMENT: test_unit_state_survives_reexec may become genuinely deterministic - killing the nested manager and THEN issuing the read should produce the peer-gone reply with no race. test_reload_survives_reexec needs the manager to return, so it stays a race.

Falsifier before rewriting either: confirm a killed nested manager produces the same error_name the session manager does. Bus_retry's header records dbus-broker answering in-flight calls with NoReply / 'Remote peer disconnected' via driver_goodbye, then NameHasNoOwner once the name is unowned. A different name means the classification under test differs from production and the rewrite is invalid.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Constraint inherited from pctl-g9l's close, which must not be lost in the retarget.

test_unit_state_survives_reexec's detection depends on a tight spin: measured ~105,000 reads in ~12s yielding 2-4 faults. g9l's review says plainly that 'a reader adding a polite sleep would silently destroy detection while leaving the test green'. Reexec.poll_until_finished's header says the same. Any retarget must preserve the no-sleep property.

Two things the close reason changes about this ticket:

1. The gate already exists and is statistical BY DESIGN. Propagations are split by op and the assertion keys on GetUnit specifically — roughly half of faults land on Properties.Get and prove nothing. Do not simplify that back into a total count.

2. request_stop ends the kicker on the first GetUnit fault, so typical runs need 1-2 reexecs (sampled: 1,2,1,1,1 and 1,1,2,1,3,2,6,1). max_reexecs is 8 and round 4 of the review argued 16 is free because raising it only lengthens the rare tail. Under a nested manager that argument gets strictly stronger — a reexec costs nothing and touches nobody — so raising the cap is the cheapest way to drive UNEXERCISED runs toward zero.

Still open and unchanged: whether killing a nested manager produces the same error_name as a session reexec. That is the falsifier before rewriting either test.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
FALSIFIER IS NOW OVERDUE, not pending: .1 already retargeted the kicker.

This ticket says 'The kicker's systemctl --user invocations gain the scratch's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR' as its deliverable. .1 delivered it for free — the kicker is a `sh` subprocess started via Sys.command, so it inherits the process environment Harness.activate wrote, which now names the scratch's manager. test/e2e/reexec.ml's header was rewritten in that diff to say exactly this.

Consequence: both reexec tests now run against a nested manager, so 'confirm a killed nested manager produces the same error_name the session manager does' is no longer a precondition for a rewrite — it is a precondition for trusting the CURRENT green. Measured this session: dune build @e2e passes, test_reload_survives_reexec reports '12 reloads across 2 confirmed reexecs, 0 failures'. That green rests on a nested manager producing the NoReply / 'Remote peer disconnected' / NameHasNoOwner sequence Bus_retry classifies. Unverified.

Do the error_name comparison before raising max_reexecs, and before reading any nested-manager reexec pass as evidence about production.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
PARTIAL FALSIFIER RESULT — correcting my previous comment's 'unverified'.

The suite prints the propagated error itself, so five runs of scripts/e2e-repeat.sh recorded it. Against a NESTED manager, test_unit_state_survives_reexec reports:

  (propagated, as designed: systemctl Properties.Get <unit> failed: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply: Remote peer disconnected)
  (propagated, as designed: systemctl GetUnit <unit> failed: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply: Remote peer disconnected)

That is the NoReply / 'Remote peer disconnected' half of what Bus_retry's header records for a session reexec, on the same error_name. So the classification under test is NOT different for this case, and the falsifier does not block on it.

Not yet observed against a nested manager: NameHasNoOwner, the reply Bus_retry expects once the name is unowned. Five runs produced only NoReply. Whether a nested manager can reach the unowned-name window at all, or whether its reexec is fast enough that it never does, is the remaining open question — and it is the one that decides the 'may become genuinely deterministic' note above.

Also measured, same five runs: the reexec tests are no longer rare-tail. Observed 4 reexecs / 99,960 reads / 1 GetUnit propagation, and 2 confirmed reexecs / 12 reloads, with 5/5 runs green and no exit-3 UNEXERCISED batch. The 'attempts become free' premise for raising max_reexecs holds.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
CORRECTION, and it matters for this epic's motivation: only ONE of the two reexec tests was ever retargeted.

My earlier comments here said .1 delivered this ticket's 'the kicker's systemctl --user invocations gain the scratch's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR' for free via environment inheritance. That is true of test_unit_state_survives_reexec, which calls Harness.with_scratch (test_unit_state_survives_reexec.ml:99) and therefore has an activated scratch for the kicker to inherit.

It is FALSE of test_reload_survives_reexec. That file never calls setup or with_scratch — it goes from Harness.skip_or_run straight to Alcotest.run and `S.Dbus.connect ~sw env` on the ambient bus (test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:50, :82-86). There is no scratch, nothing calls activate, and the kicker therefore inherits the session environment. It still runs `systemctl --user daemon-reexec` against the DEVELOPER'S session manager, twice per run — ten times per `scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5` batch.

So the epic's stated motivation, 'Two tests daemon-reexec the developer's desktop', is half addressed. CLAUDE.md:37 ('both run systemctl --user daemon-reexec against the live session ... must be last in the e2e alias') is still an accurate description of the tree, and it is test/e2e/reexec.ml's header and test/e2e/dune's comment that are now wrong to say otherwise.

Revising two things I wrote here:
- The observed NoReply / 'Remote peer disconnected' error_name DOES come from a nested manager — that output is test_unit_state_survives_reexec's, which is scratch-local. That half of the falsifier stands.
- 'An attempt disturbs nobody' does not hold yet. Raising max_reexecs is only free for test_unit_state_survives_reexec today; doing it for test_reload_survives_reexec would multiply reexecs of the developer's desktop.

Giving test_reload_survives_reexec a scratch is this ticket's work (its 'test_reload_survives_reexec needs the manager to return, so it stays a race' note already assumes a nested manager). Until then the dune ordering is load-bearing and .5 must not retire it on the premise that nothing outside a scratch is disturbed.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
THE PROSE IS NOW FALSE IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, and I got part of round 3 wrong.

Round 3 I found that reexec.ml and test/e2e/dune claimed both reexec tests hit their own scratch's manager, when test_reload_survives_reexec has none. Round 4 corrected those three sites accurately. But the mirror-image claim was left standing in the test that DID get a nested manager, and in CLAUDE.md:

- test/e2e/test_unit_state_survives_reexec.ml:60 — 'REEXECS THE DEVELOPER'S USER MANAGER, up to [max_reexecs] times.' False: that test runs Harness.with_scratch, so activate points the kicker's inherited environment at its own nested manager. Same at :145-146, 'let the kicker stop rather than spend the developer's manager on reexecs that add nothing' — the reexecs it is saving are its own.
- CLAUDE.md:37 — 'test_reload_survives_reexec and test_unit_state_survives_reexec both run systemctl --user daemon-reexec against the live session ... Both share test/e2e/reexec.ml and must be last in the e2e alias.' The 'both' is half false now; only test_reload_survives_reexec does.

CORRECTION to my round-3 comment here and on .1: I wrote that CLAUDE.md:37 'is still an accurate description of the tree'. That was too broad. What was true — and was my actual point — is that test_reload_survives_reexec still reexecs the session manager, so the ordering is still load-bearing. CLAUDE.md's 'both' claim went stale the moment test_unit_state_survives_reexec got a scratch, which was round 1 of this work, not round 4.

Two more things in that test file for whoever picks this ticket up:

1. test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:21-24 says 'This test never calls [Reexec.request_stop]: every window it gets is another chance to catch a reload failing, and there is no point at which it has seen enough.' It calls it at :67. Pre-existing (present at HEAD), and it contradicts the file's own code, not just the new prose.
2. reexec.ml:120-122 now says test_reload_survives_reexec 'calls it once its assertions are due, which is what bounds how many times the developer's session manager is reexec'd'. Also false: the call at :67 happens after poll_until_finished has already returned, and the test then asserts confirmed = reexec_count. The kicker's own loop bound is what caps reexecs; request_stop only matters on the cap-fired path.

Giving that test a scratch would make all four statements moot, which is another reason to do it here rather than patch the prose four ways.

title: checks: NixOS VM backend running the same e2e executables
description:
Enters checks so nix flake check covers real systemd. Guest: lingering test user, ~87 units, reload ~148ms without curation.

Trim boot: virtualisation.vlans = [] and DHCP off takes systemd startup 15.4s -> 9.0s (dhcpcd alone was 7.0s). Driver still observes ~19.6s; ~10s of that is QEMU startup outside systemd's view.

Does NOT simplify CI. Verified on alpha: the default nix runner sets PrivateDevices = true (no /dev/kvm) AND ProtectControlGroups = true (no writable cgroups), so it can host neither backend. nix-privileged grants DeviceAllow = ['/dev/kvm rw'] and leaves cgroups alone. Both jobs stay there.

See docs/adr/0002.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Argument for this ticket that is stronger than 'hermetic coverage', and is evidenced:

A guest's systemd is a locked flake input. The developer's is not.

pctl-f3o (closed) is the failure mode this fixes. bus_errors delegated the slice contract to a measurement recorded on systemd 257; the host had moved to 260.1; nothing detected it, and it surfaced only in review. pctl-9rt was spent on the same class just before. Both were hand-reconciliation of version pins.

With a VM check, a systemd behaviour change arrives as a flake.lock diff plus a failing check on the update commit, instead of as a stale comment discovered months later. That converts an unversioned dependency into a versioned one, which is a property no amount of host-side testing can provide.

Worth stating in the guest config: the pinned systemd version is the thing this check is buying, so it should not be casually followed to whatever nixpkgs happens to have.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Why putting this in 'checks' does not slow the local loop.

checks is an addressable attrset. 'nix flake check' builds all of its members, but any single one runs on its own:
    nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.ocaml-tests    (measured 1.8 s warm)
    nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.treefmt        (measured 2.7 s warm)

So the VM check can live in checks — where CI and a pre-push sweep pick it up — while the inner loop runs 'dune test' and the nested e2e and never touches it. There is no need for a second, non-checks output to keep it out of the way.

Recording this because I argued the opposite earlier in the design discussion, posing a false choice between 'in checks and therefore always run' and 'outside checks and therefore not covered by nix flake check'. Neither horn is real. If the question comes up again, this is the answer.

For reference, nix flake check warm is ~9.6 s today, nearly all of it OCaml compiled twice — ocaml-build and ocaml-tests are separate derivations over the same source, deliberately, so their failures surface independently.

title: docs: reconcile UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE with the nested-manager harness
description:
Terms the harness change invalidates or moves:

- Straggler — defined as 'a slice left behind on the host session by a crashed test run; each test's teardown takes its own project down, but there is no suite-start sweep'. A per-test manager makes that state unreachable, so the term narrows to something else or dies.
- Harness — 'shared setup/teardown helpers in test/e2e/harness.ml (setup, with_scratch, spec_json, wait_active, teardown)'. Gains manager lifecycle.
- Scratch — the record gains the manager's directories and handle.
- Reality test — 'run against the host's real systemd --user'. Still real systemd, no longer the host's.

Also check the Testing section against CLAUDE.md, which was amended separately (unit = one module at a time including ports through their in-memory adapters; integration = several components wired). That amendment closed pctl-uu4; the glossary should agree with it.

Carved out of docs/adr/0001 deliberately: an ADR records the decision, not the state of another document.

title: harness: opt-in escape hatch back to the session manager
description:
After this epic no gate exercises a desktop login session, which is the environment every real pctl user runs. The nested manager has a curated unit set and no logind seat; the VM guest is a lingering headless user. Both are unrepresentative in the same direction.

Add an env opt-in (e.g. PCTL_E2E_USE_SESSION=1) that makes the harness use the ambient session manager instead of spawning one. Default stays nested.

Why an escape hatch rather than a kept gate: running against the developer's session is what this epic exists to stop doing by default. But ADR 0001 says to reach for the session manager deliberately when debugging an interaction with it, and right now nothing makes that possible once setup_with owns the manager. A flag makes the ADR's advice actionable.

Also the only way to answer 'is this failure a pctl bug or a nested-manager artifact?' without hand-editing the harness — which is the diagnosis ADR 0002 says a one-sided failure requires.

Scope note: with the hatch set, the pre-existing hazards come back (shared session, serialisation, tombstones). That is expected and does not need fixing; the hatch is for deliberate debugging, not a supported mode.

title: schema: Unit_op_failed should carry the D-Bus error name as its own field, so classification is equality rather than a prefix test on a display string
description:
Follow-on from pctl-8sd, which the ticket itself scoped to [reply] ("Unit_op_failed carries [reply], which holds the D-Bus error name"). The predicate works, but it classifies on a string built for humans.

lib/schema/schema.ml:466-471:
    let is_no_such_unit = function
      | Unit_op_failed { reply; _ } ->
          String.starts_with ~prefix:no_such_unit_dbus_error reply
      | _ -> false

Two consequences:

1. lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:339-344 (format_bus_reply) has four arms, and only two put the name first:
       | Some name, Some message -> sprintf "%s: %s" name message
       | None, Some message -> message
       | Some name, None -> name ^ " (no message)"
       | None, None -> format_sd_bus_err op rc
   The `None, Some message` arm emits a bare message with no name at all. A NoSuchUnit reaching that arm classifies as "propagate". The direction is safe, but the classifier is coupled to a formatting function it cannot see, and the coupling is invisible at the call site in lifecycle.

2. lib/schema/schema.ml holds a D-Bus wire constant (no_such_unit_dbus_error) although schema is the pure core and knows nothing about the transport. The prefix test also has no terminator, so a hypothetical org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnitXxx would be tolerated (no such systemd error name exists today).

Fix: add `error_name : string option` to Unit_op_failed, populated in dbus.ml from Sd_bus_error.parts (None for transport failures, which is the correct "propagate" answer) and set explicitly by In_mem. is_no_such_unit becomes an equality test on that field; [reply] stays for rendering only. This makes the misclassification unrepresentable instead of merely unlikely.
close_reason: Unit_op_failed carries error_name : string option, set from Sd_bus_error.parts in Dbus and explicitly by In_mem. is_no_such_unit + is_peer_gone now live together in lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml and both match the name by equality; schema no longer holds a D-Bus wire constant. Attempt count and elapsed time stay formatted into reply — no caller branches on them, noted at the site.

comments.author: claude
manveru
comments.text:
Adjacent, same root cause: Dbus.daemon_reload's retry-exhaustion detail is also stringly-typed into the same field.

lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:577-583 appends '(gave up after %d attempts over %.1fs)' to `reply` before raising Unit_op_failed. A caller that wants to distinguish 'rejected immediately' from 'burned the full 5s budget' -- Gc.opportunistic_sweep is the one that most wants to, since it swallows the error and pays the latency -- has to substring-match a display string, which is exactly what this ticket says about the error name.

If Unit_op_failed grows a typed name field, consider whether it should also carry the attempt count and elapsed time rather than having them formatted into `reply`.

Noted during the round-4 review of pctl-jbd; the string form was implemented as round 1 requested, so it is not a defect in that diff.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Review of e778a30 (closes pctl-nir, a7p, q2j, 8za, 26e, srj, fl6). Working tree is clean, so the commit is what was reviewed. Posted here for the whole batch.

## Intent

- lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml:153 — pctl-a7p asked for "an integration case: arm the fake to fail get_unit_path with a non-NoSuchUnit reply and assert unit_state propagates rather than answering Inactive". In_mem.unit_state is total and the fake has only fail_next_start/fail_next_stop, so dbus.ml:725-727's narrowing has no test. Add fail_next_unit_state + one integration case. (pctl-7yg)

## Silent failures

- lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:785-795, :861-866 → lib/probe/probe.ml:192 — the signal-handler path reports and drops. Probe's callback itself calls unit_job_pending, which now propagates; that Pctl_error is printed at dbus.ml:863 and discarded, the promise never resolves, and wait_service returns Probe_timeout after the full --timeout for what was a bus fault. pctl-q2j permitted the log-instead-of-raise, so not a breach — but the error still doesn't reach a caller that could act. (pctl-vv4)
- dbus.ml:861 / in_mem.ml:74 — `with e` also covers Cancelled/Out_of_memory; same shape as pctl-6ra, commented there rather than duplicated.

## Standards and fixtures

- test/unit/test_gc.ml:308 — still `op = "stop"`, the fabricated label pctl-fl6 removed from In_mem, in a record this diff edited to add error_name. test/unit/test_bus_retry.ml:67 likewise hand-authors "org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit" although Bus_errors.no_such_unit now owns it. (pctl-jbi)
- lib/schema/schema.ml:483 — `"systemctl %s %s failed"` renders a D-Bus method as a CLI verb: real ops are StopUnit, Properties.Get(Job), Job/enter_struct. Pre-existing; fl6 unmasked it by removing the fake's lowercase labels. (pctl-19n)

## Prose

- lib/systemctl/bus_errors.ml:22-27 claims StopUnit/ResetFailedUnit "on an unloaded unit" answer NoSuchUnit, verified on systemd 260.1. test/e2e/test_down_missing_units.ml:15-27, measured on 257, records that an unloaded .slice SUCCEEDS and returns a job path — so the claim is false for slices, and the two version pins disagree. Strongest finding here: "claim only the case", and Lifecycle's down path stops a slice under exactly this tolerance. (pctl-9rt)
- The sd_bus_error_set_errno / System.Error.ENOTCONN mechanism now sits in five prose blocks (bus_retry.ml:32, bus_errors.ml:56-58, dbus.ml:109, dbus.ml:343-344, schema.ml:98) while test_bus_errors.ml:74-76 asserts it. pctl-srj deleted the two refuted copies; the corrected claim proliferated. dbus.ml:343-344 says "see [Bus_errors]" and then restates it. (pctl-2nc)
- docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md:267 — the Unit_op_failed listing gained error_name in this diff and kept `unit`, where the code has `unit_` (schema.ml:104-109). Drifted at the moment of editing. (pctl-xgl)
- lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:19-22, :103-105, :120-124 — the Removed-arm why written three times in one file. Header (pctl-8za asked for it) and inline are defensible; the apply_plan bullet is the third. (pctl-l9j)

## Gates run this session

- `dune test` — exit 0.

title: test_helpers: write_temp_file never removes the file, leaking one temp file per test run
UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md gc section describes a pre-SQLite state-dir design that no longer exists
description:
UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:50-58 defines the gc vocabulary in terms of *state dirs* and *known markers*. Neither concept exists in the code: grep for state_dir/known_marker across lib bin test nix returns only an unrelated prose mention at lib/render/render.ml:115. Gc classifies rows in the SQLite 'projects' table (lib/gc/gc.ml:32-37), not directories under XDG_STATE_HOME, and there is no marker cross-referencing anywhere.

Every one of the three class rows contradicts Gc.class_of_row and Gc.purge:

- Doc 'Live: a state dir whose known marker points at a project path that still exists'. Code: Live iff session_id = current boot_id. Path existence is not the Live test.
- Doc 'Orphan: ... points at a project path that no longer exists'. Code: Orphan is the opposite — path EXISTS but there is no live session. Path-gone is Unknown.
- Doc 'Orphan ... the only class gc --yes deletes'. False: purge (gc.ml:120-133) matches 'Schema.Orphan | Schema.Unknown'.
- Doc 'Unknown: ... reported only, never deleted automatically'. False twice over: purge deletes Unknown, and opportunistic_sweep (gc.ml:93-112) deletes Unknown automatically on every mutating command (up/reload/down/restart).
- Doc line 50 'known markers written alongside the registry under lib/state/'. No such artifact.

This matters more than an ordinary stale comment: CLAUDE.md:11 instructs readers to read UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md *before writing code or docs*, so the wrong definitions are the first thing an agent or contributor absorbs — and 'Orphan means the path is gone' inverts the actual predicate that decides whether gc deletes a project's units.

Deliberately NOT fixed in the dead-code-cleanup pass: rewriting three domain-term definitions is a domain-model change, not a comment fix. Suggest driving it with the curu-domain-modeling skill so the replacement vocabulary (registry row / session id / boot id) is settled once and reflected in CLAUDE.md too.

Adjacent pointer-only staleness in the same file WAS fixed in that pass: :21 linked deleted lib/install/, :62 credited lib/plan/ with computing the diff (it lives in State.Projects.diff_manifest), :89-91 listed harness helpers and scratch fields that do not exist.
close_reason: gc vocabulary rewritten over registry rows, session id and boot id; Known marker and the state-dir framing deleted
