comments.text:
Rewrote the gc vocabulary against lib/gc/gc.ml.

Deleted **Known marker** (no such artifact in the tree). **Registry** redefined as the SQLite DB under $XDG_STATE_HOME (was: $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pctl/projects/<id>/ with manifest.nuon, 'cleared on reboot'). Added **Registry row** as the thing gc actually classifies, and **Boot id** / **Session id** / **Session reset** as the vocabulary the three classes are defined over; section renamed 'Session & garbage collection'.

The three class rows now match Gc.class_of_row: Unknown = project path gone, Live = path exists and session id is the current boot id, Orphan = path exists and session id is not. Added **Remove (gc)**, **Opportunistic sweep** and **Purge** so the two deletion paths are distinguishable — the old text claimed --yes deleted Orphan only and that Unknown was never deleted automatically; both are false.

**State dir** moved to Artifacts, where it belongs: it is systemd's, not gc's subject. A flagged-ambiguity entry now says gc never looks at one.

Two corrections outside the gc section, same vocabulary: **Down** clears the session-scoped columns and keeps the row (Lifecycle.down -> Projects.clear_runtime_fields), it does not drop the entry; CLAUDE.md:7 listed 'store tree', an alias the file itself flags, and named none of the new terms.

Three review rounds. Round 1 fixed ten findings (two factual: session reset is not the first query of *every* invocation, and reload re-stamps the session id as well as up), round 2 one (the session id stamp is unconditional and precedes Lifecycle, so Live does not imply anything started). Filed along the way: pctl-gc-state-dir-reclaim-bd1, pctl-e2e-harness-state-dir-leak-9oz, pctl-s3y, pctl-x7m, pctl-468.

title: systemctl: reset_failed_unit has no production caller, only the e2e harness
description:
Found while narrowing its error handling under pctl-26e.

lib/systemctl/systemctl_intf.ml:34 declares reset_failed_unit and both adapters implement it (lib/systemctl/dbus.ml, lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml). The only caller in the tree is test/e2e/harness.ml's teardown, which clears a test project's failed tombstone between runs.

So the port carries an operation pctl itself never issues: no CLI command clears a tombstone, and nothing in lib/cli references it. Its behaviour is therefore specified only by what a test needs, which is how the swallow-every-rc shape survived until pctl-26e.

Two ways out, needs a judgement rather than a fix:
  - a production caller is missing — a wedged unit with a failed tombstone is a real state a user hits, and 'pctl restart' arguably should clear it before starting;
  - or it belongs to the harness, and the port should not advertise it.

Note pctl-26e made it able to raise; the harness call is already wrapped in try/with so nothing there changes.

title: systemctl/dbus: three sites comment 'NoSuchUnit tolerance' but swallow every Pctl_error, so a bus failure reads as a unit state
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing pctl-8sd, which added Schema.is_no_such_unit.

Three sites in lib/systemctl/dbus.ml catch `Schema.Pctl_error _` and substitute a value that reads as a legitimate answer:

- :635 — unit_state: `try Some (get_unit_path t ~unit:u) with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> None` → Schema.Inactive. Comment says "GetUnit may fail with NoSuchUnit for a unit that has never been loaded ... We treat any exception on get_unit_path as inactive."
- :682-689 — unit_job_pending: same get_unit_path catch → false, plus `with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> false` around read_job_path. Comment: "Same NoSuchUnit tolerance as [unit_state]".
- :695 — safe_unit_state_forward: `try unit_state t ~unit:u with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> Schema.Inactive`.

In each case a bus disconnect, a transport errno, or a malformed reply is indistinguishable from "the unit is not loaded". `pctl status` then reports inactive for a service that is actually running; the wait loop sees no pending job and can conclude early.

Fix: narrow all three to `when Schema.is_no_such_unit e` and let everything else propagate. :695 is the signal-handler forward and may genuinely need to not raise — if so, keep a catch there but log the reply rather than silently returning Inactive.
close_reason: All three sites narrowed. The two get_unit_path catches collapsed into get_unit_path_opt (no-such-unit only); read_job_path is no longer wrapped; the signal-handler forward returns an option and logs, so a bus fault fires no callback rather than reporting Inactive.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Concrete instance, observed 2026-08-02 during the pctl-jbd verification run. Details and the journal are in pctl-xxf's comment; the short version:

A 'switch-to-configuration' reexec landed while test_depends_on_wait's 'app' unit was queued-Inactive behind its migrate dependency. unit_job_pending's two 'with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> false' catches (dbus.ml) turned the peer-gone reply into 'no pending job'. Probe then read Inactive + no-job as terminal and pctl exited 5 with 'service app terminated in state inactive' — for a service systemd started successfully one second later.

This is exactly the failure mode this ticket describes ('the wait loop sees no pending job and can conclude early'), with a real trigger rather than a hypothetical one. The transient was indistinguishable from a unit state, as predicted.

title: test/lib: read_file is hand-rolled in four places; the e2e harness should own one
description:
Four near-identical open/Fun.protect/really_input_string implementations, none reachable from the others by dune scoping:

  - lib/cli/init.ml:23-29        read_file (raises on missing)
  - test/unit/test_helpers.ml:7-12
  - test/e2e/harness.ml:172-180  read_unit (same shape, unit-file specific)
  - test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:60-66  read_file (returns "" on missing) -- newest copy

test/e2e links e2e_harness, not test_helpers or cli's internals, so the fifth caller will copy it again. Harness is already the shared library every e2e test links; put a generic read_file there and have read_unit and the new test call it.

Note the copies are not equivalent: init.ml raises Sys_error on a missing file, the new e2e copy returns "". Whichever lands in Harness has to pick one and say why -- the e2e copy's "" is load-bearing for its vacuity guard (an absent marker must compare unequal to "ok", not raise).

title: state/db: default_path falls back to "/" when HOME is unset, silently siting the registry at /.local/state/pctl/state.db
description:
lib/state/db.ml:27-39:

  let default_path () =
    match Sys.getenv_opt "XDG_STATE_HOME" with
    | Some d when String.length d > 0 -> d
    | _ ->
        let home =
          match Sys.getenv_opt "HOME" with
          | Some h when String.length h > 0 -> h
          | _ -> "/"      <-- here
        in
        Filename.concat home ".local/state"

With neither XDG_STATE_HOME nor HOME set, pctl opens /.local/state/pctl/state.db instead of failing. ensure_parent_dir (db.ml:41-50) then mkdir -p that path, so on a writable root it succeeds and every project silently registers in a second, invisible registry; on a read-only root the user gets an mkdir error naming a path they never configured.

Contrast the sibling reader: Clock.read_boot_id_exn (lib/clock/clock.ml:8-12) deliberately raises on a blank read rather than degrading, with the reason at the line. Same class of input, opposite policy.

Fix: raise when both vars are absent/empty, naming both env vars in the message. There is no identity value for "where is the state database" — "/" is a plausible wrong answer where raising reports the bug.

Found while reviewing pctl-oik (UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md registry rewrite): UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:41 documents the fallback chain as ending at $HOME/.local/state/pctl/state.db, so the doc does not describe this third level either. Fixing the code removes the need to document it.

title: docs: the UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE 'host' rule is breached by the repo's own prose, including that file
description:
UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:124 states the rule verbatim:

  - **"Host"** is overloaded: the machine running pctl vs. the allocated `127.0.0.N`. In pctl code and docs, **Host** always means the allocated loopback address; for the machine, use "host system" or "dev host".

CLAUDE.md points at this file as binding ("Read UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md before writing code or docs"), but bare "host" for the dev machine is the norm in prose:

  - UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:88 - **Reality test**: "An e2e test run against the host's real systemd --user"
  - UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:91 - **Straggler**: "A slice left behind on the host session"
  - CLAUDE.md Tests section - "runs the real-systemd suite on the host"
  - lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:4,93 - "observed on this host", "Measured on this host"
  - test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:12,21,30 - "on this host"

A rule nothing observes is not a rule. Decide one way and make the docs match: either replace the bare uses with "dev host", or narrow the rule to code identifiers only and say so at :124.

Filed from the round-4 review of pctl-jbd. Pre-existing; the bus_retry/e2e sites are new in that diff but are the same breach as the surrounding prose, so not that diff's job.

title: lifecycle: two concurrent pctl runs on the same project race on user.control
description:
Two `pctl` processes invoked on the SAME project path (same project id, same slice, same unit filenames) have no mutual exclusion. Nothing in Pipeline or Lifecycle takes a lock; State.Db is a per-invocation caqti connection.

Today the overlap is write-then-persist: both render, both write the same unit files, both replace_manifest. Because the rendered bytes are a pure function of (spec, id, host, project path), two runs of the SAME spec converge; two runs of DIFFERENT specs (one mid-edit) can interleave writes and leave the manifest describing bytes neither run wrote.

pctl-468's D1 widens the window on the read side: `installed` is now derived by reading user.control before the write, so run A can read, run B can write, and run A then diffs against bytes that no longer exist and applies a plan for a state that is gone.

Not addressed in pctl-468 — that work makes the read explicit but does not create the race, and serialising it is a separate design decision (advisory flock on the project's slice file in user.control, a SQLite lock held across the invocation, or an explicit "already running" refusal).

Note that different projects do NOT race: ownership and unit filenames are project-id-scoped, so their file sets are disjoint. This is strictly about concurrent invocations on one project.
close_reason: duplicate of pctl-concurrent-runs-race-xn5, which is more thorough (covers up-racing-down) and already accounts for D1's two-phase persist

title: spec: a malformed slice_config is reported as 'service_config must be a JSON object'
description:
lib/spec/spec.ml string_map_of_yojson is shared by service_config and slice_config, and both of its error strings hard-code the name "service_config":

  | _ -> Error "service_config must be a JSON object"
  ... Error (sprintf "service_config[%s] must be a string ...")

Measured 2026-08-04: a spec.json with "slice": {"slice_config": []} reports

  spec parse error (/run/user/1000/.../spec.json): service_config must be a JSON object

naming a key the file does not contain, while the offending key sits elsewhere. Cost me a wrong fix attempt writing scripts/measure-reloads.sh, which is how it was found.

Reachable in production: spec.json is generated by nix/lib/mkProject.nix, so a hand-written or third-party spec.json is the trigger. test/unit/test_spec.ml covers the service_config cases (12, 13) and no slice_config case, so nothing catches it.

Fix: pass the field name into string_map_of_yojson, or wrap at the two call sites. The mkProject hint in the second message ("every value is coerced to string by mkProject") stays correct for both.

title: schema: two more copies of the refuted 'transport failure leaves sd_bus_error empty' claim
description:
The pctl-jbd diff corrected the 'transport failures leave the sd_bus_error struct empty' claim in three places (lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:105-111, dbus.ml:342-347, lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:59-72). Two copies outside lib/systemctl were not touched and still assert the refuted version:

  - lib/schema/schema.ml:465 -- '... its decoded-errno fallback for a transport failure -- fail the test, which is the safe ...'
  - test/unit/test_schema.ml:314 -- '(* transport failure: sd_bus_error empty, reply is the decoded errno *)'

What the source actually says (systemd v260, the version this machine runs): every fail: path in sd_bus_call_methodv and sd_bus_call runs sd_bus_error_set_errno, which resolves through errno_to_bus_error_const or falls back to strjoin("System.Error.", name) / BUS_ERROR_FAILED. A transport failure therefore arrives NAMED -- 'System.Error.ENOTCONN' for a closed bus -- not with an empty struct. The empty-struct case is near-unreachable through sd_bus_call_method.

The test at test_schema.ml:314 is not wrong as a test -- it exercises the (None, None) arm, which is legitimate coverage of a total match. Only its comment's description of when that arm occurs is wrong.

Fix: reword both to match lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:59-72, and at test_schema.ml:314 say the case is the near-unreachable backstop rather than 'transport failure'.

Filed from the round-5 review of pctl-jbd. Pre-existing: neither file is touched by that diff.
close_reason: Both copies gone: schema's comment block was replaced by the error_name field doc under pctl-nir, and the test comment moved into test_bus_errors.ml wording the no-name case as the near-unreachable backstop. No 'sd_bus_error empty on transport failure' claim left in the tree.

title: e2e harness: slice_name/service_name sprintf the unit-name convention under a comment claiming they delegate to Schema
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing pctl-8sd.

test/e2e/harness.ml:500-504:
    (* Name helpers — delegate to the canonical Schema derivations so tests
     * and production agree on the filename convention. *)
    let slice_name id_s = Printf.sprintf "pctl-%s.slice" id_s
    let service_name id_s svc = Printf.sprintf "pctl-%s-%s.service" id_s svc

The comment is true of slice_filename_for/service_filename_for immediately below (which do call Schema.Unit_filename) and false of these two, which hardcode the convention. So tests and production agree only by coincidence, and a change to Schema.Unit_filename would leave these silently stale — the exact drift the comment claims to prevent.

They also duplicate the pair below: slice_name (Project_id.to_string id) and slice_filename_for ~id return the identical string, which is why pctl-8sd's new e2e test carries both an `id_s`/`slice` pair and a `slice_file`.

Fix: delete slice_name/service_name and have callers use slice_filename_for/service_filename_for, or reimplement them in terms of Schema.Unit_filename. Then update the affected e2e tests.

title: test layering: fake-adapter tests live in test/unit, which CLAUDE.md reserves for the pure core
description:
CLAUDE.md:25-26 defines the layers:

    - **Pure / unit** (`test/unit/`) — alcotest + qcheck property tests over the pure core (schema, identity, manifest, render). Sandbox-safe.
    - **Integration** (`test/integration/`) — in-process tests against the Fake Systemctl adapter (alcotest-eio). Sandbox-safe.

test/unit/dune links eio, eio_main, eio.unix, systemctl and probe, and test/unit/test_probe.ml, test_systemctl_sig.ml and test_unit_store.ml are in-process tests against the fake adapters — by the definition above, integration tests.

Both commits in this batch added to the wrong side: 761669c put test_wait_service_read_failure_propagates in test/unit/test_probe.ml, f7ff155 added 58 lines to test/unit/test_systemctl_sig.ml. Both pctl-a7p and pctl-7yg asked for 'an integration case'; test/integration/ was not touched by either, and f7ff155's commit body says 'In_mem can now fail a state read, which is what pctl-a7p asked for'.

Nothing is broken — both directories run under `dune test` and both are sandbox-safe, which is why this drifted. But the documented split is what tells the next author where to put a test, and right now the ubiquitous answer 'integration' points at a directory that does not hold the fake-adapter tests.

Pre-existing in shape: test_probe.ml and test_systemctl_sig.ml predate this batch.

Fix: either move the fake-adapter test files to test/integration/, or amend CLAUDE.md:25-26 to describe the split that actually exists (e.g. unit = single-module, integration = Lifecycle/multi-module flows). The second is cheaper and may be the truer description — decide which, then make the two agree.

Filed from round 2 of the review of 761669c/f7ff155.
close_reason: CLAUDE.md amended to describe the split that exists rather than moving three suites: test/unit is one-module-at-a-time including ports through their in-memory adapters, test/integration is multi-component over SQLite. Moving test_systemctl_sig/test_probe/test_gc would have been churn for no gain.

title: probe: a bus fault inside the subscription path becomes Probe_timeout, not the real error
description:
e778a30 stopped the signal-handler path forging Schema.Inactive (pctl-a7p, pctl-q2j) and made it report instead — which pctl-q2j explicitly permitted ('keep a catch there but log the reply'). What is left: the error still never reaches the caller that could act on it.

Two sites, both report-and-drop:

  lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:785-795 — safe_unit_state_forward: prerr_endline then None, so the handler fires no callback.
  lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:861-866 — `try entry.cb s with e -> prerr_endline …`.

The second one matters more than it looks, because Probe's callback makes its own bus call. lib/probe/probe.ml:180-200:

    let try_resolve state = … | `Maybe_terminal ->
        if not (M.unit_job_pending handle ~unit:service_unit) then …
            Eio.Promise.resolve u state
    …
    Eio.Promise.await p

unit_job_pending (probe.ml:192) goes to the bus and, since e778a30, propagates everything but no-such-unit. That Pctl_error is raised inside entry.cb, printed at dbus.ml:863, and discarded. The promise is never resolved, wait_service's Eio.Fiber.first (probe.ml:281-287) falls to the deadline, and the row comes back `Timed_out → Schema.Probe_timeout, "probe for service X timed out after N ms" (probe.ml:139-142). The initial read at probe.ml:198 propagates correctly; only the post-subscription window has this shape.

Net: a bus fault mid-wait costs the full --timeout and is reported as a probe timeout. Better than the old silent Inactive (which concluded early with a wrong answer), still not the real error.

Fix: give the handler somewhere to put the failure — a `last_error : Schema.error option ref` on t that wait_unit_state checks alongside the promise, or resolve the promise with an Error so wait_service raises the original Unit_op_failed.

Filed from the review of e778a30.

title: dbus: dlopen discards the Dl.DL_error message, reporting 'not found' for any load failure
description:
Pre-existing; lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:34-52.

  let libsystemd_lazy : Dl.library option Lazy.t =
    lazy
      (try Some (Dl.dlopen ~filename:"libsystemd.so.0" ~flags:[ Dl.RTLD_NOW ])
       with Dl.DL_error _ -> (
         try Some (Dl.dlopen ~filename:"libsystemd.so" ~flags:[ Dl.RTLD_NOW ])
         with Dl.DL_error _ -> None))

Both DL_error payloads are dropped, and the None case then reports one fixed message:

    msg = "libsystemd.so.0 not found via dlopen; check LD_LIBRARY_PATH or systemdLibs build input"

dlopen with RTLD_NOW fails for reasons other than absence: a wrong ELF class (32/64-bit mismatch), an undefined symbol in the library or its own dependencies, or a permission error. All of them surface as 'not found ... check LD_LIBRARY_PATH', which sends the reader down the wrong path.

Fix: keep the second attempt's DL_error message and include it in the Bus_connect_failed msg — 'libsystemd.so.0: <dl error>; libsystemd.so: <dl error>'. Keeping only the fallback's message is enough; keeping both is better.

title: e2e harness: teardown swallows every failure, so a reexec test that forgets to settle leaks units silently
description:
test/e2e/harness.ml:206-219 — teardown runs three operations, each with a bare catch-all:

    (try ignore (Cli.Pipeline.Prod.down ~sw ~env ~path:s.project_dir ~quiet:true ()) with _ -> ());
    ...
    (try Systemctl.Dbus.reset_failed_unit handle ~unit:slice with _ -> ());
    (try Systemctl.Dbus.stop_unit handle ~unit:slice with _ -> ());

Of those, only daemon_reload carries a peer-gone retry (Bus_retry); stop_unit and reset_failed_unit do not. So a NoReply arriving here — which is exactly what a daemon-reexec produces — leaves the test's service and slice running on the developer's session with nothing printed anywhere.

Two e2e tests now reexec the manager. Both currently avoid the hole by calling Reexec.settle before returning, which is the right fix for them, but it is a convention: a third reexec test that forgets settle gets a silent leak, and the failure mode is invisible until the session accumulates enough stray pctl-*.slice units to be noticed.

There is also a live instance of the convention not holding. test/e2e/test_unit_state_survives_reexec.ml calls Reexec.check_completed (:149) BEFORE Reexec.settle (:154), and check_completed raises via Alcotest.failf when the kicker did not finish. The kicker not finishing is the cap-fired path — i.e. precisely the run where the manager is most likely still unsettled — so on that path teardown does run inside the window. That specific ordering is in-scope feedback on the current diff; the harness-level hole is this ticket.

Fix options, in the order I would consider them:
 1. Have teardown report rather than swallow: keep it non-fatal (teardown must not mask the test's own failure) but eprintf what failed and on which unit, so a leak is at least visible in the run's output.
 2. Give teardown's stop_unit/reset_failed_unit the same bounded peer-gone retry daemon_reload has, so a reexec window is survived rather than tolerated.
 3. Make settling the harness's job rather than each test's, so with_scratch cannot return inside a window.

(1) is cheap and strictly better than today regardless of which of the others lands.

Raised by the author during round 4 of the review as something they would rather fix in the harness than rely on convention for. Agreed — filing so it does not ride along with the pctl-g9l work.

Filed from round 4 of the review.
close_reason: Teardown no longer runs any bus operation to swallow: it is release, whose failures go through report_leak and fail the run (nak.1). Reexec.settle's rationale updated.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Still live after pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.1, and the list grew.

Unchanged catch-alls in test/e2e/harness.ml teardown: `try Some (project_id s) with _ -> None` (a derive failure silently skips ALL tombstone cleanup), the three bare `with _ -> ()` around down/reset_failed_unit/stop_unit, and `Sys.readdir ... with Sys_error _ -> [||]` treating an unreadable directory as empty.

New ones .1 introduced on the same teardown path:
  - reap_manager's `try Unix.kill m.pid Sys.sigterm with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()` swallows EPERM as well as ESRCH; EPERM means the pid was recycled, after which waitpid gives ECHILD and teardown reports success while the real manager runs on.
  - the `cgroup.kill` openfile swallows ENOENT/EACCES, so the escalation can silently not happen.
  - rm_cgroup's `try Unix.rmdir dir with Unix.Unix_error _ -> ()` swallows EBUSY — the one errno that means processes are still in the cgroup, i.e. exactly the leak reap_manager exists to detect.
  - the final 'HARNESS LEAK' path is Printf.eprintf only, so a manager that survives both SIGTERM and cgroup.kill leaves the suite green.

The eprintf-not-raise choice is justified at the site (it runs from a Fun.protect finaliser, where raising would mask the test's own failure). A module-level flag plus at_exit satisfies both.

title: cli: quiet 'pctl down' swallows every exception with a bare 'with _ -> 0'
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing the pctl-jbd retry diff.

lib/cli/pipeline.ml:292-296:

    if quiet then
      try
        work ();
        0
      with _ -> 0
    else run work

The bare `_` returns exit 0 for anything: a Pctl_error, a caqti Failure, Unix_error, Out_of_memory, Stack_overflow, and — newly relevant after pctl-jbd — Eio.Cancel.Cancelled, since Dbus.daemon_reload can now yield at a cancellable sleep inside Bus_retry.with_retry where it previously could not.

Inconsistent with the repo's own established practice one module over. lib/gc/gc.ml:65-73 narrows the analogous best-effort catch and says so explicitly:

    (* ... We still narrow from [_] to the specific
     * failure modes we've observed: systemd not running (Unix_error),
     * pctl-tracked errors (Pctl_error), and caqti wrappers (Failure). *)
    let ignore_best_effort f =
      try f ()
      with Failure _ | Unix.Unix_error _ | Schema.Pctl_error _ -> ()

Quiet down plausibly should not fail the caller — that part is a deliberate product choice and is not in question. What is wrong is the width: the catch should name what it tolerates, so an unexpected failure mode is not silently reported as success.

Fix: narrow to the same three constructors gc.ml uses (Failure | Unix.Unix_error | Schema.Pctl_error), and add a comment naming why quiet down returns 0. Decide explicitly whether Eio.Cancel.Cancelled should propagate — it should, so that a cancelled switch is not reported as a clean down.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
lib/gc/gc.ml has the same shape at three more sites, and pctl-jbd's retry diff made one of them newly reachable. Same fix, so folding it in here rather than filing a duplicate.

  gc.ml:151-155  | Schema.Unknown -> (try remove_project ... with e -> eprintf "failed to sweep %s")
  gc.ml:158-159  with e -> eprintf "pctl gc: warn — sweep aborted: %s"
  gc.ml:175-178  with e -> eprintf "pctl gc: warn — failed to remove %s"

All three bind a bare `e`. These are better than pipeline.ml:296 in that they do print — but like it, they catch everything and continue.

What changed: Dbus.daemon_reload is now a cancellation point. Bus_retry.with_retry calls Eio.Time.Mono.sleep (dbus.ml:564), so Eio.Cancel.Cancelled can now leave daemon_reload where previously the call was a synchronous FFI round trip that could not yield. gc.ml:71-73's ignore_best_effort is correctly narrow and lets Cancelled through — straight into these three catch-alls, which swallow it and carry on iterating rows inside a cancelled context. Every subsequent Eio operation then re-raises immediately, so the sweep degrades into a loop of 'warn — failed to sweep' lines rather than unwinding.

So the fix for this ticket should cover both files and should explicitly re-raise Eio.Cancel.Cancelled (and Stdlib.Exit) rather than only narrowing to the Failure | Unix_error | Pctl_error triple — narrowing alone fixes gc but not the intent, since these three sites want to keep going on a per-row failure and must NOT keep going on a cancellation.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Duplicate of pctl-67s — same defect, same lines.

lib/cli/pipeline.ml:292-296:
    if quiet then
      try work (); 0
      with _ -> 0
    else run work

pctl-67s ('down ~quiet:true maps every failure to exit 0, so a propagated stop failure reports success', P2) and this ticket ('quiet pctl down swallows every exception with a bare with _ -> 0', P3) were filed from different reviews against the same code. 67s carries the sharper framing — it names the consequence (pctl-8sd made stop failures propagate, and this site erases them) — so 67s should be the survivor and this one closed as a duplicate.

Both are instances of the wider root: pctl has no designated place where a failure is allowed to be dropped. Other members: pctl-6ra, pctl-vv4, pctl-vz9, pctl-79a, pctl-3bt, pctl-93d, and clock.ml:28's 'try read_boot_id_exn () with _ -> ""'.

title: e2e: test_worktree's 'taking one down does not affect the other' is vacuous under one manager per scratch
description:
test_worktree ups two projects and asserts that B stays active after A goes down. That was a real assertion while both projects lived in one systemd --user: down A issued StopUnit against the same manager that held B's units, so a bug in slice scoping or manifest ownership could have taken B with it.

Since pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.1, A and B are in separate managers. The isolation is now structural — nothing A's down does can reach B's manager — so the assertion cannot fail for the reason it was written to catch. It still checks distinct ids and distinct hosts, which is why it was not deleted.

Options, none chosen: give the two projects one shared manager for this test (Harness.sibling_scratch already shares a manager, but shares the registry too, which this test needs distinct); or retarget the test at what is still testable across managers; or drop the down-isolation assertion and cover it at the integration layer against the fake systemctl, where two projects in one manager is free.

Found while implementing pctl-nested-manager-harness-nak.1.

title: docs: .claude/skills/pctl still documents the pre-SQLite registry and the pre-v2 @@PROJECT@@ placeholder
description:
The bundled pctl skill teaches two models the code no longer implements. Both mislead a reader who follows the skill instead of UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md.

1. Registry is described as ephemeral runtime-dir state.
   - .claude/skills/pctl/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:15 — "the registry entry was lost (typically because $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR was cleared on logout and the slice is no longer running anyway)".
   - TROUBLESHOOTING.md:17 — "If the slice is actually running but the registry entry is gone, systemctl --user stop pctl-<id>.slice is a last-resort fallback".
   - SKILL.md:35 — "up ... writes a fresh registry entry".
   The registry is now SQLite at $XDG_STATE_HOME/pctl/state.db (lib/state/db.ml:27-39). The row survives logout and reboot; a session reset (lib/state/session.ml) NULLs only host/started_at/spec_file/session_id, and only gc deletes the row (lib/gc/gc.ml). So the TROUBLESHOOTING diagnosis is now a wrong conclusion, not just stale wording: "row is gone" no longer follows from "you logged out".
   Term is "registry row", not "registry entry" — UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:42 lists "Registry entry" as an alias to avoid.

2. @@PROJECT@@ is documented as live behaviour.
   - SPEC.md:71 — "Any literal @@PROJECT@@ in a unit's filename or body ... is replaced with the project id at install time".
   No code path substitutes it: grep across lib bin nix test templates finds it only in three comments recording its removal (nix/lib/mkProject.nix:14, lib/render/render.ml:3, test/e2e/harness.ml:58). The replacement is the logical suffix (UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:46, expanded in lib/render/render.ml). SPEC.md:63 states the expansion correctly, so :71 also contradicts its own file.

Fix: rewrite TROUBLESHOOTING.md:15,17 against the SQLite/session-reset model, s/registry entry/registry row/ in SKILL.md:35, delete SPEC.md:71.

Found while reviewing pctl-oik. Out of that ticket's scope: it is confined to UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Deliberately NOT raised to P1. manveru: blocked until a release, and the project should not release until a lot of these bugs are tackled. That reasoning holds — pctl-468's D1 fix changes what the registry means, so rewriting the skill now means rewriting it twice.

But the skill misleads every agent session that loads it in the meantime, and this repo is agent-driven. Cheap middle ground that does not pre-commit any content: a staleness banner at the top of .claude/skills/pctl pointing at UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md as the authority and naming the two known-wrong areas (the pre-SQLite registry model, and @@PROJECT@@ — which UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md's 'Logical suffix' entry explicitly records as replaced). Two lines, removes the harm, survives whatever the rewrite ends up saying.

Suggest splitting: banner now (P2, minutes), full rewrite at release (this ticket, blocked).

title: docs: the rewrite plan's Unit_op_failed listing drifted at the moment e778a30 edited it
description:
docs/src/plans/20260419-ocaml-rewrite.md:267 restates the constructor the code owns:

    | Unit_op_failed       of { op : string; unit : string;
                                error_name : string option; reply : string }

lib/schema/schema.ml:104-109 names the field `unit_`, not `unit` — see the destructuring at schema.ml:483. e778a30 touched this exact line to add error_name and left the wrong field name standing, which is the drift a second copy produces by construction.

The listing is already known to be lossy: the paragraph below it says a `Probe_exec_failed` arm was dropped from it, and Journalctl_failed (schema.ml, rendered at :492) is absent too.

Fix: don't restate the constructor — refer to Schema.error by name. If a listing is wanted for the plan's narrative, at minimum correct unit → unit_.

Filed from the review of e778a30.
close_reason: unit → unit_ corrected, and the listing is now labelled as the plan's narrative sketch with Schema.error named as the contract, plus a note that it has already dropped Journalctl_failed. Kept as a listing rather than deleted: the surrounding plan text reads as a walkthrough.

title: systemctl/dbus: only daemon_reload survives a peer-gone window; every other bus call still fails
description:
Follow-on from pctl-jbd, which scoped the retry to Manager.Reload because Reload is idempotent.

The trigger is not specific to Reload. `switch-to-configuration` (every NixOS / home-manager activation) runs `systemctl --user daemon-reexec`; the user manager drops its bus connection and dbus-broker answers every in-flight call to it with org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply 'Remote peer disconnected' (driver_goodbye, dbus-broker src/bus/driver.c:2579). Until the manager re-registers, calls get ServiceUnknown / NameHasNoOwner instead.

Unprotected sites in lib/systemctl/dbus.ml, all reachable from a single `pctl up`:
  - call_unit_op :519 -> start_unit / stop_unit / restart_unit
  - manager_subscribe :542 (Subscribe)
  - get_unit_path :576 (GetUnit)
  - read_active_state :591 and the Job read at :656 (Properties.Get)

So a rebuild racing `pctl up` no longer fails at the reload, but can still fail at StartUnit. Measured on this host (systemd 260, dbus-broker 37) with a scratch harness that reloaded 40 times while reexec'ing 4 times: 4/4 reexecs produced the failure with the retry disabled, 0/4 with it enabled — the same window applies to any call made in it.

Deciding what to do needs one judgement per op, which is why it was not folded into pctl-jbd:
  - StartUnit/StopUnit/RestartUnit are issued with mode 'replace', so re-issuing is safe, but a retry after a disconnect cannot tell whether the first job was enqueued. Probably still correct to retry; wants a deliberate call.
  - The read-only ops (GetUnit, Properties.Get) are trivially safe to retry.
  - manager_subscribe is called during connect setup; a retry there interacts with install_match_rule_and_fiber.

Bus_retry.with_retry / is_peer_gone already exist and are unit-tested (test/unit/test_bus_retry.ml); this is about choosing the sites, not new machinery.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Two things to fold in when the sites listed here get touched.

1. The with_error/with_reply/check_rc scaffold is now repeated at seven sites in lib/systemctl/dbus.ml — :520, :540 (the new daemon_reload attempt), :568, :578, :592, :602, :617, :675 — i.e. essentially the exact list this ticket enumerates. call_unit_op already extracts one instance for start/stop/restart; the rest are inline copies. Wrapping each one in a retry individually would duplicate the retry too. Extract a single 'call ~op ~unit ~args' that returns the raw (rc, name, reply) triple, put the Bus_retry wrapper on that one function, and the per-op judgement this ticket asks for becomes a flag on the call rather than seven edits.

2. daemon_reload's retry uses Unix.gettimeofday for its deadline (dbus.ml:555), which is CLOCK_REALTIME. lib/probe/probe.ml:75-81 is the repo's existing deadline code and is monotonic throughout ('mono_now env = Eio.Time.Mono.now (env#mono_clock :> ...)'). Dbus.connect (dbus.ml:472) is 'let connect ~sw _env' — it already receives the env carrying mono_clock and discards it. Whichever sites get wrapped, thread env#mono_clock onto Dbus.t once rather than repeating the realtime call; that also drops the 'unix' library that pctl-jbd added to lib/systemctl/dune solely for gettimeofday (it is the only Unix use in the whole library).

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Observed in the wild, not theoretical. This bit during the pctl-jbd verification run on 2026-08-02.

scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 3 came back 2/3. Run 3 failed in test_depends_on_wait:

  ASSERT up --wait exit=5
  systemctl wait app failed: service app terminated in state 'inactive' (expected 'active')

User journal, same second:

  00:32:44 Created slice pctl slice for project_4c9e86b8.
  00:32:45 Starting pctl service migrate for project_4c9e86b8...
  00:32:45 Reexecution requested from client PID 3432855 ('switch-to-confi')...
  00:32:45 Reexecuting.
  00:32:46 Finished pctl service migrate ... / Started pctl service app ...

Attribution is unambiguous — reexecs in that window, by client comm:
  4x 'systemctl'        <- test_reload_survives_reexec's own kicker, runs 1 and 2
  1x 'switch-to-confi'  <- a NixOS/home-manager activation, run 3

So a rebuild landed mid-run again, and this time it did NOT hit Reload (now retried) but the probe's property reads, which are the sites this ticket is about.

Exact chain:
  1. app is queued-Inactive behind migrate (Requires=/After=).
  2. Probe classifies Inactive as `Maybe_terminal and asks unit_job_pending.
  3. unit_job_pending (dbus.ml) is get_unit_path + read_job_path, and BOTH are wrapped in 'with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> false'. The peer-gone reply is swallowed.
  4. Probe sees Inactive + no pending job -> terminal -> reports 'terminated in state inactive'.
  5. pctl exits 5 on a service that started fine one second later.

That is this ticket (the read ops are unprotected) compounded by pctl-q2j (the catch is wider than the NoSuchUnit tolerance its comment claims). Either fix alone would have turned this into a retry or a loud transport error instead of a wrong unit state. Worth doing them together.

Note the read ops are trivially safe to retry — they have no side effects — so of the sites listed in this ticket they are the cheapest to fix and, on this evidence, the highest value.

title: test_schema still fabricates op = "start", so the suite asserts two op vocabularies for one constructor
description:
pctl-fl6 removed the lowercase fabricated op labels from In_mem; pctl-jbi swept the fixtures that hand-authored wire values. test/unit/test_schema.ml:315 was missed:

    { op = "start"; unit_ = "x.service"; error_name = None; reply = "nope" },

with the expected render "systemctl start x.service failed: nope".

Meanwhile test/unit/test_gc.ml:308 was corrected in 761669c to op = "StopUnit". So the sandbox-safe suite now asserts two different op vocabularies for the same constructor: the D-Bus method names the real adapter produces, and the systemctl verb no adapter has produced since pctl-fl6.

Per CLAUDE.md's cassette rule, a fixture's job is to be a recording; "start" is now a value nothing in the tree can produce.

The bad RENDER is tracked separately (pctl-19n, open — render_error prints a D-Bus method as a systemctl verb). This ticket is only about the fixture's op value, which pctl-19n does not name.

Fix: op = "StartUnit" and the expected string to match, or converge both fixtures at once when pctl-19n lands.

Filed from round 2 of the review of 761669c/f7ff155.
close_reason: op = "StartUnit", expected string follows, with a comment saying a fabricated lowercase verb would hide pctl-19n's rendering rather than fix it. One op vocabulary across the suite now.
